Bellarmine replies, first, that he read הוא in one manuscript. But since he does not name the manuscript, who can doubt that he means the Interlinear Bible printed by Plantin in 1572? There the word is not הוא as Bellarmine cites it, but (through a typographical error, or a mistake by the corrector) הוּא, and indeed with the marginal note Kethib, as if the Keri were הוּא, so that

units.la: e Fieri, oteft ut & alius volens id fecerit. Ut utrit, Deo providente Typographicum hoc erratum admissum est ut ego quidem arbitror, voluit. Deus hoc ipso quasi remorari & cardare Lectorem ut ad sphalmatis Typographici consideratione, altera malitiosa corruptela accedeet. Exod. 3. 8. & hoc ipso capite v.12. Sed cum f sacrilegium hoc ii qui secundæ Editioni eorundem Bibliorum 1584. præfuerunt detestati sint & veram lectionem restituerint, cum denique g Arias Montanus protestetur, se insciò & improbante hoc factum, Bellarminus rectius fecisset, si Camarinam hanc nunquam movisset. Quid enim hoc aliud fuit, quam ut h Campianus adversus nostros loquitur, in cœleste chirographum temulento impetu involare? Secundò respondet, הוא remotis punctis posse legi הוא & hoc ipsum sæpe poni pro היא / Fateor, undecim locis exceptis, pronomen hoc fœmininum in V. Libris Mosis scribi semper per Vau הוא / sic enim Masora in voce היא / Per totam Legem scribitur הוא præter undecim quæ scribuntur היא / recensenturque in Sectione, Et sedit, Gen.38.27. Sed in istis x i. locis semper invenis hirik sub ה / (היא) invenies vel ante vel post illud pronomen nomina vel verba fœminina. Invenies denique singula ista loca fideliter enumerata. At hoc in loco nec hirik sub ה invenies, nec invenies sequi Fœminina, imo contra omnia Masculina: nec etiam hunc locum vel illic vel alibi usquam inter x i. illa reperies. Secundum Argumentum nostrum hoc est, posito per errorem vel hominum incuriam in aliquot exemplaria irrepsisse vel הוא vel היא / obstaret tamen isti lectioni, imo confiteret eam antecedens Masc. זרע semen, sequens verbum Masc. ישופך & denique eodem versu occurrens affixum Masc. in תשופנה / Objicit Bell. b loca aliquot ex quibus probare studet, novum aut insolens non esse ut cum nominibus Fœmininis jungantur pronomina aut verba Masculina. Ad quæ loca cum solidissime respondent i Cl. Junius & alii, nos nihil reponemus Bellar. præter illud, quod ipse in simili casu de personarum mutationibus ait, Si licet, inquit, personarum sine causa fingere mutationes, nihil certi unquam ex S. literis colligi poterit k. Claudemus verbis Epiphanii cedro dignissimis, ἵνα βλάσφ, inquit, ἐκαπυπλιξόντων τὸ ἁγίαν παρθένον τῶν π ἐπὶ ὲ τὸ δίον δοξαζόντων. Quæ verba docent pat detrimentum veræ religioni afferre eos, qui vilem habent beatam virginem, eosque qui ultra fas gloriam ejus adaugent. Hactenus mea Censura.
units.tr: it may be that someone else also, wishing to do so, did it. Whoever it was, by God's providence this typographical error was allowed to stand, as I for my part think he intended. By this very thing God, as it were, holds back and delays the reader, so that by attending to the typographical slip he might notice another, malicious corruption. See Exod. 3. 8., and this same chapter, v. 12. But since those who oversaw the second edition of the same Bible, in 1584, detested this sacrilege and restored the true reading, and since Arias Montanus finally protests that this was done without his knowledge and against his approval, Bellarmine would have done better never to have stirred up this Camarina. For what else was this, as Campian says of our people, than to rush with drunken violence upon the heavenly handwriting? Second, he replies that הוא, with the vowel points removed, can be read הוא, and that this very form is often used for היא [hiy]. I grant that, apart from eleven places, this feminine pronoun is always written in the five books of Moses with Vau, הוא; for so the Masora says of the word היא [hiy]. Throughout the Law it is written הוא, except for eleven places which are written היא, and these are listed in the section "Et sedit", Gen. 38.27. But in those eleven places you will always find a hireq under the ה of היא [hiy], and you will find before or after that pronoun feminine nouns or verbs. Finally, you will find those places faithfully enumerated. But in this place you will find neither a hireq under the ה, nor feminine words following; on the contrary, all are masculine. Nor will you find this place, either there or anywhere else, among those eleven. My second argument is this: even granting that through error or the carelessness of men either הוא or היא [hiy] crept into some copies, this reading would still be opposed, indeed refuted, by the antecedent masculine noun זרע [zera, "seed"], the following masculine verb ישופך [yeshupekha], and finally the masculine suffix on תשופנה [teshufenah] in the same verse. Bellarmine objects some passages, by which he tries to prove that it is neither new nor unusual for feminine nouns to be joined with masculine pronouns or verbs. To these passages the learned Junius and others reply most solidly. Against Bellarmine I will add only what he himself says in a similar case about changes of persons: "If it is permitted," he says, "to invent changes of persons without cause, nothing certain can ever be gathered from the Holy Scriptures." I will close with the words of Epiphanius, most worthy of cedar oil: "so that they blaspheme the holy virgin, some by diminishing her, others by glorifying her beyond what is fitting" [ἵνα βλασφημῶσιν τὴν ἁγίαν παρθένον, τῶν μὲν ἐλαττούντων, τῶν δὲ ὑπὲρ τὸ δέον δοξαζόντων]. These words teach that they do harm to true religion who hold the blessed virgin cheap, and also those who increase her glory beyond what is right. So far my Censure.

units.la: Hic demum serio in me destomachatur & paratragœdiat Mersennus, & cum antea folia tantum jactaret, nunc arboribus in me arietat, jamque faces & saxa volant.
units.tr: Here at last Mersennus rages seriously against me and plays the tragic actor. Before, he only brandished leaves; now he batters me with trees, and already torches and stones are flying.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Ubi caeteris impudentior Amama venenum eructat merasque vomit blasphemias.
units.tr: Where Amama, more shameless than the rest, belches out poison and pours forth nothing but blasphemies.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Ubi sunt blasphemiae? Nota paginam, lineam. Estne haec blasphemia, et tribuere victoriam, cui ex veritate litera debetur, ut cum vestro Gregorio Veneto loquar? Ergo blasphemus tibi quoque Bonaventura, qui in comm. super magistrum non erubuit asserere, cavendum esse ne dum matris excellentia ampliatur, filii gloria minuatur, ὑ καπνοπλίζω τὸν ἁγίαν παρθένον, ἀλλὰ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τὸ θεῖον δοξάζω, nec vilem habeo beatam Virginem, nec ultra fas eam colo. Γράφει γὰρ βλασφημίας, inquit Epiphanius, Par verae Religioni detrimentum afferunt & qui hoc & qui illud faciunt. Medio tutissimus ibo.
units.tr: Where are the blasphemies? Note the page and the line. Is this blasphemy: and to give the victory to the one to whom the victory is owed by the truth of the letter, to borrow the words of your Venetian Gregory? Then Bonaventure is a blasphemer too, who in his commentary on the Master did not blush to assert: we must take care that, while the excellence of the mother is magnified, the glory of the Son is not diminished [ὑ καπνοπλίζω τὸν ἁγίαν παρθένον, ἀλλὰ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τὸ θεῖον δοξάζω: I do not puff up the holy Virgin, but I do not glorify her beyond what is divine]. Yet I do not regard the blessed Virgin as cheap, nor do I worship her beyond what is right. For he writes blasphemies [Γράφει γὰρ βλασφημίας], says Epiphanius: those who do this and those who do that both do harm to true religion. I shall go the safest middle way.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Ejusdem criminis D. Bernardum super Missus est, insimulat, quia ex eo Scripturae loco amplam laudum virginis materiam arripit, eumque imperitiae arguit, cujus tamen unicam sententiam pluris fecero, quam omnia quae scribit hic Frisius, in omnes injurias, &c.
units.tr: He accuses me of the same crime with regard to Bernard, on the text "Missus est", because from that passage of Scripture I seize on a broad matter for praising the Virgin, and he charges him with ignorance, though I value his one opinion more highly than all that Frisius writes here, with all its insults, etc.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Non accuso Bernardum ejusdem criminis, vid. temeratae scripturae. Invenit enim in codice suo hanc lectionem Ipsa, & quia ad fontes per Ebraismi imperitiam recurrere ei non licuit, de veritate hujus lectionis non dubitavit. Multo minus eum hujus criminis arcesso, quod pessimam lectionem confirmaverit. Papa enim non fuit, ad quem, sicuti supra pag.107. ostensum est, proprie pertinet Scripturarum correctio.
units.tr: I do not accuse Bernard of the same crime; see my treatment of corrupted Scripture. For he found the reading Ipsa in his manuscript, and since through ignorance of Hebrew he could not go back to the sources, he did not doubt the truth of this reading. Still less do I charge him with the crime of having confirmed a very bad reading. For he was not the Pope, to whom, as was shown above on page 107, the correction of the Scriptures properly belongs.

units.la: Illud doleo, Bernardum in ea incidisse tempora, queis prae linguarum ignorantia doctissimis etiam Theologis & Ecclesiae luminibus ad fontes recurrere non licuit. Non ergo accuso eum, sed produco, ut ostendam quæ consectaria prava hac lectione etiam magnus ille vir elicuerit. Sed dicis te unam Bernardi sententiam pluris facere quàm omnia quæ ego scribo in omnes injurius. In omnes, inquis, homines, an Patres, an vestræ sectæ sequaces? Ne hoc postremum quidem mihi vere objectaveris. Ubi enim in Ariam Montanum, ubi in Pagninum, ubi in Cajetanum, ubi in Oleastrium, ubi in Espensæum, ubi denique in te injurius fui? Nota lineam, paginam, Ego certe, quòd ipse non ignoras, non nisi honorificentissime ipsorum memoriam usurpavi. Si in alios fortassis liberius aliquando dixi, an hoc vobis injuria est? Cæterum quod ad Bernardum attinet, eum ego, uti par est, veneror & suspicio. Agnosco me indignum esse, qui magno isti viro corrigias, quod ajunt, solvam. Non tamen ideo omnes ejus errores, in quos seculi infelicitate impegit, probabo. Et quod de unica ejus sententia affers, quæso te, Marsenne, responde quo loco illam habeas, quæ extat Epist. 174. Virgo Maria non egest falso honore, veris cumulata honoribus. Non est virginem honorare, sed ejus honori detrahere, &c. Festum conceptionis non fuit instituendum. Et istam, In cantic. serm. 14. Quisquis pro peccatis compunctus esurit & sitit justitiam, credat in te qui justificas impium, & SOLAM justificatus per fidem, pacem habebit ad Deum. Et denique istam, Epist. 190. Fides non est æstimatio sed certitudo. — Asignata est homini aliena justitia, qui caruit sua. Homo qui debuit, homo qui solvit. Satisfactio unius omnibus imputatur.
units.tr: I grieve that Bernard fell into those times when, because of ignorance of languages, even the most learned theologians and lights of the Church could not return to the sources. So I do not accuse him; I cite him, so that I may show what harmful consequences even that great man drew from this reading. But you say that you value one opinion of Bernard more highly than everything I write, with its insults against all. Against all, you say, men, or the Fathers, or the followers of your own sect? Do not even bring this last charge against me in truth. For where have I insulted Arias Montanus, where Pagninus, where Cajetan, where Oleaster, where Espencaeus, where finally you? Note the line and the page. I, at least, as you yourself know, have mentioned their memory only in the most honourable terms. If I have spoken more freely about others at some point, is that an injury to you? As for Bernard, I, as is fitting, venerate and respect him. I acknowledge that I am unworthy to untie, as they say, the thongs of that great man's sandals. Yet I shall not therefore defend all his errors, into which he fell through the unhappiness of his age. And as to the single opinion of his that you cite, I ask you, Marsenne, to answer where you find it: it stands in Epistle 174: The Virgin Mary does not need false honour, she who is heaped with true honours. It is not to honour the virgin but to detract from her honour, etc. The feast of the Conception ought not to have been instituted. And that in Sermon 14 on the Song of Songs: Whoever, pricked by sins, hungers and thirsts for righteousness, let him believe in you, who justify the ungodly, and being justified by faith ALONE, he will have peace with God. And finally that in Epistle 190: Faith is not an estimate but a certainty. — Another's righteousness is assigned to a man who lacked his own. The man who ought to pay, a man, paid. The satisfaction of one is imputed to all.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Verùm ut viros Catholicos & vulgatam Catholicè tueamur, rem totam diligentius excutiendam judico.
units.tr: But, that we may defend Catholic men and the Vulgate in a Catholic manner, I judge the whole matter must be examined more carefully.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Ergo Catholici tibi non sunt Cajetanus, Steuchus, Pagninus, Arias Mont. Felifius, Ribera, Perererius, Hartus, Canus, Andradius, Lindanus, quos in Censura mea à nostris partibus stare docui? Sed videamus tuas excussiones.
units.tr: So are Cajetan, Steuchus, Pagninus, Arias Montanus, Felifius, Ribera, Pererius, Hart, Canus, Andradius, Lindanus not Catholics for you, though in my Censure I showed that they stand on our side? But let us see your examinations.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: הוא ergo sine punctis vel hu vel hi legi potest, tàm masc. quàm fœm. genere. Sic enim versic.12. de muliere dicitur, הוא hi אותו ipsa dedit mihi de arbore. Et Gen. 17. vers.14. anima illa habe-tur הוא / item Gen.24.44. & Gen.38. quater ita legitur, vid. vers. 1. vers. 14. vers. 16. & 25.. Nec enim punctorum ratio habesso vpu circa annum 476. inventorum.
units.tr: Therefore הוא can be read without points either as hu or as hi, in the masculine or the feminine gender. For so in verse 12 it is said of a woman: הוא [hu] "hi" ... [she] gave me of the tree [ipsa dedit mihi de arbore]; and in Genesis 17 verse 14 that soul is held as הוא; likewise in Genesis 24:44, and in Genesis 38 it is read thus four times: see verse 1, verse 14, verse 16 and 25. For there was no reason for points before about the year 476, when they were invented.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Hæc est si quid video, tua ratiocinatio, הוא aliquando le-gitur per bi fœmininum, Ergo & hïc sic legi potest. 1. Negatur consequentia propositionis hic omissæ. Eam tu nunquam probatam dabis. 2. Negatur assumtio hæc, הוא sine punctis consideratum vel Hu, vel Hi legi posse. הוא enim cum vau scriptum, semper legitur Hu, ipse, sive punȡta hebeat adscripta sive non. Et contra הוא cum Iod scriptum, semper legitur הוא/ Quæ vero contra asters loca, nihil ad rem præsentem faciunt. Scribitur illic quidem in textu הוא / sed errore libratiorum & descriptoruin, quam critici Ebræorum Masoritæ in margine Bibliorum castigarunt, in eo repræsentantes veram & germanam lectionem היא / cujus punctum hirik voci mendosæ, præpostera religione in textu relictæ, subjecêre, eo ipso ostendentes hirik legendum esse, Hi. Et non ignoras ipse, & Ebræos & Christianorum doctissimos rò קְרֵי id est marginalem lectionem tanquam emendationem passim ferè sequi solere. Vnde verò hujus sphalmatis origo sit, in Dissertatione nostrâ ostendimus, & quivis videt, videl. ab affinitate, quæ est inter charaóteres Iod & Vau. Inspice Masoram & emendatiora Biblia & videbis non istis solummodò, quæ tu affers, sed & aliis locis voculam הוא in ipso contextu circulo insignitam, eique in margine respondere voculam היא cum litera ף id est קְרֵי legitur. Id quod propter Tirones noto. Correctionem autem illam esse certissimam, vocemque in ipso contextu, vel ob lectionis istius vetustatem, vel codicum multitudinem, relictam, in manifesto mendo cubare & antecedentia & consequa verba ostendunt. Ex. gr. vers.12. hujus ejusdem capitis, הָאִשָּׁה mulier quam dedisti ut effet mecum הוא נָתְנָה לִי illa dedit mihi, Ecce antecedens fœmininum אִשָּׁה mulier, & consequens ejusdem generis verbum נָתְנָה evidentur docent, errore descriptorum הוּא irrepsisse pro הִיא / quem proinde Maforitæ correxerunt, dum propriam fœminini pronominis vocalem, videl. Hirik ei addidêre, atque illud ipsum in margine exhibuêre. Sed quid exempla ista cum hoc, de quo jam agimus loco, habent commune? Hic antecedit nomen non fœm. sed mascul. generis, זֶרַע semen. Sequitur verbum Masc. יִשְׁמְפֶה & affixum relativum cjusdem generis in תִּשׁוּפֶּנּוּ / Vnde in hoc ipso loco de mendo nec Ebræorum nec Christianorum quispiam somniavit unquam, Codicesque Ebræi constanter legerunt atque etiamnum legunt הוּא / Sed dicis primò
units.tr: This, if I see anything, is your reasoning: הוא is sometimes read as feminine bi; therefore it may be read so here too. (1) The inference from the omitted premise is denied; you will never prove that premise. (2) This assumption is denied, namely that הוא, considered without points, can be read either Hu or Hi. For when הוא is written with vau it is always read Hu [ipse, he], whether or not it has points attached. And when הוא is written with yod it is always read as the feminine form. The passages you cite against this have nothing to do with the present matter. It is indeed written in the text הוא, but through the error of scribes and copyists, which the Hebrew critics, the Masoretes, corrected in the margin of the Bibles, there representing the true and genuine reading היא. They added the point hiriq to the faulty word, which was left in the text through misguided reverence, and by this very act showed that hiriq is to be read: Hi. You yourself are not unaware that both the Hebrews and the most learned Christians generally follow the קְרֵי, that is, the marginal reading, as a correction. Where the origin of this slip lies we have shown in our Dissertation, and anyone can see it: namely from the likeness between the letters yod and vav. Consult the Masora and the more accurate Bibles, and you will see that not only in the passages you cite but also in other places the little word הוא is marked with a circle in the very text, and in the margin the word היא with the letter ף, that is, the קְרֵי, is read in response. I note this for beginners. That this correction is most certain, and that the word left in the text itself, either because of the antiquity of that reading or the number of manuscripts, lies in manifest error, is shown by the preceding and following words. For example, in verse 12 of this same chapter: הָאִשָּׁה, the woman whom you gave, that she might be with me, הוא נָתְנָה לִי [she gave me]. Here the preceding feminine noun אִשָּׁה, woman, and the following verb of the same gender נָתְנָה clearly show that by the error of copyists הוּא crept in instead of הִיא; which the Masoretes accordingly corrected, adding to it the proper vowel of the feminine pronoun, hiriq, and displayed this very form in the margin. But what do those examples have in common with the place we are now discussing? Here the noun that precedes is not feminine but masculine: זֶרַע, seed. It is followed by the masculine verb יִשְׁמְפֶה and a relative suffix of the same gender in תִּשׁוּפֶּנּוּ. Hence in this very place neither Hebrew nor Christian has ever dreamed of an error, and the Hebrew manuscripts have constantly read, and still read, הוּא. But you say first...

units.la: Bellarm. isthic artic. 2. dicit, se VNVM legisse, in quo scriptum erat הוּא / Hoc longè aliud est & diversum ab eo quod tu ei affingis, illum vid. asserere se in vetustissimis EXEMPLARIBUS legisse Hi. Certè si me ita exorbitantem deprehendisses, quos fluctus excitasses? Sed veniam tibi do inconsideratæ istius assertionis, & rogo ut facias paria, si mihi idem fortassis contigerit. Homo sum, humani nihil à me alienum puto. Volens sciensque non dicam mendacium, nec te id ex proposito commisisse spero. Sed quàm vellem, Bellarm. nominasse illud unum exemplar! An fuit ἀκίφαλον, ut & nomen loci & Typographi & editionis annus exprimi non potuerint? An scire nefas erat, cujus formæ fuerit illud exemplar? an in folio, an quarto, an verò in octavo, ut loquuntur, complicatum fuerit? Aut fuit alicujus authoritatis, vetustatis & fidei, aut nullius. Si alicujus, cur non nominatur? Si nullius, cur memorätur? Sed religiosus magis fuit Cardinalis, quàm ut mentitus fuerit. Ita equidem de ipso sentio, Quid ergo? Jam notavi in censura meâ, eum proculdubio intellexisse Editionem Antverp. interlinearem, quæ Bibliis Regiis addita est, anni 1572. ubi Guido Fabricius, verba Lucæ Brugensis, Principii Mirandulani authoritate nixus excudi curavit הוה / licet errore Typographico positum sit הורה / Sed callidè fecit Bellarminus, quod Editionem non nominaverit. Eadem calliditate Gretzerus editionem dissimulavit. Cum enim nostri certatim peterent, nominari Editionem, tamen Gretzerus, qui super ea re Bellarminum per Epistolam consulere potuisset, pisce hic mutior est. Non ignorabant enim multos Catholicos hanc audaciam fuisse detestatos, eosque qui Antverpiensi Editioni Bibliorum Interlin. anno 1584. præfuere, veram lectionem הוא restituisse, ipsumque adeò * Ariam Mont. adversus hoc facinus, sine Romanæ Ecclesiæ authoritate suâque approbatione patratum, in prolegomenis secundæ Bibliorum Interlin. editioni præmissis diserte fuisse protestatum. Rectius itaque fecisset Bellarm. si hanc Camarinam non commovisset. Addo, si unicum illud exemplar veram & germanam hujus voculæ lectionem, vocali hirik subjecta, expressit, necessariò sequi omnia, quotquot sunt & fuerunt exemplaria, utpote vocem illam cum litera vau in medio exhibentia, esse corrupta. Illud enim ipsum exemplar, (quod notari velim à lectore meo) licet hirik sub ה exhibuerit, הוא / tamen cum vau in medio ipso Bellar. teste, pronomen illud expressit. Si genuina lectio est Hi, certè à Mose scriptum oportuit הוא / Unde necessariò inferetur universalis & generalis corruptio loci ad fidem pertinentis. id quod iis, quæ Bellarm. lib.2. cap.2. disseruit, è diametro repugnat. Sed inquis, pag.1366.
units.tr: Bellarmine, in the second article there, says that he read ONE copy in which it was written הוּא [hu']. This is quite different from what you attribute to him, namely that he asserts he read in very ancient COPIES the word Hi. Indeed, if you had caught me wandering off like that, what a storm you would have raised! But I forgive you that thoughtless assertion, and I ask that you do the same for me, should the same thing happen to me. I am a man, and I consider nothing human foreign to me. I would not, knowingly and willingly, tell a lie, and I hope you did not commit this error on purpose. But how I wish Bellarmine had named that one copy! Or was it headless [ἀκέφαλον], so that neither the place, the printer, nor the year of the edition could be stated? Or was it forbidden to know what format that copy was, whether folded in folio, quarto, or, as they say, octavo? Either it had some authority, antiquity and reliability, or none. If it had some, why is it not named? If none, why is it mentioned? But the Cardinal was too scrupulous to have lied. That is certainly my view of him. What then? I have already noted in my criticism that he doubtless had in mind the Antwerp interlinear edition, added to the Royal Bible, of 1572, where Guido Fabricius, on the words of Luke of Bruges, relying on the authority of Mirandula's Principle, had it printed הוה [hwh], although through a printer's error it is set down as הורה [hwrh]. But Bellarmine acted craftily in not naming the edition. Gretser concealed the edition with the same craftiness. For when our men were eagerly demanding that the edition be named, Gretser, who could have consulted Bellarmine about the matter by letter, is here as silent as a fish. For they knew that many Catholics had detested this audacity, and that those who oversaw the Antwerp edition of the interlinear Bible in 1584 had restored the true reading הוא [hu'], and that Arias Montanus himself had explicitly protested against this crime, committed without the authority of the Roman Church and without its approval, in the prolegomena prefixed to the second edition of the interlinear Bible. Bellarmine would therefore have done better not to stir up this hornets' nest. I add this: if that single copy expressed the true and genuine reading of this little word, with the vowel hireq placed beneath it, it necessarily follows that all the copies that exist or have existed, since they show that word with a vav in the middle, are corrupt. For that very copy (which I would have my reader note), although it showed hireq under the ה [he], nevertheless, according to Bellarmine's own testimony, expressed that pronoun with a vav in the middle. If Hi is the genuine reading, then it must surely have been written by Moses as הוּא [hu']. Hence there would follow a universal and general corruption of a passage that bears on the faith, which directly contradicts what Bellarmine argued in book 2, chapter 2. But you say, on page 1366,

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Nec enim punctorum ratio habenda est. Et pag.1368. Unde facilè convelluntur Amaunæ objectiones blasphemæ, qui veritate coactus fatetur, pronomen hoc fæm. הִיא Hi, semper in Pentateucho per ' scribi, הוא / locis 11. exceptis, nec obstat, quod tunc hirik_sub ה scribatur, cùm puncta recentiora esse superius dixerimus.
units.tr: Nor indeed is the reason of the points to be taken into account. And at p. 1368: hence Amama's blasphemous objections are easily overturned. He, forced by the truth, admits that the feminine pronoun הִיא (Hi) is always written in the Pentateuch with yod, and הוא (hu, with vav) in eleven places excepted. Nor does it stand in the way that the hireq is then written under ה, since we have said above that the points are more recent.

units.la: Nulla necessitas est, ut disputationem illam de punctorum authoritate ingrediar. Ego enim hic non puncta sed literas urgeo הוא cum vau in omnibus codicibus scribi, inter Bell. & nos convenit, neque tu id negabis. Hanc vos literam sollicitatis. Si enim pronomen fœm. est, oportet ut cum Jod in medio à Mose scriptum fuerit. Id quod reponendum vobis fuerat. Nec obstat, inquis, quod tunc quando vid. pronomen fœm. Hi per vau scribitur) hirik sub ה scribatur, cum puncta recentiora sint, &c. Quid audio? Vis ergo punctum sub ה tolli & in vau collocari? At tunc esset pronomen extra controversiam Masc. generis, & nullo modo Hi legi posset. Cur ergo non potius literam vau palàm sollicitatis? Cur non illam potius in Jod transmutatis & punctum sub ה ponitis? Sed miror te meas objectiones vocare blasphemas. Bona verba quæso, & dic sedato animo, utrùm in Deum ipsum O.M. an verò B. Virginem Θεοτόκον blasphemæ sint. Non in Deum, dices, opinor. Nec in B. Virginem. Probo. Nihil enim interest, te ipso judice, animadvers. in l v. Probl. Veneti. non est enim contra vulgatam Editionem, verba Bellarm. si convincatur debere legi Ipse vel Ipsum. Si ea lectio non repugnat vulgatæ Editioni, nec Catholicæ fidei adversabitur. Habeo etiam astipulantem Corn. à Lapide, qui docet nullam ex his * tribus lectionibus esse rejiciendam, sed omnes esse veras; ut nihil jam de iis dicam, quos supra produxi, lectionem Ipse alteri audacter præferentes. Miror & illud, quod dicas me veritate coactum confiteri, &c. Cum ea confessio causam nostram non solum non lædat, sed etiam vehementer firmet. Quicquid enim agas, quòcunque te vertas, nihil aliud colliges, quam hoc, הוא aliquando per הוא legi. Ergo & hic. Cur non & mihi eodem jure sic licebit ratiocinari, הוא passim legitur Hu ut scribitur. Ergo & hic. Dixi jam, ibi antecedentia & consequentia manifestè indicare librariorum sphalma, atque istis in locis Masoritas veram lectionem in margine omnino, atque adeo in ipso quoque textu ex parte restituisse. Hic verò nihil tale occurrere. Quid hic opponis? Audio tamen haereticos, qui possint objicere, hic verbum esse masc. יְשׁוּפָה / At saepe videas in Scriptura cum verbis masculinis jungi pronomina foeminina, ut Ruth. 1. 8. cum עֲשֵׂיתֶם de duabus mulieribus dicitur. Esth. 1. 20. נָשִׁים יִהְנוּ Et Koheleth. 12. 4. יְשֵׁהוּ בָּנוֹת Et p. 1367. Gen. 2. 23. יִקְרָא אִשָּׁה pro תִּקְרָא /
units.tr: There is no need for me to enter into that dispute about the authority of the points. I am not pressing the points here but the letters: that הוא is written with vav in all manuscripts. Bellarmine and we agree on this, and you will not deny it. It is this letter you are tampering with. For if the pronoun is feminine, Moses ought to have written it with a yod in the middle. That is what you should have answered. "Nor does it stand in the way," you say, "that when the feminine pronoun Hi is written with vav, the hireq is put under ה, since the points are more recent." What do I hear? Do you want the point under ה removed and placed under the vav? But then the pronoun would be beyond dispute masculine, and in no way could it be read Hi. Why, then, do you not openly tamper with the letter vav instead? Why not change it into a yod and put the point under ה? But I am surprised that you call my objections blasphemous. Please choose your words well, and tell me calmly whether they are blasphemous against God Almighty or against the Blessed Virgin, Theotokos. Not against God, I suppose you will say. Nor against the Blessed Virgin. I prove it. For, by your own judgment, it makes no difference (see your notes on the fifth book of the Venetian Problems) whether Bellarmine's words, "it is not contrary to the Vulgate edition," are applied to the reading Ipse or Ipsum, if it is shown that one of these ought to be read. If that reading does not conflict with the Vulgate edition, it will not be opposed to the Catholic faith. I also have a supporter in Cornelius a Lapide, who teaches that none of these three readings is to be rejected but all are true. I say nothing now of those I cited above, who boldly prefer the reading Ipse to the others. I also wonder at your claim that I am "forced by the truth to confess," and so on. That confession not only does no harm to our cause but strongly confirms it. For whatever you do and wherever you turn, you can draw only this conclusion: הוא is sometimes read as הוא; therefore here too. Why may I not reason by the same right: הוא is everywhere read hu as it is written; therefore here too? I have already said that in those places the preceding and following words clearly show a scribal slip, and that there the Masorites restored the true reading in the margin altogether, and so in part in the text itself. Here, however, nothing of the kind occurs. What do you object here? "I hear, however, heretics who might object that here the verb is masculine," יְשׁוּפָה [yeshuphah]. "But you often see in Scripture feminine pronouns joined with masculine verbs, as in Ruth 1:8, where, of two women, עֲשֵׂיתֶם [asitem] is said; Esth. 1:20, נָשִׁים יִהְנוּ [yihnu nashim]; and Eccles. 12:4, בָּנוֹת יִשְׁחוּ [yishchu banot]." And p. 1367, Gen. 2:23, יִקְרָא אִשָּׁה [yiqra ishah] for תִּקְרָא.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Quàm vellem te locum vel unicum protulisse, ubi pronomen foem. sine errore scriptum [הִיא] cum verbo Masc. jungitur. Ruth. 1. 8. est manifesta enallage. Alloquitur enim Noëmi duas mulieres. Necessario ergo ibi עֲשֵׂיתֶם positum est pro עֲשִׂיתָן vel per simplicem Enallagen, vel honoris causa, ut διὰ χρῶμα τῷ, verba Cl. Junii, virile mulierum factum enuncietur. Latet autem illud χρῶμα non tàm in verbo, quàm in pronomine, Faciat Deus עִמָּכֶם cum vobis masc. generis, misericordiam, quemadmodum עֲשִׂיתֶם fecistis vos m. g. Est enim haec persona composita ex themate & pronomine corrupto, אַתֶּם / Hic vero χρῶμα illud juxta te non in pronomine, sed in verbo latebit. Sed non urgebo illud. Hoc satis erit ostendendae dissimilitudini, illic ad foeminas extra dubium sermonem dirigi: Hic verò de foemina agi, ne per somnium quidem in mentem venisset ulli veterum, eorumve, qui ante controversias has motas vixere, nisi codicibus Latinis depravatis usi fuissent. Illic ad foeminas dirigitur oratio in versionibus omnibus. Hic & Ebraei & Graeci & Chaldaei codices constanter masculinum legunt, locumque vel de mare, vel genere humano sub maris specie concepto, intellexêre. Et ut daretur tibi, hoc exemplum esse per omnia simile, quid aliud ex eo lucraberis, quàm hanc conclusionem, Ergo verbum Masc. non obstat, quominus הוא hic possit esse foemininum, & reddi per Ipsa. At probare prius oportuerat, variam hujus voculae lectionem, & deinde firmioribus praesidiis munienda erat ea, quae Chaldaeis & Graecis codicibus adversatur & nihilominus Ecclesiis sub poenâ anathematis recipienda obtruditur, versio; conclusionem denique non imbecillum illud potest, sed robustius debet ingredi debuerat.
units.tr: I wish you had cited even one place where the feminine pronoun [הִיא] is written without error and joined with a masculine verb. Ruth 1:8 is a plain enallage. For Naomi is addressing two women. Therefore עֲשֵׂיתֶם [asitem] must stand there for עֲשִׂיתָן [asitan], either by a simple enallage or out of respect, "so that by a figure of gender (διὰ χρῶμα τῷ [dia chroma to]), in the words of the learned Junius, a masculine act is expressed of women." That figure of speech lies not so much in the verb as in the pronoun: "May God do" עִמָּכֶם [immakhem], "with you" (masculine), "mercy, as you [masculine] have done" עֲשִׂיתֶם [asitem]. For this form is composed of the stem and a corrupted pronoun, אַתֶּם [attem]. By your account, however, that figure would lie not in the pronoun but in the verb. I will not press the point. It will be enough to show the difference: there the speech is clearly directed to women, whereas here it is about a woman, and no one of the ancients, or of those who lived before these controversies were stirred up, would have dreamed of it, unless they had used corrupted Latin copies. There, in all the versions, the address is to women. Here the Hebrew, Greek and Chaldee manuscripts consistently read the masculine, and interpreted the passage either of a man, or of the human race conceived under the form of a man. And suppose this example were in every respect similar. What else would you gain from it than this conclusion: that a masculine verb does not prevent this הוא from being feminine and rendered "she"? But you ought first to have proved that the reading of this little word varies, and then the version which conflicts with the Chaldee and Greek manuscripts, yet is nonetheless thrust upon the Churches under penalty of anathema, ought to have been defended by stronger supports. Finally, you ought to have brought your conclusion in not with the weak word "can," but with the stronger "must."

units.la: Quod ad locum Esth. 1. 20. & Eccles. 12. 4. attinet, eadem utriusque est ratio. Illic נָשִׁים / hic בְּנוֹת extra dubium foem. generis sunt. Ut dubium esse non posset, quin illic יְתֵנִי pro תְּתַנֶּנָה / hic vero יִשְׁחוּ pro תִּשְׁחִיָּה positum sit. Sed & in promptu est ratio, cur ea Enallage & hic & alibi admissa sit, vid. Homonymia istarum vocum, quae & secundae & tertiae personae sunt. Ejus vitandae causa non solum haec persona, vid. tertia plur. masc. sed secunda non semel pro foeminina usurpatur E. g. Jer. 49. 11. תִּבְטְחוּ אַלְמְנוֹתֶיךָ sperabunt vidua tua. Jezech. 37. 7. תִּקְרְבוּ עַצְמוֹת appropinquabunt ossa. At quae causa assignabitur, cur hic non adhibitum fuerit foem. תִּשּׁוּפֶךָ Dices & illud factum Ἀλγαχεῖσως ἵνεκα, cum & illa persona תָּשׁוּף ambigua sit, jam secundae masc. jam tertiae foem. Sed ambiguitatem istam sustulisset additum pronomen tertiae personae הוא / deinde & affixum secundae personae, quod verbo ejusdem personae non solet addi. Quod vero ad locum Gen. 2. 23. attinet לְאִשָּׁה יִקָּרֵא אִשָּׁה & tu & a quo mutuatus es, Corn. a Lapide hic longe a scopo aberratis. Versio vulg. habet, hac vocabitur virago, ut & Graeca αυτη ἀληθῶς οὖσα γυνή Si illud לְאִשָּׁה ad sensum bene reddi-tum est per hac, ut existimo, vides vel manifestam Ellipsin vocis alterius, quae si masc. sit, apparebit dissimilitudo ingens. Sic enim integra esset locutio, לְאִשָּׁה יִקָּרֵא שֵׁם אִשָּׁה huic vocabitur nomen VIRA. Verba enim nuncupandi in forma passiva praeter nominativum jungi solent cum dativo personae: vel vox nomen inclusa erit ipsi verbo, ut sic reddere possis, Huic nomen erit Vira, quomodo Pagninus in Thesauro suo passivum הקרא solet interpretari, atque hunc ipsum locum interpretatur. Sed demus hæc exempla appositè esse adducta, quid inde lucraberis mi Marsenne? Si vel masculinum Ipse, vel neutrum Ipsum à Pontificibus in textu fuisset relictum, & fœminino Ipsa in margine locus fuisset assignatus; si insuper Ebræum pronomen variè in cod. Ebraïs fuisset lectum; persuadere forsan imperitiori posses, non adeò absurdum & insolens esse, fœmininum Ipsa legi, nec obstare verbum Masc. At cum omnes Ebr. codices juxta cum Chald. & Græcis constanter legant הוא (exemplar enim Antverpiense quod de industriâ corruptum est, ut stabiliretur vulgatum Ipsa, ipsi allegare erubescitis) iterum dico, firmioribus præsidiis niti oportuisse lectionem Ipsa, antiquam papali authoritate in locum Masculini Ipse, quod & Chald. & & Græcis codicibus respondere, omnes, Ebraïcis verò pleri- que agnoscitis, & orthodoxum sensum habere confitemini, substitueretur.
units.tr: As for the passage Esth. 1:20 and Eccles. 12:4, the reasoning is the same for both. There נָשִׁים [nashim] and here בְּנוֹת [benot] are beyond doubt feminine. Hence there can be no doubt that יְתֵנִי [yetheni] stands for תְּתַנֶּנָה [tethannenah], and here יִשְׁחוּ [yishchu] for תִּשְׁחִיָּה [tishchiyah]. But the reason why this enallage was admitted both here and elsewhere is also ready to hand: namely, the homonymy of these forms, which are both second and third person. To avoid this, not only this form, the third person plural masculine, but also the second person is used more than once for the feminine. For example, Jer. 49:11, תִּבְטְחוּ אַלְמְנוֹתֶיךָ [tivtechu almenotekha], "your widows will trust." Ezek. 37:7, תִּקְרְבוּ עַצְמוֹת [tiqrevu atzmot], "the bones will draw near." But what reason will be given why the feminine תִּשּׁוּפֶךָ [tishuphekha] was not used here? You will say that this too happened for some reason (Ἀλγαχεῖσως ἵνεκα [...]), since this form תָּשׁוּף [tashuph] is also ambiguous, being now second masculine, now third feminine. But that ambiguity would have been removed by the added pronoun of the third person, הוא [hu], and then by the suffix of the second person, which is not usually added to a verb of the same person. As for Gen. 2:23, לְאִשָּׁה יִקָּרֵא אִשָּׁה [le-ishah yiqqare ishah], "she shall be called woman," Cornelius a Lapide has strayed far from the mark. The Vulgate reads, "this shall be called virago," and so does the Greek, "αὕτη ἀληθῶς οὖσα γυνή" [hautē alēthōs ousa gynē]. If לְאִשָּׁה has been rendered well enough in the sense "this," as I think, you see either a manifest ellipsis of another word, which, if it were masculine, would reveal a great difference. For the phrase would then be complete: לְאִשָּׁה יִקָּרֵא שֵׁם אִשָּׁה [le-ishah yiqqare shem ishah], "to this one the name Vira shall be given." Verbs of naming in the passive form are usually joined, besides the nominative, with the dative of the person; or the word "name" is included in the verb itself, so that you could render it, "to her the name shall be Vira," as Pagninus, in his Thesaurus, usually interprets the passive הקרא and interprets this very passage. But grant that these examples are rightly cited: what will you gain from them, my dear Marsenne? If the Papists had left the masculine "Ipse" or the neuter "Ipsum" in the text, and had assigned the feminine "Ipsa" to the margin; and if, further, the Hebrew pronoun had been read in various ways in the Hebrew manuscripts, you might perhaps persuade a less learned reader that reading the feminine "Ipsa" is not so absurd or unusual, and that a masculine verb does not stand in the way. But since all the Hebrew manuscripts consistently read הוא, together with the Chaldee and Greek ones (for you blush to cite the Antwerp exemplar, which was corrupted on purpose to establish the familiar "Ipsa"), I say again: you ought to have relied on stronger supports, to substitute the reading "Ipsa," an old reading, for the masculine "Ipse" by papal authority. Yet all of you admit that the masculine corresponds to the Chaldee and Greek manuscripts, and that most Hebrew manuscripts agree with it, and you confess that it has an orthodox sense.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Iterum ostendimus, nos optimo consilio potius Ipsam, quam Ipsum, vel Ipse retinuisse. Primum enim cum הוא per Iscribimus, aut Masculinum, magna denotatur Emphasis, ut ipsissimam magis, quam ipsam significet, ut etiam verf. 12. & 20. &c.
units.tr: Again I show that we kept the reading Ipsam, not Ipsum or Ipse, for a very good reason. For first, when הוא is written with Iod, or as the masculine, a strong emphasis is intended, so that it means the very same one more than the simple ipsam; see also verses 12 and 20, etc.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Magnum hic pandis mysterium, הוא Emphaseos causa pro הוא poni, quod ego librariorum errori semper adscribendum putavi. Sed quâ authoritate הוא per Hirik & Vau scribitis? An ipsius Moßis, an Masoritarum, an denique Pontificis? non Moßis, opinor. Si enim ille, quæ tua quoque est sententia, puncta non adscripsit, & tamen pronomen fœmininum intendit, oportet eum illud ipsum per Jod in medio expressisse. Non Masoritarum; illorum enim authoritatem vilipendis, & quod iterum hic inculcandum, salsissimum est eos hoc loco הוא scripsisse. Ad omnes punctatos codices ad ipsam Masoram provoco in quâ omnia loca, queis הוא pro הוא irrepsit, indicarunt, de hoc altum silentes. Sed tu quoque paulo post, hanc punctationem הוא in Rabbinos (Masoritas te intelligere opinor) transcribis, quando ais, Sed & gratis concedere possumus, puncta à Rabbinis recte collocata esse. Non denique Pontificis, id quod Arias Montanus evidenter probat istis verbis, quæ supra p. 32. repræsentavimus. Cætera ergo, quæ hic rursus producis loca, nihil cum habent commune, & Emphasis ista tuâ tantum conjecturâ nititur.
units.tr: Here you reveal a great mystery: that הוא is put for הוא for the sake of emphasis. I have always thought this should be put down to the error of copyists. But on what authority do you write הוא with Hirik and Vau? Is it the authority of Moses, of the Masorites, or finally of the Pontiff? Not Moses, I think. For if he, as you also hold, did not add the vowel points, yet intended a feminine pronoun, he must have expressed it by a Jod in the middle. Nor is it the Masorites: you despise their authority, and (what must be pressed again here) it is most absurd that they wrote הוא in this place. I appeal to all the pointed codices and to the Masora itself, in which they noted all the places where הוא has crept in for הוא, and yet are silent about this one. But you too, shortly afterwards, attribute this pointing of הוא to the rabbis (I think you mean the Masorites) when you say: But we may also freely grant that the points were rightly placed by the rabbis. Finally, it is not the Pontiff's either, as Arias Montanus clearly proves by the words I set out above on page 32. So the other passages you bring forward here have nothing in common with this, and that emphasis of yours rests on conjecture alone.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Sed & gratis concedere possumus, puncta à Rabbinis recte collocata esse. Etenim mulier est nomen collectivum totam Ecclesiam designans ac proac proinde Virginem, partem nobilissimam Ecclesia. At Maforeta nomina collectiva communis generis esse volunt, ut docet Pagn. lib. 2. Gramm. cap. 2. &c.
units.tr: But we may also freely grant that the points were rightly placed by the rabbis. For mulier is a collective noun designating the whole Church, and therefore the Virgin, the noblest part of the Church. But the Masorites want collective nouns to be of common gender, as Pagninus teaches in book 2 of his Grammar, chapter 2, etc.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Non inspexisti locum Pagnini, cum hæc scriberes. Toto isto capite nulla Maforitarum fit mentio. Illud solummodò in fine notat Pagninus, esse quædam nomina quæ utroque genere usurpentur, id quod nullus negaverit. At inter ea vocem אשה non reperies. Quomodo verò אשה hic accipiendum sit, non disputo. Quæstio inter me & te de lectione voculæ הוא est. Hoc agamus.
units.tr: You had not looked at Pagninus's passage when you wrote this. In that whole chapter there is no mention of the Masorites at all. Pagninus only notes at the end that there are certain nouns which are used in either gender, a point no one would deny. But you will not find the word אשה among them. How it is to be taken here I do not dispute. The question between you and me concerns the reading of the little word הוא. Let us deal with that.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Hinc concludendum est, non semper Maforethis credendum esse, neque scripturam sacram juxta eorum dogma atque puncta emendandum: siquidem ejus sensum aut intellectum depravârunt, ubi Christiana religionis mysterium includi deprehendebant, vel etiam se credebant argui.
units.tr: Hence it must be concluded that the Masorites are not always to be believed, nor is Holy Scripture to be emended according to their doctrine and points, since they corrupted its sense or meaning wherever they found a mystery of the Christian religion enclosed, or even believed themselves to be refuted.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Ego, μαχὺε τς ἀν, non video quomodo hanc conclusionem ex superioribus elicias. Dixisti enim ante, concedi posse, Rabbinos hic punctum in ו bene collocasse, dixisti sensum eodem recidere, sive ipse, sive ipsum, sive ipsa legatur. Cur ergo hic eorum fidem sublestam reddere satagis? Cur hic iis non credam? Præsertim cum ante illos & Chaldæus Paraphrastes & LXX. ita legerint ipse contextus evidenter eò ducat. Enumeras postea aliquot loca in quibus putas Maforitas malâ fide fuisse versatos, quæ obiter lustrabimus.
units.tr: For my part, I do not see how you draw this conclusion from what went before. For you said earlier that it may be conceded that the rabbis rightly placed the point on the ו here, and you said the sense comes to the same whether ipse, ipsum or ipsa is read. Why, then, are you now at pains to make their good faith suspect? Why should I not believe them here? Especially since both the Chaldee paraphrast and the Seventy read it this way before them, and the context itself clearly leads to this. You next list some passages in which you think the Masorites acted in bad faith; we shall run through them briefly.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Jud. 19. 3. ubi legimus להשיבו Iahaschiba Maforeta mutari voluerunt & affixum masc. g. in ה fœm. quandoquidem de muliere sermo est, quod tamen falsum est, cum ibi Synagoga per fœminam à Vi-
units.tr: Judges 19:3, where we read להשיבו (lahaschiba), the Masorites wished it changed, and the masculine suffix in the feminine ה, since the talk is of a woman; which is nevertheless false, since there the Synagogue is represented by the woman, and God by the Levite, the husband who is departing.

units.la: roin recedentem, & per Levitam Deus repræsentetur.
AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: 1. Mirabor si להשיבו possis legere Lahaschiba. 2. Masoretæ non sine judicio aut codicum authoritate tradiderunt pro לְהָשִׁיבוֹ legendum esse לְהָשִׁיבָה / quam vocem proinde in margine posuerunt, atque ejus vocalem ultimam (ˇ) literæ ב subjecêre, ut juxta eam legeretur. 3. Velim hîc doceri quodnam religionis Christianæ mysterium hic inclusum sit, vel quâ ratione hic arguantur, ut propterea cœleste hoc Dei chirographum temulento impetu violare voluerint. 4. Quomodo negare audes hic de muliere sermonem esse? Annon pellex est mulier? Annon eam voluit reducere? Inspice textum, mi Marsenne. 5. Quomodo probabis per mulierem hîc Synagogam denotari? Quo fundamento? Quibus principiis? Apage istum allegorizandi pruritum. Somnia hæc sunt otiosorum hominum, circa quæ præstantia ingenia, quibus tuum quoque annumero libens, occupari indignum est. 6. Concedatur tibi hæc allegoria. Per mulierem repræsentetur Synagoga. Hæc allegorica interpretatio haudquaquam tollere debet propriam, quæ primaria & genuina est. Et nihilominus manet fœm. genus, quod non solum tribuitur fœminis, sed & rebus sub fœminæ specie conceptis. Si ergo Synagoga repræsentabitur per fœminam, non minùs æquum erit, ut affixum fœm. sit in לְהָשִׁיבָה sicuti in præcedentibus, לְבָהּ & אַחֲרִיהָ /
units.tr: 1. I shall be surprised if you can read להשיבו as Lahaschiba. 2. The Masorites did not hand down, without judgment or the authority of the manuscripts, that לְהָשִׁיבָה [lahashibah] is to be read instead of לְהָשִׁיבוֹ [lahashibo]. Accordingly they placed this form in the margin and set the final vowel point under the letter ב, so that it would be read in that way. 3. I should like to be taught what mystery of the Christian religion is enclosed here, or on what ground they are refuted here, so that they would therefore wish to violate this heavenly charter of God with drunken fury. 4. How do you dare to deny that there is talk of a woman here? Is she not a concubine? Did he not want to bring her back? Look at the text, my dear Marsenne. 5. How will you prove that a woman here denotes the Synagogue? On what foundation? On what principles? Away with that itch of allegorising! These are the dreams of idle men, with which outstanding minds, among whom I gladly count yours, should not be occupied. 6. Let this allegory be granted you: that the Synagogue is represented by the woman. This allegorical interpretation ought by no means to remove the proper sense, which is primary and genuine. And nevertheless the feminine gender remains, which is attributed not only to women but also to things conceived under the form of a woman. If, then, the Synagogue is represented by a woman, it will be no less fitting that the feminine suffix stand in לְהָשִׁיבָה [lahashibah], just as in the preceding words, לְבָהּ [lebah] and אַחֲרִיהָ [aharehah].

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Secundus locus, Prov.31.16. in fine נטע nataha, dicunt ה ponendum esse, cum ibi de muliere sermo sit. At de Ecclesia loquitur sapiens sub mulieris similitudine.
units.tr: The second place: Prov. 31.16, at the end of נטע (nataha). They say that a ה must be placed there, since the passage is about a woman. But the wise man speaks of the Church under the likeness of a woman.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Si male additam putas literam ה quomodo ergo potes legere nataha? Sermo ibi est de muliere strenua, cujus studia & laudes ibi recenset Regum sapientissimus. Omnia verba quæ de ea enunenunciantur sunt fœm. generis, tam præterita quàm futura, טַעֲמָה / חִגְרָה / זְמְמָה / חָעַשׁ / תָּקוּם / תִּתֵּן / הָיְתָה / הִרְשָׁה / &c. Solùm נטע plantavit ibi sine ה legitur. Itaque Maforetæ, codicum nonnullorum authoritate & rei evidentiâ freti, vocem eam librariorum culpâ in fine decurtatam, in margine restituerunt integram, נטֶעָה/ejusque puncta voci textuali subjecêre נטֶעָה. Eaque correctio adeò certa visa est magno Aria, & Theologis Lovaniensibus, qui Editionem Interlin. anni 1584. approbarunt, ut vocem נטֶעָה à Maforethis nimia religione in margine collocatam, in ipsum textum receperint, nullo facto variantis lectionis נטע indicio. Ad allegoriam tuam, quam & hic in textum infers, idem respondeo quod ad superiorem. Et hic monstrare debuisses; quodnam Christ. religionis mysterium in hoc loco delitescat, aut quomodo vel hac voce vel versu arguantur Judæi.
units.tr: If you think the letter ה was added wrongly, how then can you read nataha? The passage is about a woman of strength, whose industry and praises the wisest of kings recounts there. All the verbs said of her are feminine, both past and future: טַעֲמָה, חִגְרָה, זְמְמָה, חָעַשׁ, תָּקוּם, תִּתֵּן, הָיְתָה, הִרְשָׁה, etc. Only נטע, planted, is read there without ה. Therefore the Masoretes, trusting the authority of some manuscripts and the evidence of the matter, restored the word in the margin in its full form, נטֶעָה, and set its vowel points under the textual word, נטֶעָה. That correction seemed so certain to the great Arias Montanus, and to the Louvain theologians who approved the Interlinear edition of 1584, that they received the word נטֶעָה, which the Masoretes with excessive scruple had placed in the margin, into the text itself, without any sign of a variant reading נטע. To your allegory, which you also introduce here into the text, I give the same answer as to the earlier one. And here you ought to have shown what mystery of the Christian religion lies hidden in this place, or how the Jews are refuted either by this word or by this verse.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Locus 3. Jer. 2. 24. ubi in fine נַפְשִׁי naphscau, convertendum esse * afferunt (ita habet textus tuus) ׳ in ה / quia רפה onager est fœm. generis. Sed omnium animalium nomina, Pagnino teste 2. Gramm. cap. 2. sunt comm. gen. Adde quod per onagrum Israeliticus populus intelligitur.
units.tr: On the passage Jer. 2.24, where at the end נַפְשִׁי [naphshi] they say must be read as * (so your text has it) ׳ changed into ה, because the word for wild ass is of the feminine gender. But the names of all animals, according to Pagninus, Grammar 2, chapter 2, are of common gender. Add that the Israelite people is understood by the wild ass.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Potuisses & illud addere, ejusdem versus initio פְּרָה cum Masc. למור construi. Ut negari non possit, illud comm. gen. esse. Sed cum nullum hic quoque Christ. Religionis mysterium lateat, nec magis arguatur populus Israëliticus, si נפשו quàm si נַפְשָׁה legas, cùm denique hoc versu sæpius cum fœmininis quàm cum Masculinis jungatur, quis Masoretas arguat, quod non sine codicum authoritate alteram lectionem in margine notaverint? Quod verò postea multa adducis loca, in quibus affixa non mutaverint, licet masculina sint cum fœm. idque ut malitia eorum (Masoretharum) clarius innotesceat, frustra es. Vel ex eo discere potuisses, nisi animum tuum præjudicium cœcasset, eos in superioribus citra bonæ notæ codicum authoritatem nihil tentasse. Quæ autem hic malitia est bone vir, cum ex locis illis nullus sit, qui utrovis modo lectus, ullum Chri- stianæ fidei detrimentum, vel Judaicæ perfidiæ adjumentum afferat.
units.tr: You could also have added that at the beginning of the same verse פְּרָה is construed with the masculine למור, so that it cannot be denied that this word is of common gender. But since no mystery of the Christian religion lies hidden here either, and the people of Israel is no more accused whether one reads נפשו or נַפְשָׁה, and since in short this word in that verse is joined more often with feminines than with masculines, who would accuse the Masoretes of having noted the other reading in the margin without the authority of manuscripts? As for your claim that, in the many places you cite where they did not change the attached word, although the words are masculine with a feminine, they did so in order that the malice of the Masoretes might become clearer, you are wasting your effort. You could have learned from this, unless your prejudice had blinded your mind, that in the earlier places they attempted nothing without the authority of good manuscripts. What malice is there here, good sir, when none of those passages, read in either way, brings any harm to the Christian faith or any help to Jewish perfidy?

units.la: Marsennus.
units.tr: Marsennus.

units.la: Ex quibus utinam haretici sapientiores evadant dum viderint ישה mulierem statim fœmineo, alias genere masc. sumi debere. Sic enim in Scriptura sacra multa mysticè significantur.
units.tr: Would that the heretics became wiser from these things, when they see that ישה [ishah], woman, must immediately be taken as feminine, and otherwise as masculine. For in Holy Scripture many things are mystically signified in this way.

units.la: Amama.
units.tr: Amama.

units.la: Video hic ῥημάτων ναμέλα, mentis verò & solidæ rationis ne guttulam quidem. Quid enim? an ישה hoc uno eodemque loco simul masculinum & fœm. erit?
units.tr: I see here a mere jingle of words, but not so much as a drop of sense or solid reasoning. For what? Is ישה in this one and the same place to be both masculine and feminine at once?

units.la: Marsennus.
units.tr: Marsennus.

units.la: LXX. qui verterunt ἀνδρὸς, non ad ἀνθρώπων, quod est neutrius generis, sed ad ישה quod hic est Mascul. respexerunt. Quia tamen Interpres noster vidit apud Latinos mulierem semper esse fœmin. dixit IPSA.
units.tr: The LXX, who translated ἀνδρὸς [of a man], did not refer it to ἀνθρώπων [of men], which is of neuter gender, but looked to ישה, which here is masculine. Yet because our translator saw that among the Latins a woman is always feminine, he said IPSA.

units.la: Amama.
units.tr: Amama.

units.la: Miserēt me tui Marsenne. LXX. vertêrunt ἀνδρὸς, tum habitâ ratione vocis Ebrææ, quæ Masculina est, tum etiam habitâ ratione sensus: per Semen enim hic primo, literali & genuino sensu Filius intelligitur, Quomodo etiam usurpatur Genes.4. 25. Posuit mihi Deus semen aliud pro Habel, Et quid facies loco Gal.3.16. ubi eadem constructio, ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου, ὅς ἐστι Χριστός, Et semini tuo, qui est Christus. Quod verò dicis זרע hic esse Masculini generis, cui persuadebis? Nulli certè, nisi ἀμέλει τῆς ἀνδρολήπτης siderato. Et si ita est, rursus quærere illud liceat, cur pronomen Masc. הוא sollicitaris?
units.tr: Pity me, Marsennus. The LXX translated ἀνδρὸς [of a man], both taking account of the Hebrew word, which is masculine, and taking account of the sense: for by "seed" here, in the first, literal and genuine sense, a son is understood, as it is also used in Gen. 4.25: God has appointed me another seed in place of Abel. And what will you do with Gal. 3.16, where the same construction occurs: ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου, ὅς ἐστι Χριστός [to your seed, which is Christ]? As for your claim that זרע here is of masculine gender, who will you persuade? Nobody, surely, except one struck by some man-hating madness [ἀμέλει τῆς ἀνδρολήπτης]. And if that is so, may I ask again why you are troubled by the masculine pronoun הוא?

units.la: Patrum aliorumque quas adducis authoritates alii discussere Josephi testimonium ex I. lib. Antiq. cap.2. citas non optimâ fide, præcepit ut mulier ejus capiti plagas inferret. Monstra vel unum Græcum, codicem, qui vocem γυναῖκα habeat. Sed inquit Corn. à Laà Lapide, hæretici vocem γνωη suffulêrunt. Itane? Si soli illi codices, qui vel à nostris Typographis, vel post exortas super hoc loco contentiones excusi sunt, voce illa γνωη carerent, speciem aliquam haberet hæc criminatio. Quod pag. 1366. dicis Chaldæum paraphrasten pronomen hoc neutro posuisse, miror cur non idem de Ebræo asseras. Cum utrobique sit הוא & utraque lingua neutro genere careat. Sed & lxx. inquis, neutraliter sumere videntur, cum post αὐτὸς posuerunt αὐτὸς. Ad illud jam responsum est.
units.tr: As for the testimonies of the Fathers and others that you adduce, others have examined them. You cite Josephus, Antiquities book 1, chapter 2, not with good faith: he commanded that his wife should inflict blows on his head. Show me even one Greek manuscript that has the word γυναῖκα [woman]. But Cornelius à Lapide says the heretics propped up their case by the word γνωη. Really? If only those manuscripts which were printed either by our printers or after the disputes over this passage arose lacked that word γνωη, the charge would have some appearance of truth. As for your statement on p. 1366 that the Chaldee paraphrast put this pronoun in the neuter, I wonder why you do not say the same of the Hebrew. Both have הוא, and both languages lack a neuter gender. But the LXX too, you say, seem to take it neuterly, since after αὐτὸς they put αὐτὸς. To that the answer has already been given.

units.la: Antequam manum tollam de hac tabula, ponam verba Corn. à Lapide in hunc ipsum locum. * Hæc inquit, videtur etiam esse vera lectio in Ebr. Nam est hic keri uketif, id est alia lectio alia scriptio. Licet enim in textu legatur הוא ipsum tamen de more in margine (uti habent exemplaria correctiora) notatur vera lectio, sc. legendum esse היא id est ipsa. Hæc Cornelius. Audimus vero libentes illam confessionem, in textu legi masc. הוא / At desideto videre exemplar vel unum, quod in margine habeat היא / Ipsum enim illud Antverp. exemplar de quo supra prolixe egimus, in textu quidem habet הוּא cum nota ׂ Chetib, at in margine nullum Keri repositum est. Temerè ergo hæc chartis illevit Cornelius, & magis temere probavit ea Marsennus censurâ in Probl. 55. Georgii Veneti. Incepimus, Lector, manum conferre cum Marsenno, itaque & aliqua hic pergam attexere, ut molestissimo hoc labore defunctus, ad illud redeam, quod præcipuum hujus operis argumentum esse volui.
units.tr: Before I take my hand off this board, I will set down the words of Cornelius à Lapide on this very passage. He says: this also seems to be the true reading in the Hebrew. For here there is the keri uketif, that is, a different reading from the writing. For although הוא is read in the text, the true reading is nonetheless noted in the margin, as is customary (as the more correct copies have), namely that היא, that is, "she herself," is to be read. So says Cornelius. We gladly hear that confession, that the masculine הוא is read in the text. But I would like to see a single copy that has היא in the margin. For that very Antwerp copy, of which we have spoken at length above, has הוּא in the text with the mark of Chetib, but no Keri is placed in the margin at all. Cornelius therefore scribbled these things on his pages rashly, and Marsennus, in his criticism of Problem 55 of Georgius Venetus, approved them all the more rashly. Reader, I have begun to come to grips with Marsennus, and so I shall add a few more points here, so that, having got through this most tiresome labour, I may return to that which I wanted to be the chief argument of this work.

units.la: CAP. IV. verf. 13.
units.tr: CHAP. IV. verse 13.

units.la: Vulg. Majus est peccatum meum, quàm ut veniam merear. ]Ebr. מִנְּשׂוֹא / Dixi Ebr. נשׂא alique iniquitatem, aliquando pœnam iniquitatis, metonymicè significare. Ut doceremur pœnam & peccatum natura sua indivisos esse comites. Hoc ipse Marsenus negare non audet. Addidi, utramque significationem hic satis commodè posse explicari, modò, si primam signif. eligas, מִנְּשׂוֹא reddas per passivum מִתְּנַשֵּׂא / id quod non est insolens: hoc sensu, major est iniquitas mea, quàm ut possit condonari. Alias sic reddendum esse locum, Major est pœna iniquitatis meæ, quàm ut ferre possim, scil. eam. [& Vatabl. Pagn. Oleastrius. Et ex nostris stris Mercerus, Pisc. Martin. Junius, Genevenses, Deodatus, Drusius & alii. Quam interpretationem si admittimus, & certe cò videntur cogere sequentia, tunc illud Augustini, Mentiris Cain, nam major est Dei misericordia, quam omnium hominum iniquitas, pie quidem, sed non ad rem dictum fuerit. Posset tamen hic versus, etiam voce עָוֹן pro iniquitate sumpta, cum sequentibus satis commode cohærere si pronuntiatione eum jungeres & notam interrogandi subaudias, An major est iniquitas mea quam ut condonari possit? Ac tunc quidem erunt verba non desperantis, sed cum Deo de poenæ gravitate expostulantis.] Sed quod ad vocem מנשא attinet, eam nunquam significare, veniam mereri asserui, atque ex ea versione meritum congrui aluisse Pontificios, &c. Quid ad hæc.
units.tr: Vulgate: My sin is greater than that I can deserve pardon. ] Hebrew: מִנְּשׂוֹא [minnesōʾ]. I have said that the Hebrew נשׂא is sometimes used metonymically for iniquity, and sometimes for the punishment of iniquity, so that we might be taught that punishment and sin are by nature inseparable companions. Marsenus himself does not dare to deny this. I added that both meanings can be explained here quite fitly, provided that, if you choose the first meaning, you render מִנְּשׂוֹא by the passive מִתְּנַשֵּׂא [mitnaśśēʾ], which is not unusual. In this sense the sentence reads: my iniquity is greater than it can be forgiven. Others have rendered the passage otherwise: The punishment of my iniquity is greater than I can bear, namely it. [So also Vatablus, Pagninus, Oleastrius. Among our own writers Mercerus, Piscator, Martin, Junius, the Genevans, Deodatus, Drusius and others. If we accept this interpretation, and indeed what follows seems to compel it, then the saying of Augustine, You lie, Cain, for the mercy of God is greater than the iniquity of all men, would be pious but not to the point.] Yet this verse, even if עָוֹן [ʿāwōn] is taken to mean iniquity, can cohere well enough with what follows, if you join it to the following words in pronunciation and understand a question mark: Is my iniquity greater than that it can be forgiven? The words would then be not those of one who despairs, but of one who complains to God about the severity of the punishment. As for the word מנשא, I have asserted that it never means to deserve pardon, and that the Papists have fed on this version to build their doctrine of merit, and so on. What does Marsenus say to this?

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Mentitur Amama, cum ait nos in hoc loco meritum congrui vel fundare vel saltem alere, & מנשא pro מהנשא positum esse, sicut in ulti-mo versu hujus capitis לקרא pro להקרא.
units.tr: Amama lies when he says that we in this place either found or at least nourish congruous merit, and that מנשא stands for מהנשא, just as in the last verse of this chapter לקרא stands for להקרא.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Quin tu inspice ut alios omittam Lindani Panopliam, lib. 3. cap. 20. in margine, videbisque ex his locis Gen. 4. 13. Eccl. 16. 15. Ebr. 13. 6. cum sic inferre, en meriti vocabulum in Scriptura Si hic fallor circa locum præsentem, liber enim mihi nunc ad manum non est, non erubescam retractare hanc assertionem. Quod vero ad מנשא attinet, an ideo tibi fides habebitur, quia dicis me mentiri? Illum enim flosculum Sot, nova repetendum mihi reliquisti.
units.tr: Why don't you look, to pass over the others, at Lindanus's Panoplia, book 3, chapter 20, in the margin? You will see from these passages, Gen. 4.13, Eccl. 16.15 and Heb. 13.6, that he infers from them here is the word merit in Scripture. If I am wrong about the present passage (for I do not have the book to hand now), I will not be ashamed to retract this assertion. But as for מנשא, will I be trusted on that account, just because you say I am lying? For you have left me that little flower Sot, nova to repeat.

units.la: CAP. codem, vers. 16.
units.tr: Chapter the same, verse 16.

units.la: Vulg. Habitavit profugus in terra.] Ebr. habitavit in terra Nod. Sic quoque Cajet. Sic Josephus & LXX. licet voce aliquantulum corrupta, ἐν γῇ Ναιδ. Ita quoque Marcus Marinus in Arca Noë, Pagn. Arias Mont. & alii.
units.tr: The Vulgate: He dwelt a fugitive in the land. The Hebrew: he dwelt in the land of Nod. So also Cajetan. So Josephus and the Septuagint, though with the word a little corrupted: in the land of Naid [ἐν γῇ Ναιδ]. So also Marcus Marinus in Arca Noë, Pagnine, Arias Montanus and others.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Sed ineptit Amama, dum Vulgatam arguit, quod vertat, in terrâ, cum tamen Nod terram vagam & profugii significet, ut ipsi Novatores eo longè doctiores, fatentur, Fagius, Mercerus, Drusius & alii. At non est mirum si cæcus cæcutiat & qui lynceos oculos habere credit, nihil videat.
units.tr: But Amama is foolish in that, while he accuses the Vulgate of rendering it "in the land", Nod nevertheless means a wandering and fugitive land, as the Novatores themselves, far more learned than he, admit: Fagius, Mercerus, Drusius and others. But it is no wonder if a blind man gropes about, and one who believes he has lynx's eyes sees nothing.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Non arguo vulgatam, quod vertat, in terra. Quid enim? An ארץ non significat in terrâ? Nod significare terram vagans & profugii, nego. Neque hoc unquam ex Fagio, Drusio, Mercero, quos me longe doctiores fuisse libens agnosco, probaveris. Nod semel extra hunc locum reperitur, sed cum affixo, נודי Ps.56.9. estque Infinitum Kal, ut à מורת fit מורת cum holem, & significat τὸ vagari meum; id est vagationem meam. At ubi significet terram vagam vel profugii, ostendendum tibi erat.
units.tr: I do not accuse the Vulgate of rendering it in the land. For what? Does ארץ not mean in the land? That Nod means wandering and fugitive land, I deny. Nor will you ever prove this from Fagius, Drusius or Mercerus, whom I gladly acknowledge to be far more learned than I am. Nod occurs only once outside this place, but with a suffix, נודי in Ps. 56.9, and it is the infinitive of Qal, formed as a noun with holem, and means my wandering, that is, my vagrancy. But where it means wandering or fugitive land, you were obliged to show.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: 1. Debuisses à tuo Mercero discere נוד idem significare, quod נדד ונע vagum & profugum. Fatemur autem LXX. vertisse εἰς γῆ Naid: sed nihil contra nos. 2. Nec enim negamus terram, in quam Cain fugit, Nod vocatam fuisse.
units.tr: 1. You ought to have learned from your Mercerus that נוד means the same as נדד and נע, wandering and fugitive. We grant, however, that the Septuagint translated it as into the land Naid [εἰς γῆ Ναιδ]; but that is nothing against us. 2. For we do not deny that the land into which Cain fled was called Nod.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: 1. Magno me honore mactas, dum Mercerum meum vocas. Virum, cui in Ebraicis parem nunquam edidit Gallia. Sed ubi docet, נוד idem significare quod נדד ונע? Verba Merceri in comment. Simplicius puto, esse loci seu terræ nomen aut regionis, quæ ita sit, non ante, sed post, ab ejus vagatione, quod in eâ obervârit, dicta, In addit. ad Thes. Pagn. Terra Nod (quod est commotio, demigratio, seu in terra vagationis (exilii) Hoc nomen inditum regioni, quam pulsus & profugus Cain inhabitavit. M. Citatque postea Pagnin. ex Thargum, in terra נדוד / Alii tamen codices habent נלי וּמטלְטל &c. Vides Mercerum interpretari per abstracta? Non ergo dicit idem esse quod נע וָנָד / 2. Si agnoscis, terram hanc vocatam fuisse Nod, quid in me incurris? Idem dico, & dum hoc dico, non nego, ita vocatam fuisse a vagatione & exilio Caini.
units.tr: 1. You overwhelm me with great honour in calling him my Mercerus, a man whom France has never produced an equal of in Hebrew. But where does he teach that נוד means the same as נדד and נע? Mercerus's words in his commentary are: I think it is more likely to be the name of a place or region, which was so called not before but after his wandering, from what he observed in it. In his addition to Pagnine's Thesaurus: The land of Nod (which means commotion, migration, or the land of wandering (exile), נדוד). This name was given to the region which the banished and fugitive Cain inhabited. M. And then he cites from Pagnine the Targum, in the land, נדוד. Other manuscripts, however, have נלי וּמטלְטל, and so on. Do you see that Mercerus explains it by abstract nouns? So he does not say it is the same as נע וָנָד. 2. If you acknowledge that this land was called Nod, why do you run into me? I say the same, and while I say it I do not deny that it was so called from Cain's wandering and exile.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: 1. At pecus illud Arcadicum relinquamus, nec enim dictionarium ipsum aut intellexisse aut legisse videtur, in quo נוד & נָד idem significant. Nempe motus, agitatus, vagatus est, fugit, migravit, exulavit, & נוד significat motionem, fugam, vagationem & exilium. 2. Itaque licet Nod nomen loci proprium designare possit, 3. attamen appellative Thargum & Hieron. sumsere,
units.tr: 1. But let us leave that Arcadian dolt alone, for he seems to have neither understood nor read the dictionary itself, in which נוד and נָד mean the same. Namely: moved, agitated, wandered, fled, migrated, went into exile; and נוד means motion, flight, wandering and exile. 2. So although Nod can designate the proper name of a place, 3. nevertheless the Targum and Jerome took it as a common noun,

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: 1. Ut qui ocymum serunt, felicius id nasci ad convitia interjecta autumant, ita tu quoque, quicquid dicis dicteriis rigas. Non retaliabo. Illud solummodo tibi expendendum relinquo, utrum haec convitia faciant ad gloriam Dei. Tu certe in ipso limine protestabaris, nihil te dicturum quod eo non spectaret. Dictionaria varia legi mi Marsenne, sed nullum repperi Lexicographum, qui id asserat, quod tu vis. Quomodo enim idem significarent thema seu Infinitivus, vel ut hoc tibi largiar, abstractum, & concretum? Quis dixerit idem significare <bl>צרק</bl> & <bl>צדיק</bl>? 2. Supra dixisti, te non negare, Nod esse nomen proprium loci. Hic illud largiris quasi per liberalem concessionem. 3. De iis non est quaestio, licet ex Pagnino supra ostenderim, codices aliquot Chaldaeae Paraphraseos nomen Nod retinuisse.
units.tr: 1. Just as those who grow basil believe it sprouts better when insults are thrown in, so you too sprinkle your remarks with taunts. I will not retaliate. I leave it to you alone to consider whether these insults serve the glory of God. You certainly declared at the very threshold that you would say nothing that did not aim at that. I have read various dictionaries, my Marsennus, but I have found no lexicographer who asserts what you want. For how could the theme or infinitive (or, to grant you this, the abstract and the concrete) mean the same? Who would say that צדק and צדיק mean the same? 2. Above you said you do not deny that Nod is the proper name of a place. Here you grant it as if by a generous concession. 3. That is not the question, although from Pagnine above I have shown that some manuscripts of the Chaldee Paraphrase retained the name Nod.

units.la: Vers. 26.
units.tr: Verse 26.

units.la: Ebr. | Vulg. Tunc coeptum est invocari nomen Domini. | Iste coepit in vocare nomen Domini.
units.tr: Hebrew | The Vulgate: Then it began to be called upon the name of the Lord. | This one began to call in the name of the Lord.

units.la: Duo
units.tr: Two

units.la: BIBLICI LIBER II
units.tr: BOOK II OF THE BIBLICAL ANTI-BARBARUS

units.la: Duo hic sunt, inquis, quæ negotium facessere videntur. 1. est אֵי adverbium temporis, quod à vulgato per iste redditum est. 2. Verbum הוחל cujus ambiguitate in varias itum est sententias. Pergis
units.tr: There are two things here, you say, that seem to cause trouble. (1) ei [אֵי], an adverb of time, which the Vulgate rendered by iste. (2) The verb huchal [הוחל], whose ambiguity has led to various interpretations. You go on.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Hoc advertit nescio quis Amama & exultat hic, imò insultat (non secus ac Aman alius) populo Dei & comprehensam putat Esthe-rem, Ecclesiam dico Catholicam, &c.
units.tr: Some fellow, Amama, has noticed this, and he exults here; nay, he insults (no differently from another Haman) the people of God, and thinks he has caught Esther, I mean the Catholic Church, etc.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Si penitius me nosses, Marsenne, poeniteret te, scio, hujus judicii, quod non caritas, sed bilis tibi dictavit. Dignus eras quem Generalis ista Memnonis increpatione affaretur Pu-gnare conduxi, te, non conviciari. λοιδορεῖ̈ ὃ ἀ̓ρξάτω ἀνδρες ποιητάς, ἀσπις ἀρπακόλιδας inquit ille apud Aristophanem. Multo minus ἀνδρα ξυλλόγων decet canina ista facundia. Amani me compa-ras & paronomasiam captas. Possem & te cum Marsya, allusione non minus commoda, conferre, Drusiumque contra, vel Mer-cerum, quos tam neglectim habes, cum Apolline. Sed quis-fructus, quis finis esset talium ineptiarum? Non istis machinis edomabis haereticos. Non his armis Catholicam religionem propagabis.
units.tr: If you knew me more intimately, Marsenne, I know you would repent of this judgment, which was dictated to you not by charity but by bile. You deserved to be addressed in the words that the general of Memnon used: "I hired you to fight, not to hurl abuse." [λοιδορεῖ, ὃ ἀρξάτω ἀνδρες ποιηταί, ἀσπὶς ἁρπακόλιδες] So says that man in Aristophanes. Still less does such doglike eloquence suit a man of the assemblies. You compare me with Aman and go hunting for a paronomasia. I could also compare you with Marsyas, an allusion no less apt, and set Drusius or Mercerus, whom you treat so carelessly, against Apollo. But what profit, what purpose would such trifling have? You will not tame heretics with these engines. You will not spread the Catholic religion with these weapons.

units.la: MARSENNUS.
units.tr: MARSENNUS.

units.la: Alia est vis dictionis alicujus in contextu ratione, quam si per se sumatur. Exemplum sis quod pro manibus habemus.
units.tr: The force of a word is different in its context from what it is when taken on its own. Let the example we have at hand serve as an illustration.

units.la: AMAMA.
units.tr: AMAMA.

units.la: Melius de Lectore tuo fuisses meritus, si aliud exemplum adduxisses. Hic enim τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ ἀνάμνησιν petis. Sed perge,
units.tr: You would have deserved better of your reader if you had brought forward a different example. Here you are asking for a reminder of the beginning [τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ ἀνάμνησιν]. But go on.

units.la: MAR. IN sumptum per se est adverbium temporis : orationi junctum, 1. non amittit quidem vim hujus significationis, sed alió refert, aut certè determinat ex antecedentibus & consequentibus, & significat tempus quo res hæc & ab eâ persona, de qua sermo est, facta esse dicitur. Tempus igitur significat, & 2. consignificat personam, maximè autem 3. ubi verbum est ambiguæ significationis, tempus aut personam à verbo consignificari solitam determinat. Verùm quia apud Latinos verba non habent hanc in significando ambiguitatem, & tempus personamque satis exprimunt, liberum fuit interpreti, eorum alterum explicite ponere. Satius tamen, ut personam exprimeret, quo 4. ambiguitatem quæ in Ebraeo occurrebat, tolleret, doceretque verbum הוחל personale esse non impersonale, quale mavis.
units.tr: MARSENNUS. Taken by itself, sumptum, the word is an adverb of time. Joined to a sentence, (1) it does not lose the force of this meaning, but it refers it elsewhere, or at least fixes it from what comes before and after, and it signifies the time at which the thing is said to have been done by the person who is the subject of the discussion. So it signifies time, and (2) it co-signifies the person, but most of all (3) where the verb is of ambiguous meaning, it fixes the time or person that the verb usually co-signifies. But since in Latin verbs do not have this ambiguity in signifying, and express both time and person well enough, it was open to the translator to state one of the two explicitly.
