units.la: Ex eo in vestra urbe prodiit doctissimi viri tractatus de genuina antiquitate vocalium, cum appendice oratione de hoc ipso nomine. Tum vere plane sedebat, meum istum fœtum æternis tenebris sepelire. Tam enim eleganter, tam plene Orationis istius author de isthoc argumento disserebat, nihil ut à me addi posse existimarem. At rursus, postquam incidi in postremos libros Miscellaneorum Cl. Viri, D. N i c. FULLERI, ut vidi magnum virum in appendice disputare adversus Cl. Drusii præceptoris mei, aliorumque eruditissimorum virorum sententiam, ut cognovi quosdam vitio creatos Prætores, iis qui Adonai legunt, superstitionis & nequiter imminuta textus efficacia crimen impingere, consilia in contrarium re-culi. culi. Ostendendum quippe erat, quam procul doctissimi viri, quorum me sequacem profiteor, superstitionis causas habuerint. Abstergenda erat nequiter imminuta textus efficacia macula. Ostendendum erat auditoribus meis, hanc lectionem esse antiquam & ab ipsis Apostolis sacratam, occurrendum erat scandalo, quod ea lectio tenerae conscientiae auditori praebere posset. Rogandi denique erant omnes boni, ne pertinaci praejudicio condemnent lectionem, quae gravissimis rationibus & magnorum virorum exemplis nititur. Hae rationes cum apud me praepotuissent, recognovi juvenile scriptum & multis additamentis auctum ivi. In testimonia Thalmudicorum & Rabbinorum, quae vulgo huc afferuntur, inquisivi accuratius. Ibi vero deprehendi, quam saepe testimonia Ebraeorum obtorto collo a viris etiam doctissimis trahantur aliorsum atque authores voluere. Ea causa est cur multa praeteriverim testimonia, quae vulgo in hac materia accongeruntur. Interim alia se obtulere, quae studioso lectori non molenti erit legere. Ita factum est, ut quod antea unius atque alterius schedae erat, ut vara vibiam sequitur, in aliquot schedas succreverit. Hic vero publice protestor, sicuti nulli unquam ob lectionem Iehova litem movi, ita ne nunc quidem mihi scopum esse, ut cum quopiam super hac re litigem, nedum ut petulantis linguae verbere eos insecter, qui hic diversi a nobis abeunt. Qui me historiam sacram Sulpitii Severi publice enarrantem audiunt, norunt, me a voce Iehova, quando loca scripturae integra ex Versione Junio-Tremelliana cito, non abhorrere. Quis enim ego sum, ut brachia dirigam contra hunc inveteratae consuetudinis torrentem? Adhaec, non ista quaestio est à qua salus vel pax Ecclesiarum dependeat, Grammaticæ pulpæ est. Ac proinde pedoris me augustiæ non capiunt subtilitatem istius responsi, quo omnia argumenta nonnulli difflare solent, Non curamus Grammatica argumenta.
units.tr: Since then there has appeared in your city the learned man's treatise on the genuine antiquity of the vowels, with an appended oration on this very name. At that point I truly resolved to bury my own little offspring in eternal darkness. The author of that oration treats this subject so elegantly and so fully that I thought nothing could be added by me. But then, after I came upon the last books of the Miscellanies of the distinguished man, Mr Nicholas Fuller, and saw the great man arguing in an appendix against the opinion of my teacher, the distinguished Drusius, and of other very learned men, and learned that some men, made magistrates by their faults, charge those who read Adonai with superstition and with having wickedly diminished the efficacy of the text, I changed my plan and went the other way. For it had to be shown how far from superstition the learned men whom I profess to follow had been. The stain of having wickedly diminished the efficacy of the text had to be wiped away. It had to be shown to my hearers that this reading is ancient and was hallowed by the Apostles themselves. The scandal that this reading might give to a tender conscience had to be met. Finally, all good people had to be asked not to condemn with a stubborn prejudice a reading that rests on very weighty reasons and on the examples of great men. Since these reasons carried great weight with me, I went over the youthful writing, which had been enlarged with many additions. I looked more carefully into the testimonies of the Talmudists and Rabbis that are commonly brought forward here. There I found how often the testimonies of the Hebrews are dragged, even by very learned men, twisted by the neck to a sense other than their authors intended. That is why I have passed over many of the testimonies that are commonly heaped together on this subject. Meanwhile other matters presented themselves, which the studious reader will not find tedious to read. So it happened that what had been the work of one or two sheets, as the saying goes, grew into several sheets. Here, however, I publicly declare that, just as I never brought a quarrel against anyone over the reading Iehova, so now too it is not my aim to contend with anyone on this matter, much less to lash with the whip of a wanton tongue those who here differ from us. Those who hear me publicly expounding the sacred history of Sulpicius Severus know that I do not shrink from the word Iehova when I quote whole passages of Scripture from the Junius-Tremellius version. For who am I to direct my arms against this torrent of long-established custom? Moreover, this is not a question on which the welfare or peace of the churches depends; it belongs to the grammar schools. And so the narrow limits of my chest cannot grasp the subtlety of that reply by which some people are wont to blow away all arguments: We do not care about grammatical arguments.

units.la: Nunc ad te venio, Reverende & Clarissime vir, Magna sunt tua quibus me tibi obligasti, merita. Jam tum cum Lugduni Batavorum Musis litarem, eximium in te patronum habui. Ex quo in hac statione versatus sum, sæpe benevolentiam tuam expertus sum. Atque hactenus fortassis gratitudinem aliquam præstare potuissem. At ex quo molestissimum istud iter, ante biennium, hyberno tempore, intensissimo gelu, suscepisti, ut mihi representares diploma Magnificorum Acad. Leidensis Curatorum, quo, te præcipue obstetricante, ad ordinariam Ebrææ linguæ professionem, quam magnus ille Erpenius immaturo suo obitu vacivam fecerat, vocabar, ex eo, inquam, omnis dignas grates persolvendi spes decollavit. Ex eo, ingrato mihi vivendum & moriendum esse video. Et quidem hæc ingenua, & ab intimis mentis meæ penetralibus profecta confessio est. Ejus chirographi vicem hanc dissertationem accipe, quam ex antiqua formula tuæ Rev. L. M. Q. dico & dedico. Materiam quam tracto, ut tibi approbem, non admodum laboro. Tu enim istius Synodi pars magna fuisti, in qua illa, quam hic defensum eo, lectio, prudentissimo decreto approbata est. Magis laboro, ut candidum hunc animum tibi probem, qui tuæ Rev. æternum devotus erit. Vale Rev. Domine & diurna bono Ecclesiarum & Academiæ. Franck. Frif. 12. Janu. 1628.
units.tr: Now I come to you, Reverend and distinguished sir. Great are your merits, by which you have bound me to you. Already when I was offering my sacrifices to the Muses at Leiden, I had you as an outstanding patron. Since I have been placed in this post, I have often experienced your goodwill, and up to now I might perhaps have been able to show some gratitude. But since you undertook that most troublesome journey, two years ago, in winter, in the most intense frost, to bring me the diploma of the Curators of the Illustrious Academy of Leiden, by which I was called, chiefly through your midwifery, to the ordinary professorship of the Hebrew language, which that great man Erpenius had left vacant by his untimely death, from that time, I say, all hope of paying you proper thanks has been cut off. From that time I see that I must live and die an ungrateful man. This is a candid confession, coming from the innermost recesses of my mind. Accept this dissertation in place of that written acknowledgement. I dedicate it to your Reverence, in the old formula. I do not take great pains to win your approval of the subject I treat, for you were a large part of that Synod in which the reading I defend here was approved by a most prudent decree. I take greater pains to show you this honest mind, which will be devoted to your Reverence for ever. Farewell, Reverend sir, and may you long be of good service to the churches and the Academy. Frankfurt on the Oder, 12 January 1628.

units.la: Tuæ Rev. devotissimus cultor
units.tr: Your Reverence's most devoted admirer,

units.la: S. AMAMA.
units.tr: S. AMAMA.

units.la: SIXTINI AMAMA DE NOMINE Tetragrammato DISSERTATIO.
units.tr: SIXTINI AMAMA ON THE NAME TETRAGRAMMATON: A DISSERTATION.

units.la: I. Nominum Dei alia ab essentia ejus, alia ab effectis attributisque desumpta sunt.
units.tr: I. Some names of God are taken from his essence, others from his effects and attributes.

units.la: II. Primas meritissimò tenent illa, quæ ab essentiâ desumpta, Theologi Græci ὀνόματα τὰ ὄντος vocarunt. Itaque Deo propriissimè conveniunt, utpote qui ἓλον ἐν ἑαυτῷ συνλαβὼν ἔχει τὸ εἶναι, οἷον π πέλαγος ὑσίας ἄπειρον id est universum illud esse complectens in se habet, quasi pelagus quoddam infinitum & immensum.
units.tr: II. Those taken from his essence come first, and rightly so. The Greek theologians called them names of being [ὀνόματα τὰ ὄντος]. Therefore they belong most properly to God, who, holding the whole of being gathered within himself [ἓλον ἐν ἑαυτῷ συνλαβὼν ἔχει τὸ εἶναι], is, as it were, an infinite and immense sea of being, that is, containing in himself that whole being, as if it were some infinite and immense sea.

units.la: III. Suntque ea numero tria, יה / אהיה & quod principem locum obtinet. יהוה /
units.tr: III. There are three such names: יה [Yah], אהיה [Ehyeh], and the one that holds the chief place, יהוה [YHVH].

units.la: VI. Nam quod alii quartum accongesêre, vid הוא / ni-nium à veritatis regione, ut Luciliano isto utar, aberrârunt. Citant locum ex Ps.102.28. ubi & Lxx. ὁ αὐτὸς reddidêre. Sed & isthîc, & alibi, vid. Jesa.42.8. quæ duo loca hîc afferri solent, pronomen illud à propriâ notione dimovere nihil cogit. Merito ergo à viris doctis explosum est.
units.tr: IV. As for the fourth name that others have added, namely הוא [Hu], they have strayed from the region of truth, to borrow that Lucianic phrase. They cite Ps. 102.28, where the LXX rendered it ὁ αὐτὸς [the same]. But there, and elsewhere, see Isa. 42.8, which are the two passages usually cited here, do not compel us to remove that pronoun from its proper meaning. Rightly, therefore, learned men have rejected it.

units.la: V. Tria hæc nomina ab uno eodemque themate descendunt. Primum enim quod attinet, vid. אהיה / futurum est, Kal. ab יה / esse autem nomen Dei adversus Paulum Burgensem docent ex loco Exodi 3.14. אהיה misit me ad vos.
units.tr: V. These three names descend from one and the same root. First, as for אהיה [Ehyeh], it is the future tense, Qal, of היה [to be]. That יה [Yah] is a name of God, however, they teach against Paul of Burgos from Exodus 3.14, "Ehyeh has sent me to you."

units.la: VI. Sunt qui putant hoc esse πιεγαγέμματ & quod Deus de se dixit primâ persona, אהיה id est sum, id homines de illo efferre in tertiâ יהיה est ille qui est, & mutato Jod in Vau (ut literæ istæ alternare solent) יהוה /
units.tr: VI. Some think that what God said of himself in the first person, אהיה, "I am", men express about him in the third person, יהיה, "he is who is", and that by changing Yod into Vav (as these letters commonly alternate) it became יהוה.

units.la: VII. Hiscuni ad Exod.3.15. אהיה האשר בפסוק הראשון הוא שמיל עולם שכן אנוכותכין השם המיוהר כמצפץ שהכה קורא לעצמו תחצץ ואנו קורין לו מצפץ/ Quæ verba sic convertit Cl. Drusius, pag. 94.
units.tr: VII. Hiscuni, on Exod. 3.15, [writes in Hebrew, roughly:] Ehyeh, in the first verse, is my name for ever; for the Holy One, blessed be he, called himself by the ineffable name, and we call him by another name. Drusius, p. 94, translates these words as follows.

units.la: 94. Ehjeh memoratum versu praecedente [vid. 14.] est nomen meum in seculum. [ Sic enim nos scribimus nomen appropriatum per Mitz-phatz, ] Deus enim benedictus vocaverat [ vocat ] se ipsum תצפץ hoc est אהיה / sed nos vocamus eum מצפץ id est יהוה / Hactenus Cl. Druf. Ecce ה מצפץ interpretatur יהוה / & תצפץ exponit per אהיה / Sed non explicat. Ego hic haerebam, neque me expedivissem, nisi commodum in mentem mihi venisset commutatio literarum, quam Ethbasch vocant. מצפץ ergo in ista commutatione est יהוה / Et מצפץ est אהיה / Ita amant tenebriones isti caliginem offundere suis commentariis, ut saepe alium commentarium desiderent. In sequentibus clarior est idem Hiscuni, Porro, inquit, Vau in מצפץ (id est יהוה) ponitur pro Jod, ut in הוה fuit, pro היה / Et quia non convenit, ut dictio significans essentiam sanctitatis eadem sit cum dictionibus denotantibus essentiam profanam, mutata est ab aliis profanis vocibus, vid. per migrationem Jod in vau, uti antea dixerat.
units.tr: 94. Ehyeh, mentioned in the preceding verse [see 14], is my name for ever. [Thus we write the proper name by Mitz-phatz.] For the blessed God had called himself תצפץ, that is Ehyeh, but we call him מצפץ, that is YHVH. So far Drusius. See, he interprets מצפץ as YHVH and explains תצפץ as Ehyeh, but he does not explain how. I was stuck here and would not have got free, had the exchange of letters, which they call Atbash, not conveniently come to mind. So in that exchange מצפץ is YHVH, and מצפץ is Ehyeh. Thus those shadowy men love to cast darkness over their commentaries, so that one often needs another commentary to explain them. In what follows Hiscuni is clearer: Furthermore, he says, Vav in מצפץ (that is YHVH) stands for Yod, as in הוה for היה. And because it is not fitting that a word signifying the essence of holiness should be the same as words denoting profane essence, it has been changed from other profane words, namely by the migration of Yod into Vav, as he said before.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Secundum quod attinet, יה / f decurtatum putatur ex Tetragrammato יהוה / cujus certe duas anteriores literas nec id tantum, sed & primae syllabae sonum, si vera ea lectio est, quam Samaritanis g Theodoretus aliique ascribunt, nimirum Jave.
units.tr: As for the second name, יה [Yah] is thought to be shortened from the Tetragrammaton יהוה, of which at least the two first letters are kept, and indeed the sound of the first syllable as well, if that reading is correct which Theodoret and others ascribe to the Samaritans, namely Jave.

units.la: IX. Hoc esse illud nonnulli opinantur, quod in nominum quorundam finibus occurrit, ut זכריה ישעיה עובריה / &c. cui sententiae adversatur Scindlerus, tum quia in ejusmodi nusquam comparet ה Mappik, tum quia saepe cum vau Paragogico leguntur, ישעיהו / &c. sed primae ejus rationi oppono vocem ידידיה * quam ipse Scindlerus in themate ידר interpretatur dilectum Domini, praeunte Scriptura, 2. Sam. 18. verf. 24. 25. Quicquid sit, illud extra omnem contraversiae aleam positum est, ex hoc nomine compositam esse vocem הללויה / unde, licet ὀι Lxx. vocem Ebr. retinuerint, ᵇ Theodotio tamen Interpres vetus, ἐιμὶ τὸ ὤν, reddidit. Ergo יה τὸ ὄν. Ens entium, principium essendi.
units.tr: IX. Some think this is the ending found in certain names, such as זכריה [Zechariah], ישעיה [Isaiah], עובריה [Obadiah], and so on. Scindlerus opposes this view, both because a mappiq he never appears in such names and because they are often read with the paragogic vav, as ישעיהו. But to his first reason I oppose the word ידידיה [Yedidyah], which Scindlerus himself, from the root ידד, explains as "beloved of the Lord", following Scripture (2 Sam. 12.24–25). However that may be, it is beyond all dispute that the word הללויה [Hallelujah] is compounded from this name. Hence, although the LXX kept the Hebrew word, the old translator Theodotion rendered it ἐγὼ εἰμὶ τὸ ὤν [I am the one who is]. Therefore יה = τὸ ὄν, Ens entium, the principle of being.

units.la: X. Friget nimium illud quorundam commentum, hoc nomen, ut a Tetragr. decurtatum est, sic & denotare Deum decurtatum & imminutum id est Christum hominem factum & pro peccatis nostris passum. Neque etiam video quid spectaverit Hieronymus, quando ad Jesa. 26. asserit, nomen JAH inviinvisibilem, ADONAI vero ineffabilem significare.
units.tr: X. That opinion of some is rather frigid, namely that this name, as shortened from the Tetragrammaton, also denotes God shortened and diminished, that is, Christ made man and suffering for our sins. Nor do I see what Jerome had in view when, on Isa. 26, he asserts that the name JAH means "invisible" and ADONAI means "ineffable".

units.la: XI. Facessam ab hoc nomine, si illud apposuero, juxta Cabalistas hoc nomen symbolum esse iltius affectus in Deo, quo condonat peccata; Quia vid. frequentissimè iis in locis & argumentis usurpatur, ubi hæc misericordia ceu materia & sermo divinæ laudis commendatur. Onkelos & Jonathan vocem illam aliquando reddiderunt per רחילא id est timorem, pavorem Certe Gen. 31.42. Deus vocatur פחד יצחק pavor Isaac id est interprete Chaldæo Onkelos, דחהל לה יצחק quem timuit Isaac. At cur nomen יה ita reddiderint, adhuc quæro. Loca ex multis hæc sunt, Jesa.12.2. Jesa.26 4. Pfal.118.14. Exod. 17. verf. ult.
units.tr: XI. I will drop this name once I have mentioned it. According to the Cabalists, it is a symbol of that affection in God by which he pardons sins, since it is most often used in those places and contexts where this mercy is commended as the matter and theme of divine praise. Onkelos and Jonathan sometimes rendered that word by רחילא, that is, fear or dread. Certainly in Gen. 31.42 God is called פחד יצחק, "the dread of Isaac", that is, according to the Chaldee interpreter Onkelos, "whom Isaac feared". But why they rendered the name יה in this way, I still ask. The passages are many: Isa. 12.2; Isa. 26.4; Ps. 118.14; Exod. 17, last verse.

units.la: XII. Restat tertium, κατ' ἐξοχὴν ὄνομα γῆ ὄνλος & שם nomen substantiæ dictum, videlicet nomen Jod, He, Vau, He.
units.tr: XII. There remains the third, the name par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν ὄνομα], called the name of substance, שם, namely the name Yod, He, Vav, He.

units.la: XIII. Thema habet היה fuit. Ergo ab essentia deductum hoc nomen est. Et certe Deus non solum est, sed & facit esse. Hinc optimè dicitur nomen illud denotare Dei æternitatem, & veracitatem. Æternitatem: Ille enim verè est, qui æternus est, qui est primus & ultimus, Apocal. 1.8. ὁ ὢν, ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος. * & verf. 4. ἀπὸ ὁ ὢν, καὶ ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, pro quo Apoc.16.5. ὁ ὢν, ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ὅσιος, quomodo istum locum restituit D. Beza. Quam æternitatem simili periphrasi Gentiles suo quoque Jovi adscripsère. Illi enim, teste Pausania, hoc versu accinebant vates, Ζεὺς ἦν, Ζεὺς ἔστι, Ζεὺς ἔσεσθαι, ὦ μεγάλη Ζεῦ
units.tr: XIII. Its root is היה, "was". So this name is derived from essence. And certainly God not only is, but also makes things to be. Hence it is rightly said that this name denotes God's eternity and truthfulness. Eternity: for he truly is who is eternal, who is first and last, Rev. 1.8, ὁ ὢν, ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος [the one who is, who was, and who is to come]; and v. 4, ἀπὸ ὁ ὢν, καὶ ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, for which Rev. 16.5 has ὁ ὢν, ὁ ἦν, καὶ ὁ ὅσιος [the one who is, who was, and the holy one], as Beza restored that passage. The Gentiles ascribed this same eternity to their Jupiter, using a similar periphrasis. For, as Pausanias reports, the seers chanted in this verse: Ζεὺς ἦν, Ζεὺς ἔστι, Ζεὺς ἔσεσθαι, ὦ μεγάλη Ζεῦ [Zeus was, Zeus is, Zeus shall be, O great Zeus].

units.la: XIV. Independentiam addidi. Ille enim verè est, qui à seipso est. Quò respiciens Cl. Junius hoc ipsum nomen in suo Jrenico, αὐτῶν, reddidit. Efficacitatem: A Deo enim habent suum esse omnes creaturæ. Veracitatem denique: Namque Deus præstat & esse facit id quod promisit, sive quod idem est. omnibus suis promissionibus dat τὸ εἶναι; ut non solum sit ὁ ὢν καὶ αὐτῶν, sed & ὢν & ἀποστολὸς. Atque hoc postremum, veracitatem, potissimum spectavit Deus apud Mosem, Exod. 6.2. Istorum enim verborum hæc mens est: Apparui quidem Abrahamo, &c. nomine El schaddai, id est Dei omnipotentis, atque ita docui me posse ipsis præstare promissionem terræ Canaan: At in nomine יהוה non innotui illis id est nondum praestiti ipsis quod promisi. Nunc demum cognoscetis vim hujus nominis, vid. cognoscetis me non solùm ὅντα, sed & οὐσιοῦντα. Quod promisi, quod mihi factu possibile esse Abrahamo declaravi, jam tandem faciam ut existat, jam praestabo. Ebraeorum de voce illa pervulgata sententia haec est, in Elohim esse significationem מדת הדין id est proprietatis iudicii & stricti juris, at in יהוה contineri מדת הרחמים proprietatem misericordiae. At neutrum firmo in S. Literis tibicine nititur. Namque τὸ Elohim quod attinet, illis accedimus, qui ejus thema ti jam inusitato (אלה) notionem adorandi assignant, idq; ex Arabismo, in quo אלה adorare significat. Unde Arabes Deum quoque Ilahon vocant, quia solus adorandus est.
units.tr: XIV. I have added independence. For he truly is who is from himself. Looking to this, the learned Junius rendered this very name in his Irenicum as αὐτῶν [self-existent]. Efficacy: for all creatures have their being from God. Veracity, finally: for God brings about and makes to be what he has promised, or, which is the same, he gives τὸ εἶναι [being] to all his promises, so that he is not only ὁ ὢν [the one who is] and αὐτῶν, but also ὢν and faithful [ἀποστολός]. And this last, veracity, was what God especially had in view with Moses, Exod. 6.2. The sense of those words is this: I indeed appeared to Abraham, etc., under the name El Shaddai, that is, God Almighty, and so taught that I am able to perform for them the promise of the land of Canaan. But by the name YHVH I was not made known to them, that is, I had not yet performed for them what I promised. Now at last you will know the power of this name, that is, you will know me not only as one who is, but as one who makes things be. What I promised, what I showed Abraham could be done by me, I will now at last bring into being; now I will perform it. The Hebrews' widely held view about those names is this: in Elohim is the attribute of judgment, the property of strict justice, while in YHVH is contained the attribute of mercy. But neither view rests on firm support in the Holy Scriptures. As for Elohim, we follow those who derive it from the now unused root אלה, assigning it the sense of "to worship", from Arabic, where אלה means "to worship". Hence the Arabs also call God Ilah, because he alone is to be worshipped.

units.la: XV. Graviter ergo hic lapsus est. * Hieron. ab Oleastro, Hispanus, Dominicanus, facerrumque Senatus Inquisitionis, dum viveret, assessor, dum vocem Jehova, quam putat veram lectionem Terragrammati esse, serio deducit à nomine הוה, quod perniciem, calamitatem, accidensque malum significat, semperque in malam partem sumi & Lexica & concordantiae docebunt.
units.tr: Therefore he fell badly here. Hieronymus ab Oleastro, a Spanish Dominican and, while he lived, the most scrupulous assessor of the Spanish Inquisition, seriously derives Jehova, which he thinks is the true reading of the Tetragrammaton, from the word הוה, which signifies destruction, calamity and accidental evil. Lexicons and concordances will show that it is always taken in a bad sense.

units.la: XVI. In hunc errorem praecipitem cum dedit falsa hypothesis, quâ credidit, vocem Jehova veram nominis, de quo agit, lectionem esse. Sed quemadmodum cavendum est, ne in disputatione vocem controversam Jehova cum nomine Tetragram. confundamus, nisi βαλτολογεῖν & τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ κεἰμενον petere velimus, ita & ab altera parte videndum, ne cum nomine אהיה (per quod tamen ab omni aevo lectum est) in interpretatione miscceamus. In quo prae imperitiâ Ebraismi Tertullianum lapsum fuisse supra pag.292. ostendimus.
units.tr: This headlong error came from a false hypothesis, namely that the word Jehova is the true reading of the name under discussion. But just as we must take care not to confuse the disputed word Jehova with the Tetragrammaton in argument, unless we wish to beg the question [βαλτολογεῖν, τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ κείμενον], so on the other side we must take care not to mix it up in interpretation with the name אהיה, by which the name has nevertheless been read from every age. In this, through ignorance of Hebrew, Tertullian went wrong, as we have shown above on page 292.

units.la: XVII. Sed redeamus ex diverticulo in viam. Vocatur hoc nomen πεντάγραμμα id est quadriliterum, idque κατ' ἐξοχὴν, nam & alia Dei nomina quadrilitera sunt, ut יהוה / אלוה / אהיה / Atq; hic non possum non mirari crassam illam Mathaei Doringii inscitiam, qui ipsam hanc vocem [πεντάγραμμα] putavit esse illud nomen, quod eruditi πεντάγραμμα vocare consueverunt.
units.tr: But let us return from the digression to the road. This name is called πεντάγραμμα [pentagramma], that is, the four-lettered name, and it is so called preeminently, for other names of God are also four-lettered, such as יהוה, אלוה and אהיה. Here I cannot but marvel at the gross ignorance of Matthaeus Doringius, who thought that this very word [πεντάγραμμα] was the name that learned men customarily call the pentagramma.

units.la: XVIII. Appellatur & aliis nominibus quae invenies apud alios. Celeberrima appellatio ista est, שם המפרש schem hammeforash, me-
units.tr: It is also called by other names, which you will find in other writers. The most famous of these is שם המפרש, schem hammeforash, me-

units.la: * Comm. in Genes. cap. 1. verba ejus haec sunt, Ego video in radice הוה duo esse vid. הוה esse & הוה quod juxta Ebraos est accidens eventus quo malus; Et cum hova plus similitudinem habeat cum Jehova, quam hava, puto melius derivari ab hova quam ab Hava.
units.tr: * Commentary on Genesis 1. His words are these: "I see that there are two things in the root הוה: הוה, to be, and הוה, which according to the Hebrews is an accident of an event, by which something evil happens. And since hova has more resemblance to Jehovah than hava does, I think it is better derived from hova than from Hava."

units.la: • Hujus replicae pro Lyra contra Burgensem in Bibliis Lyrae simul excudi fo- lio. Dixe. ac mephorasch. Vnde autem ita appellatum sit, non una eruditorum sententia est. In causa est ωολύωνυμον vocis. Radix enim in linguis orientalibus significat separare, exponere, proferre. Hinc alii reddunt, nomen separatum. Maimon in More, cap. 61. כל שמותיו יתעלה הנמצאים בספרים כלם נגזרים מן הפעולות וזה מה שאין העלם בו, אלא שם אהר והוא יור הא ויו הא שהוא שם מיוחד לו יתעלה ולה נקרא שם מפורש ענינו שהוא יורה על עצמו יתעלה הוראה מבוארת אין השתתפות כה / hoc est, omnia nomina [ Dei] exaltandi quae reperiuntur in libris desumpta sunt ab ejus operibus. Atque hic plane nulla est occultatio. Sed nomen unum est, vid. nomen, Jod, He, Vau, He, quod est appropriatum illi exaltando, quod ideo vocatur nomen mephorasch, nempe quia denotat Deum significatione perspicua &c. אםנם שאר שמותיו הנכבדים מורים בשחוף להיותם נגזרים מפעולות / hoc est, Sed cetera nomina ejus gloriosa * ambigue significant quia sumpta sunt ab operibus. Vides ex hujus mente dici mephorasch id est separatum, quia separatum est ab aliis Dei nominibus, utpote nomen ab omni æquivocatione & ambiguitate liberum & proinde creaturis incommunicabile. Ut non male reddi quoque possit, nomen clarum, evidens. Sed quia omne id fere, quod miramur, ideo miramur, quia ratio agendi & causæ ejus à mente captuque nostro separata sunt, ideo Munsterus in Diction. Chald. reddidit nomen mirabile. Jud. 13. 18. In Ebraeo est פלאי mirabile, proprie separatum. Haec enim est generalis themati notio, ad quam reliquae significata, occultum, difficile, impossibile, mirabile, ignotum esse, &c. tanquam species ad genus referri possunt. Chaldaeus reddit מפרש / ad verbum, separatum, scilicet, ex Munsteri mente, à nostro captu. Et certe merito dixeris nomen mirabile, quod puram Dei essentiam significat, quam humani pectoris angustiæ non capiunt. Sed Cl. Drusius conjectat istic loci pro מפרש legendum מפרש / in Afel, & vocem פרישו quoque notare miracula. Alii perpetuo שם המפורש interpretantur, nomen expositum. Hanc Interpretationem sibi prae altera illa arridere, profitetur Cl Drusius cap.6. Et certe usitatissima notio פרש in conjug. Phiel haec est, interpretari, exponere, declarare. Cur autem sic dictum? Respondent ita appellatum, quod per nomina 12. & 42. literarum exponeretur, de quibus in sequentibus dicetur. Vide Galatin. 2. 10. Ego ut hanc interpretationem non dammo, ita eruditorum judiciis expendendam dabo meam conjectu-ram. פָּרַשׁ in Phael Chald. passim significat proferre, pronunciare, nuncupare, Quid ergo, nomen suis propriis literis prolatum pronuntiatumve? שְׁקְרִיאָתוֹ כְּכְתִיבָתוֹ quod legitur uti scribitur. Ut hac nomenclatura distinguatur à cognomine Adonai, per cujus ceu vicarii nominis consonas vulgo exprimitur. Atque haec de pervulgata illa hujus nominis appellatione. A caeteris abstineo.
units.tr: • This reply to Lyra against the Burgensis was printed together with Lyra's commentary in the Bibles, on the same folio. It is also called mephorasch. Opinions of scholars differ as to why it is so called. The reason lies in the many meanings of the word. In the eastern languages the root means to separate, to set forth, to bring forth. Hence some render it "the separated name." Maimonides in More, chapter 61, says: "[Hebrew: כל שמותיו יתעלה הנמצאים בספרים כלם נגזרים מן הפעולות וזה מה שאין העלם בו, אלא שם אחד והוא יוד הא ויו הא שהוא שם מיוחד לו יתעלה ולכן נקרא שם מפורש ענינו שהוא יורה על עצמו יתעלה הוראה מבוארת אין השתתפות בה] All the names of God, exalted be He, which are found in the books, are derived from his works, and in these there is no concealment. But there is one name, namely the name Yod, He, Vau, He, which is peculiar to him, exalted be He, and therefore it is called the mephorasch name, because it denotes God, exalted be He, by a clear signification, with no sharing in it." And [Hebrew: אמנם שאר שמותיו הנכבדים מורים בשתוף להיותם נגזרים מפעולות] "but his other glorious names signify ambiguously, because they are derived from works." You see from his meaning that it is called mephorasch, that is, separated, because it is separated from the other names of God, being a name free from all equivocation and ambiguity and therefore incommunicable to creatures. It could also fairly be rendered "the clear, evident name." But because almost everything we admire, we admire because the reason for its working and its cause are separated from our mind and grasp, Munsterus in his Chaldee dictionary rendered it "the wonderful name," citing Judges 13:18. In the Hebrew there is פלאי, "wonderful," properly "separated." For this is the general notion of the theme, to which the other meanings, "hidden, difficult, impossible, wonderful, unknown," and so on, can be referred as species to a genus. The Chaldean renders מפרש literally as "separated," that is, in Munsterus's sense, separated from our grasp. And certainly one could fairly call it the wonderful name, which signifies the pure essence of God, which the narrowness of the human breast cannot grasp. But the learned Drusius conjectures that in that place one should read מפרש as the Afel form, and that the word פרישו also means "miracles." Others always interpret שם המפורש as "the name set forth." Learned Drusius, in chapter 6, declares that this interpretation pleases him more than the other. And certainly the most common meaning of פרש in the Piel conjugation is "to interpret, to expound, to declare." But why is it so called? They answer that it was so called because it was expounded through the names of twelve and forty-two letters, which will be discussed in what follows. See Galatinus 2.10. I do not condemn this interpretation, but I will offer my own conjecture for the judgment of learned men. פָּרַשׁ in the Chaldee Pael commonly means "to bring forth, to pronounce, to name." What then? The name brought forth and pronounced in its own letters: [Aramaic: שְׁקְרִיאָתוֹ כְּכְתִיבָתוֹ] that is, read as it is written. This is so that the name may be distinguished by this designation from the substitute name Adonai, through whose consonants it is commonly pronounced as a substitute. So much for the widespread explanation of this name. I leave the rest aside.

units.la: XIX. Abstinebo quoque manum ab inumeris aliorum circa hoc nomen speculationibus, quas dum tractant multi, videre quidem est verborum p vάματα, solidae autem veritatis vix q μελαγμὸν. Illud tamen inter eas paululum eminet; In hoc nomine tres esse literas distinctas, יהו / quae totidem personas in adoranda Triade denotent, literam autem secundam ה secundam personam denotantem duplicari, ad indicandam duplicem Christi naturam. Sed ridiculi illi sunt, qui ex hoc nomine nomen r Ιησῦς deduxêre. ש vero insertam putant ex voce אישׁ Vir, ad incarnationem ejus denotandam, quasi Jehovam virum dicas. Nos literam y/ praecipue si vocem claudat, demi aliquando, at nunquam addi solere didicimus.
units.tr: I will also keep my hand off the countless other speculations of others about this name. While many people handle these, one sees indeed mere empty sounds of words [ψόφματα], but scarcely any solid truth [μελάγμα]. Among them, however, one stands out a little: that there are three distinct letters in this name, יהו, which denote the three persons of the adored Trinity, and that the second letter ה, which denotes the second person, is doubled to indicate the double nature of Christ. But those are ridiculous who derived from this name the name Ἰησοῦς [Iesous]. And they think the ש is inserted from the word אישׁ, "man," to denote his incarnation, as if you could call him "Jehovah the man." We have learned that the letter י is sometimes removed, especially when it closes a word, but never added.

units.la: XX. Circa hoc nomen multa quaeruntur ad forum Theologorum magis pertinentia, quae imprsesentiarum non tangam, ne objectetur mihi τὸ ὑπὲρ τὸ σκάμμα πηδᾶν, ἐν ἀπολείψ Χοῦ πίδα πήνας. Illud nostri fori esse opinor quo quaeritur, quomodo haec vox sit efferenda, sitne hodie usitata & pervulgata vox Jehova certa & germana nominis ejus, de quo agitur, lectio. Hanc controversiam ad captum juniorum hic tractare mihi decretum est. Judices depose omnes quotquot has literas amant, existimant, intelligunt. Sicubi lapsus fuero, ostendant, viam erranti comiter monstrent, lapsum erigant, non tam paratus quisquam ad monendum fuerit, quam ego ad corrigendum.
units.tr: Many questions are raised about this name that pertain more to the forum of theologians, and I will not touch them at present, lest I be charged with leaping beyond the sand-line [τὸ ὑπὲρ τὸ σκάμμα πηδᾶν] and weaving a pot from the lees of a jar [ἐν ἀπολείψ Χοῦ πίδα πήνας]. I think the question belongs to our forum: how this word is to be pronounced, and whether the word Jehova, now common and widespread, is the certain and genuine reading of the name in question. I have decided to treat this controversy here for the sake of younger readers. Let all judges depose who love these letters, think about them and understand them. If I have slipped anywhere, let them show it, kindly point out the way to the one who has gone astray, and raise up the fallen. No one will be more ready to give advice than I am to be corrected.

units.la: XXI. Sed antequam ad ipsam quaestionem accedam, tu, φιλομαθὴς Lector, patere te per diverticula quaedam non omnino, ut spero, injucunda duci, historiamque hujus paulo altius repetituro, aures paululum substringe.
units.tr: But before I come to the question itself, you, lover of learning [φιλομαθὴς], allow yourself to be led through certain digressions, which I hope are not altogether unpleasant, and lend me your ears a little while I go back somewhat further into the history of the matter.

units.la: XXII. Illud primo animo imprime, nomen hoc quia Deum ab essentia, peculiari & singulari quodam modo denominat, illudque que Deus sibi peculiariter reservatum, nec alteri communicatum voluit, apud priscos Ebraeos in majori reverentia fuisse quam reliqua Dei nomina. Hinc pio quodam studio ab ejus pronunciatione abstinebant, ne quotidiano usu vilesceret, ut solent ea quae quotidie in ore & usu sunt. Maimonides in More cap. 61.
units.tr: First, impress this on your mind: because this name designates God from his essence in a peculiar and singular way, and because God wished to reserve it for himself and not share it with another, the ancient Hebrews held it in greater reverence than the other names of God. Hence, with a certain pious zeal, they abstained from pronouncing it, lest it become cheap through daily use, as things do which are constantly in the mouth and in use. Maimonides in More, chapter 61.

units.la: [Hebrew text, Exodus-style quotation, Hebrew letters: סוף דבר נדולת זה השם והשמירה מלקרא אותו להיותו פורה על עצמו יתעלה מאשר לא ישתתף אחר מן הכרואים בהוראה ההיא]
units.tr: The sum of the matter is this: the greatness of this name and the caution against reading it come from the fact that it indicates of Himself, exalted be He, that no other created being shares in that signification [Hebrew: סוף דבר גדולת זה השם והשמירה מלקרא אותו להיותו פורה על עצמו יתעלה מאשר לא ישתתף אחר מן הנבראים בהוראה ההיא].

units.la: hoc est, Summa rei hac est, magnitudo hujus nominis & cautio ne quis illud legat hinc est, quod significet Dei exaltandi substantiam seu essentiam, & quidem ita significet, ut nulla creatura communicet cum eo in ista significatione. [Alsted. in Paratitlis Theol. p. 153. Principio tenendum est veteres Judaeos, non ex superstitione aliqua, ut hodie posteri eorum faciunt, hoc nomen vulgo proferri noluisse: sed quod primum in eo Christi mysterium agnoscerent, quatenus is tunc adhuc a tergo Abraham, ut sic dicam, cognoscebatur, Gen. 22.13. Deinde, ut indicarent ea, per quae Deus se iis revelasset, religiose potius custodienda & observanda esse, quam ut profano vulgi usui, aut humana disceptationi permitterentur. Qua sancta & castissima consuetudo si in Ecclesia N. Test. semper observata fuisset, Theologiam hodie multo simpliciorem haberemus, ambitiosaque contentionis & scandalosissimorum certaminum minus esset. Et pag. seq. Certum est; veteres Judaeos ante Christum abstinuisse a promiscua hujus nominis prolatione, non superstitione, sed religione.]
units.tr: That is, the sum of the matter is this: the greatness of this name, and the caution that no one should read it, arises from the fact that it signifies the substance or essence of the exalted God, and signifies it in such a way that no creature shares with him in that signification. [Alsted, in Paratitla Theologica, p. 153. First it must be held that the ancient Jews did not wish this name to be commonly pronounced, not from any superstition, as their descendants do today, but because they recognised in it the mystery of Christ, inasmuch as he was then still known, so to speak, from behind Abraham, Gen. 22.13. Then, so that they might indicate that those things through which God had revealed himself to them were to be kept and observed religiously, rather than given over to the profane use of the common people or to human dispute. If this holy and most chaste custom had always been observed in the Church of the New Testament, we would today have a much simpler theology, and there would be less of ambitious contention and most scandalous quarrels. And on the following page: It is certain that the ancient Jews before Christ abstained from the promiscuous pronunciation of this name, not from superstition but from religion.]

units.la: XXIII. Tantum a sacerdotibus in benedictione illa solenni, de qua Num. 6. versibus ultimis, & quidem cum illam in ipso templo recitabant, pronuntiabatur. Thalmud in Massecheth Sota, cap. 7. Misna 6.
units.tr: It was pronounced only by the priests in that solemn blessing, which is in the last verses of Numbers 6, and indeed when they recited it in the Temple itself. Talmud, Massechet Sota, ch. 7, Mishnah 6.

units.la: [Hebrew text: ברכת כהנים כיצד במדינה אומרים ... בהמקדש אותה ג' ברכות ...]
units.tr: How is the priestly blessing said? In the province they say it as three blessings, but in the Temple as one blessing. [ברכת כהנים כיצד במדינה אומרים ... בהמקדש אותה ג' ברכות ...]

units.la: hoc est, benedictio sacerdotum (N B. non dicit sacerdotis magni) quomodo se habet? In * provincia pronunciant eam tanquam tres benedictiones (Scholion, & populus respondet Amen inter singulos versus) at in templo tanquam benedictionem unam. (Schol. Ibi enim non interponit populus suum Amen) In templo pronunciat nomen (Tetragammaton) secundum scripturam ram ejus at in provincia per cognomen ejus (Scholion, per nomen Aleph daleth id est Adonai) In provincia attollunt sacerdotes manus versus humeros. At in templo, supra caput, excepto summo Pontifice, qui non attollit manus supra laminam (intelligit frontale, cui inscriptum erat קדש ליהוה Exod.28.36. Maimonides in libero Jad, halacha de Precatione & benedict. Sacerdotum cap.14.§.10. ואומר ארת השם בכתכו והוא השם הנהגה מיוד הא ויו הא וה הוא השם המפורש האמור בכל מקום ומרינרה אומרים אותו בכגוין הוא באלף דלרת שאין מזכירין ארת השם נכתבו אלא במקדש בלבר ומשמרת שמעון הצדיק פסקו הכהנים מלכרך בשם המפורש אפילו במקדש כדי שלא ילמור אותו ארם שאינו השוב ושאינו הגון ולא היו הכמים הראשונים מלמרים שם זה לתלמידים ובניהם ההגונים אלא מעם אצרת לשבע שנים כל זה גרולה לשמו הנכבר והנורא hoc est, Pronuntiat nomen tetragrammaton secundum scripturam ejus (repete ex §. praecedenti, in sanctuario, id est, in templo) atque hoc est illud nomen, quod pronuntiatur per Jod, He, Vau, He, quod Schem hammephorasch dicitur. In omni loco & provincia efferunt illud per cognomen ejus, vid. nomen Aleph Daleth, neque enim pronunciant nomen illud secundum scripturam ejus, nisi in templo tantum. At ex quo in fata concessit * Simeon Justus, a defierunt sacerdotes benedicere per nomen illud, etiam in ipso templo, vid. b ne illud disceret homo, qui non esset bona existimationis & honestus. Et prisci Sapientes non docebant discipulos suos, nisi semel tantum singulis septimanis atque hoc totum in honorem nominis honorati & reverendi.
units.tr: That is, the priestly blessing (note: it does not say of the high priest): how is it? In the province they pronounce it as three blessings (the Scholion says the people answer Amen between the individual verses), but in the Temple as one blessing (the Scholion says the people do not interpose their Amen there). In the Temple the priest pronounces the name (the Tetragrammaton) according to its writing (repeat from the preceding paragraph: in the sanctuary, that is, in the Temple), and this is the name that is pronounced with Yod, He, Vav, He, which is called the Shem ha-Meforash. In every place and province they utter it by its substitute, namely the name Aleph Daleth, for they do not pronounce that name according to its writing except in the Temple alone. But from the time Simeon the Just departed, the priests ceased to bless by the explicit name, even in the Temple itself, lest a man who is not of good repute and not honest should learn it. The ancient sages did not teach this name to their disciples and sons, except those who were suitable, and then only once in seven years. All this is in honour of his glorious and awesome name.

units.la: XXIV. Idem in More parte 1. cap. 62. quod in exemplari Latino est 61. fol. 44.
units.tr: XXIV. The same in the More, part 1, ch. 62, which in the Latin copy is ch. 61, fol. 44.

units.la: צונו בברכת כהנים ובה שם יי בכתבו אשר הוא שם המפורש ולא היה נורע אל כל אדם איך יהיה הרבור כו ובאיזה הנועה יניע כל אורת מאותיותיו או אם ידגש קצת אותיותיו אם היתה מקבלת דגשות / אבל אנשי הכמה היו מוסרים אותו זה לזה רוצה לומר תואר הדבור בו ולא היו מלמדים אותו לארם אלא לתלמיר הגון פעם אחרת כשבוע : hoc est. Mandatum accepimus de benedictione sacerdotum & cum ea de pronuntiando nomine Domini secundum scripturam ejus, atque hoc est sthem hammephorasch. Non constabat autem cuilibet homini ejus pronuntiatio, vid. qua vocali singula litera essent exprimenda, an litera aliqua esset dagessanda, hoc est, an reciperet duplicationis symbolum, &c. Sed viri sapientes tradebant filii invicem, volo dicere, modum pronuntiationis ejus. Non docebant autem ullum hominem nisi discipulum idoneum seu honestum, idque semel in septimana. Pergit Maim. ואני סובר שזה שאמרו שם בן ארבע אותיות הכמים מוסרים אותו לבניהם ולתלמידיהם פעם אחת בשבוע אין זה איך יהירו הרבור בו לבר אלא ללמר נם הנניין אשר בעבורו יוחר זה ויהיה בו סוד אלהי id est Ego autem opinor,
units.tr: We have been commanded concerning the priestly blessing, in which is the name of the Lord according to its writing, which is the explicit name, and it was not known to every man how the pronunciation goes, or with what vowel each letter is to be uttered, or whether some letter is to be doubled, if it admits the doubling mark. But the wise men handed it down from one to another, I mean the manner of its pronunciation, and they did not teach it to any man except a suitable or honest disciple, and that once a week. [מצונו בברכת כהנים ובה שם יי בכתבו אשר הוא שם המפורש ולא היה נודע אל כל אדם איך יהיה הדבור וכו' ובאיזה תנועה יגיע כל אות מאותיותיו או אם ידגש קצת אותיותיו אם היתה מקבלת דגשות / אבל אנשי החכמה היו מוסרים אותו זה לזה רוצה לומר תואר הדבור בו ולא היו מלמדים אותו לאדם אלא לתלמיד הגון פעם אחת כשבוע] That is: We were commanded in the priestly blessing, and in it the name of the Lord according to its writing, which is the explicit name; the manner of its pronunciation was not known to every man, namely with which vowel each letter is to be reached, or whether some letter is to be doubled, if it receives doubling. But the wise men handed it down to one another, I mean the form of its pronunciation, and taught it to no man except a suitable or honest disciple, and that once a week. Maimonides continues: [ואני סובר שזה שאמרו שם בן ארבע אותיות הכמים מוסרים אותו לבניהם ולתלמידיהם פעם אחת בשבוע אין זה איך יהיה הדבור בו לבד אלא ללמד גם הענין אשר בעבורו יוחד זה ויהיה בו סוד אלהי] that is, I myself think that what the sages said, that they handed down this four-lettered name to their sons and disciples once a week, is not about how the pronunciation of it alone is to be taught, but also to teach the matter on account of which this name was set apart, and in which there is a divine secret.

units.la: illud quod ajunt sapientes, istos nomen hoc quadriliterum semel qualibet septimana filiis suis discipulisve tradidisse, non sic intelligendum esse, quasi tradiderint solummodo nominis pronuntiationem, sed etiam insuper docuisse ejus significationem, propter quam hujusmodi nomen Deo esset appropriatum, qua in re divinum latitat mysterium.
units.tr: That which the sages say, that they handed down this four-lettered name to their sons or disciples once every week, is not to be understood as if they had handed down only the pronunciation of the name, but that they also taught its meaning, on account of which such a name was appropriated to God, and in which matter a divine mystery lies hidden.

units.la: XXV. Pronuntiatum ergo fuit hoc nomen in benedictione Sacerdotali usque ad Simeonem Justum, si vera narrant Thalmudistae.
units.tr: XXV. If the Thalmudists tell the truth, this name was therefore pronounced in the priestly blessing down to Simeon the Just.

units.la: Sed & illud addit Maimonides cap. 61. quod in Lat. exempl. est 60. pronuntiatum itidem fuisse a Pontifice ipso die expiationis, vid. x. die mensis Thisri. Nomen hoc non pronunciabatur, inquit אלא במקדש וכהני השם המקודשים לבר בברכת nisi in sanctuario, & quidem a sacerdotibus Dei sanctificatis tantum in benedictione Sacerdotali & a Pontifice, ipso die jejunii. Massechetb Joma sol. 39. p. 2. הנו רבנן עשר פעמים מוביר כהן גדול ארת השם בו ביום שלשה בוורוי ראשון שלשה כוורוי שני ושלשה בשיר המשתלח ואהר בגורלות hoc est,
units.tr: Maimonides adds something further, in chapter 61 (which is numbered 60 in the Latin edition), that the name was likewise pronounced by the high priest himself on the day of atonement, that is, on the tenth day of the month Tishri. This name was not pronounced, he says, [אלא במקדש וכהני השם המקודשים לבר בברכת] except in the sanctuary, and indeed only by the priests of God who had been consecrated, in the priestly blessing, and by the high priest, on the day of fasting. In the Mishnah, Yoma, folio 39, page 2: [הנו רבנן עשר פעמים מוביר כהן גדול ארת השם בו ביום שלשה בוורוי ראשון שלשה כוורוי שני ושלשה בשיר המשתלח ואהר בגורלות] that is,

units.la: Tradiderunt Magistri nostri, decies eo die memorasse Pontificem τὸ τετραγράμματον ὄνομα, ter in confessione a prima, ter in confessione b secunda, ter circa c bircum ἀπορομπαῖον, semel d in sortitione. Atque huc respexit magnus Scaliger, quando in notis ad fragmenta select. pag. 34. ita scribit, Quomodo efferendum erat, nemini licebat concipere praeterquam Pontifici maximo, idque decima Thisri & quidem ἐν ἁγίοις. Quem tamen in eo hallucinatum fuisse, quod sacerdotes reliquos ab hujus pronuntiatione excludat, ex iis quae ante dicta sunt, liquido apparet. Caeterum & ad Pontificem & ad sacerdotes reliquos respexit Philo, cum lib. 3. de vita Moßis sic inquit, χρυσᾶν δὲ πέπαλον ὡς σφαῖρα ... ὁ μόνος τῆς ὤπα καὶ γλώττων σοφία. φθία κεκαθαρμένοις ἡμῖν ἀκύειν, ἢ ἐν ἁγίοις λέγειν. Α̈ℵ̈ ἀδεὶ ᾧ Ϡ̈ἀπαᾱ ϗ̈ἀμῶ. Ubi ἐν ἁγίοις, nihil aliud est, quam Thalmudicorum בִּמְקוֹם / in sanctuario, quod totum templum complectitur.
units.tr: Our masters have handed down that on that day the high priest spoke the name, [τὸ τετραγράμματον ὄνομα], ten times: three times in the first confession, three times in the second confession, three times around the bullock, [ἀπορομπαῖον], and once at the casting of lots. It is to this that the great Scaliger refers when, in his notes on the Select Fragments, page 34, he writes: How it was to be pronounced, no one was permitted to conceive except the high priest, and that on the tenth of Tishri, and indeed [ἐν ἁγίοις]. That he was mistaken in excluding the remaining priests from its pronunciation is plain from what has been said above. Philo, however, had both the high priest and the other priests in view when, in the third book of his Life of Moses, he says: [χρυσᾶν δὲ πέπαλον ὡς σφαῖρα ... ὁ μόνος τῆς ὤπα καὶ γλώττων σοφία. φθία κεκαθαρμένοις ἡμῖν ἀκύειν, ἢ ἐν ἁγίοις λέγειν] [the golden plate like a sphere ... the wisdom of eye and tongue alone ... for us, who are purified, to hear, or to speak in the holy places]. Here [ἐν ἁγίοις] means nothing other than the Thalmudists' [בִּמְקוֹם], in the sanctuary, which takes in the whole temple.

units.la: XXVI. Ex his jam illud insuper liquere arbitror, illam priscorum ἰυλαξεία paulatim degenerasse in superstitionem, quæ ubi semel admissa fuit, altiores indies radices egit. Etenim, ut porro ejus incrementa videamus, à cujus promiscua pronuntiatione primo quidem ex quadam ἰυλαξεία, postea verò ex superstitione, sed ἰυλαξείας mantello velatâ, abstinebatur, illud postea sub poena mortis æternæ pronuntiari vetitum fuit. Præcipuè vero ejus pronuntiatione interdictum fuit plebeiis, quo respexisse autumant Eusebium, cum illud ἄλεκτον τοῖς ποσοῖς appellat.
units.tr: XXVI. From these things I think it is now further clear that that ancient reverence gradually degenerated into superstition, and once superstition was admitted, it struck deeper roots day by day. To see its further growth: at first, from some kind of reverence, and afterwards from superstition, but dressed in the cloak of reverence, people abstained from pronouncing the name indiscriminately; later it was forbidden to pronounce it on pain of eternal death. Above all, its pronunciation was forbidden to the common people. Eusebius, I think, had this in mind when he calls it [ἄλεκτον τοῖς ποσοῖς], not to be spoken by the common people.

units.la: XXVII. Si quæras super hac re expressum Thalmudicorum testimonium, ecce tibi illud ex cap. * x i. Masechet h Sanhedrin, folii 90. facie prima, ubi sic scisciunt Magistri nostri, כל ישראל יש להם חלק לעולם הבא שנאמר ועמך צדיקים ואלו שאין חלק לעולם הבא האומר אין תחיית המתים מן התורה ואין תורה משמים ואפיקורוס ריעקיבא אומר אף הקורא בספרים החיצונים ולוחש על המכה ואומר כל המחלה וג׳ אבא שאול אומר אף ההוגה את השם באותיותיו ישראלים id est Omnis Israelita habebit partem in futuro saeculo, sicuti scriptum est, Et populus tuus, &c. Jesa.60. 21. Iisti autem Israelitae non erit pars in futuro saeculo, qui dicunt non esse resurrectionem mortuorum ex Lege, qui negant Legem coelitus datam, * Epicurus. R. Akiba addit, qui legit libros profanos, qui admurmurat super plaga, recitatque ista verba, omnem ægritudinem, &c. Exod. 15. 26. Abba Saul dicit, etiam qui pronuntiat nomen literis suis.
units.tr: XXVII. If you ask for an explicit testimony of the Thalmudists on this matter, here it is, from chapter 11 of the tractate Sanhedrin, folio 90, first side, where our masters thus decide: [כל ישראל יש להם חלק לעולם הבא שנאמר ועמך צדיקים] Every Israelite has a portion in the world to come, as it is written: "Your people also shall be all righteous," Isaiah 60:21. But these are the Israelites who have no portion in the world to come: he who says that the resurrection of the dead is not from the Law, and that the Law is not from heaven, and the Epicurean. R. Akiba adds: also he who reads the outside books, and he who mutters over a wound and recites the words, "All the diseases, etc." Exodus 15:26. Abba Saul says: also he who pronounces the name according to its letters.

units.la: XXVIII. Ubi in Gemara adjecta est hæc glossa, כנבולין ובלשון ענה / id est extra Jerusalem locum illum sanctum (nam גבולים vocantur קרי חוץ למקדש inquit R. Salomo, id est urbes reliquæ præter illam inqua erat sanctuarium) & lingua barbara, vel ut alii, in sermone profano & otioso.
units.tr: XXVIII. In the Gemara a gloss is added here: [כנבולין ובלשון ענה] that is, outside Jerusalem, that holy place (for R. Solomon says that the cities other than the one in which the sanctuary stood are called "outside the sanctuary"), and in a barbarous tongue, or, as others have it, in profane and idle speech.

units.la: XXIX. Audiamus etiam Philonem, libro 3. de vita Moisis de historia Levit. 24. multa locutus sic tandem ait, Quod si quis quis non dico blasphemaverit hominum Deorumque Dominum, sed aut sui fuerit vel nomen ejus intempestive pronuntiare, noxam luat capite. Quandoquidem ne mortalium quidem parentum nomina proferunt ii qui bene cordis est pietas, sed omissis propriis honoris gratia, utuntur naturalibus, patrem appellantes matremque: atque ita profitentur accepta immensa beneficia, suamque gratitudinem. Quomodo igitur merentur veniam, qui temere abutuntur sanctissimo Dei nomine, tantum ad explendum sermonem, non aliter quam profanis vocibus.
units.tr: XXIX. Let us also hear Philo, in the third book of his Life of Moses, where he speaks at length on the history of Leviticus 24, and at last says: But if anyone should blaspheme, I do not say the Lord of men and gods, but should utter his name unseasonably, let him pay the penalty with his head. For those who have true piety do not even speak the names of their own parents, but, omitting the proper names out of honour, they use the common ones, calling them father and mother; and so they acknowledge the immense benefits they have received and their gratitude. How then can those deserve pardon who rashly abuse the most holy name of God, merely to fill out their speech, no differently than with common words?

units.la: XXX. Atque huc illa quoque pertinent, quae in eodem tractatu Sanhedrin occurrunt, cap. 7. המקלל אביו ואמו אינו היב עד שיקללם בשם קללם בכנוי מאיר רבי מאיר מהייב וחכמים פוטרים hoc est, Qui maledicit patri & matri sua, non est reus [lapiditionis, pendent enim haec ab isto paragrapho, אלו הנסקלין isti lapidantur.] nisi maledixerit illis per nomen [tetragrammaton: ] Quod si maledixerit illis per cognomen aliquod, [ex gr. Elohim, Schaddai, Adonai, &c.] R. Meir eum condemnat [ut lapidetur,] at sapientes eum absolvunt [non a peccato vel omni poena, ut vulgo haec accipiuntur, sed a lapidatione.] Ibidem, חסגדף אינו חייב עד שיפרש השם id est blasphemus non est reus [lapidationis] nisi expresserit NOMEN. Iterum κατ' ἐξοχὴν τὸ πτεϱεγγεγμμάτον innuitur. Hoc decretum superstruxerunt Magistri nostri istis verbis Levit. 24. vers. 15. & 16. quae hoc modo vulgo interpretantur, איש איש כי יקלל אלהיו ונשא חטאו id est unusquisque, ubi maledixerit Deo suo, portabit peccatum suum id est peccato congruam. זנוקב שם יהוה מות יומת בנקבו שם יומת At qui nominat, vid. inter * maledicendum, nomen DOMINI, morte morietur, — quando nominat nomen, morietur, Abenezra, ויש אומרים כי יקלל אלהיו בסתר והנכון שמלת אלהים שם התואר והמלאכים יקראו אלהים וכן הדיינים ומי יוכל לדעת מה יש בלב הקלל אך אם יפרש השם הנכבד שאינו שם התואר ולא יתערב כי הוא לברו שם עצם [ita enim locum, in posterioribus verbis corruptum, restituendum putabat eximius juvenis dignusque qui vel in celeberrima Acad. literas Graecas Ebraicasve profiteatur, JOH. COCCEIUS Bremensis, cujus ego in tanta Graecismi, Ebraismi, Rabbinismi, Thalmudismi & Theologiae peritia, insignem modestiam cum singulari pietate con-junc-
units.tr: XXX. To this also belong the things that occur in the same tractate Sanhedrin, chapter 7: [המקלל אביו ואמו אינו חייב עד שיקללם בשם קללם בכנוי מאיר רבי מאיר מחייב וחכמים פוטרים] that is, He who curses his father and mother is not liable [to stoning, for these matters depend on that paragraph, "These are the ones who are stoned"], unless he has cursed them by the name [the tetragrammaton]. But if he has cursed them by some other designation [e.g. Elohim, Shaddai, Adonai, etc.], R. Meir condemns him [to be stoned], but the sages acquit him [not of sin or of every penalty, as is commonly understood, but of stoning]. Likewise: [חסגדף אינו חייב עד שיפרש השם] The blasphemer is not liable [to stoning] unless he has expressed the NAME. Again, [κατ' ἐξοχὴν τὸ πτεϱεγγεγμμάτον] is intended. Our masters built this ruling on the words of Leviticus 24:15–16, which are commonly interpreted thus: [איש איש כי יקלל אלהיו ונשא חטאו] that is, Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin, that is, a penalty fitting to the sin. [ונוקב שם יהוה מות יומת בנקבו שם יומת] But he who names the name of the LORD, in cursing, shall surely be put to death; when he names the name, he shall die, says Abenezra. [ויש אומרים כי יקלל אלהיו בסתר והנכון שמלת אלהים שם התואר והמלאכים יקראו אלהים וכן הדיינים ומי יוכל לדעת מה יש בלב הקלל אך אם יפרש השם הנכבד שאינו שם התואר ולא יתערב כי הוא לברו שם עצם] [for the outstanding young man, worthy to teach Greek and Hebrew even in the most celebrated academy, JOHANNES COCCEIUS of Bremen, thought this passage, corrupt in its latter words, should be restored thus; in his great learning in Greek, Hebrew, rabbinic and Talmudic matters and theology, I cannot praise his notable modesty combined with singular piety as he deserves. In the printed text it reads thus, with a sense either nil or unsuitable:] Some say that those words, "Whoever curses his God," verse 15, are to be understood of one who blasphemed secretly (that is, without witnesses and prior warning, as R. Solomon likes to put it). But it is more correct that Elohim be a common noun, for angels and judges are also called Elohim. And who can know what is in the heart of the blasphemer, unless he expresses the glorious name itself, which is not a common noun, and cannot be confused, for it alone is a proper noun.

units.la: * Ita quoque Augustinus, Quaest. 87. in Leviticum. junctam non possum pro merito praedicare. In editis sic legi-tur ולא יתערב עם שם כי הוא לברו sensu aut nullo aut incommodo.] id est Sunt qui dicunt, illa verba יקלל אלהיו verf.15. de ea intelligenda esse qui clanculum (id est sine testibus & praemonitione, ut loqui amat R. Sal.) blasphemavit. Sed rectius est, ut ה' Elohim sit nomen appellativum, Namque & angeli & Judices vocantur Elohim. Et quis scire potest quid fuerit in corde blasphemi, nisi expresserit ipsum nomen gloriosum ( יהוה ) quod non est appellativum, neque confundi potest, nam illud solum est nomen proprium. Doctores in Gemara, Massecheth Sanhedrin, sol.56. sic interpretantur, Qui maledixerit Deo per nomen proprium יהוה / morte afficitur: at qui per cognomina, increpatur. Glossa, Illi incumbit כרת id est exterminium (Hiscuni, res illa pendet inter ipsum & * possessorem ejus) & quod dicitur de increpatione, dicitur ad excludendam mortem, sed non ad excludendum כרת / Ibidem illam quoque Legis restrictionem invenies, qui maledixerit nomini per nomen, ut lapidari non potuerit blasphemus עד יברך שם בשם id est nisi ipsum Deum nomine יהוה indigitatum blasphemaverit per ipsum illud יהוה / vide §. 40. Hanc glossam admodum subtiliter exsculpsere ex verbis istis, ונוקב שם בנקבו שם / Ecce inquiunt, illud requiritur שיקוב שם ut blasphemet בשם יהוה per יהוה / In Massecheth Sanhedrin cap. 9. Misna ultima, alius & ab his diversus casus proponitur, הגונב ארת הקסורת והמקלל בקופם וגי קנאין פונעין בו id est In eum qui furatur vasa ministerii (Maimonides Hal. Sanhedrin cap. 18. clarius הגונב כלי שרת מן המקרש qui furatur vasa ministerii ex Sanctuario) & qui maledicit per idolum, in eum, inquam, zelota irruunt, id est occidunt. Maimonides distinctius, Quisquis occidit talem, praeclarum & magni meriti opus patrat, (vid. instar Phineas). בית דין אין נזקקין להו domus judicii non miscet se istis. Addam obiter quae sequuntur & in Thalm. & in Maim. כהן ששמש בטומאה אין אחיו הכהנים מביאים אותו לכר אלא פרחי בהונה מוציאין אותו חוץ לעזרה ומפציעין ארת מוהו בגזירין id est sacerdotem pollutum, qui sacris operatur, Collega sacerdotes non sistunt domui judicii, sed flores sacerdotii (id est, adolescentes, candidati sacerdotii). educunt eum ex atrio & elidunt ipsi cerebrum lignis. Sed redeamus ad locum Levitici. R. Sal. qui maledixerit
units.tr: * So also Augustine, Questions 87 on Leviticus. conjoined — I cannot praise it as it deserves. The printed text reads: [ולא יתערב עם שם כי הוא לברו] which makes no sense or an unsuitable one. Those who say that the words [יקלל אלהיו] in verse 15 are to be understood of one who blasphemed in secret. Yet the Doctors in the Gemara, tractate Sanhedrin, folio 56, interpret thus: he who curses God by the proper name [יהוה] is put to death, but he who curses by a designation is only rebuked. The gloss says that [כרת], that is, exclusion, attaches to it (it is a matter hanging between himself and its owner), and what is said of rebuke is said to exclude death, but not to exclude [כרת]. In the same place you will find this further restriction of the Law: he who curses the name by a name, so that the blasphemer could not be stoned [עד יברך שם בשם], that is, unless he has blasphemed God himself, named by the name [יהוה], by that very name [יהוה]. See §40. They have worked out this gloss with great subtlety from the words [ונוקב שם בנקבו שם]. Look, they say, it is required that the name be pierced [שיקוב שם], so that he blasphemes [בשם] by [יהוה] through [יהוה]. In the last Mishnah of Sanhedrin, chapter 9, another and different case is put: [הגונב ארת הקסורת והמקלל בקופם וגי קנאין פונעין בו] that is, Against him who steals the vessels of the ministry (Maimonides, Hilchot Sanhedrin, chapter 18, more clearly: [הגונב כלי שרת מן המקרש]: who steals the vessels of the ministry from the sanctuary), and who curses by an idol, against him, I say, the zealots fall, that is, they kill him. Maimonides more distinctly: whoever kills such a man performs an excellent work of great merit (see, like Phinehas). [בית דין אין נזקקין להו] The court does not concern itself with them. I will add in passing what follows, both in the Talmud and in Maimonides: [כהן ששמש בטומאה אין אחיו הכהנים מביאים אותו לכר אלא פרחי בהונה מוציאין אותו חוץ לעזרה ומפציעין ארת מוהו בגזירין] that is, a priest who ministers while polluted is not brought by his fellow priests before the court, but the flowers of the priesthood (that is, young men, candidates for the priesthood) lead him out of the court and beat his brains out with sticks. But let us return to the passage of Leviticus. R. Solomon: whoever curses by the name itself, which is also the proper name, the Lord, his God, shall bear his sin, that is, he shall be punished at the hands of the Lord, when, as you see, no prior warning has preceded.

units.la: (Nota eum נקב שֵׁם לשון קללם id est significationem maledicendi, sicuti & Phesiktha) Deo suo etiam per nomen ipsum יהוה / portabit peccatum suum, id est punietur בַּקֵּר / quando vid. nulla antecessit praemonitio. At si praecesserit praemonitio, tunc morte morietur. Vides ut adversis frontibus inter se concurrant magistri? Theodoretus Quaest. in hunc locum ait vers. 15. nomen Dei aequivoce sumi, pro eo qui talis falso nominatur, cui quidem qui detrahit, hunc peccare asserit, nulla tamen poena condemnat. Non enim peccat qui, dum blasphemat Deum, qui falso Dei nomen usurpat; sed credit in eum & tamen convitiatur. Blasphemat enim: peccatum igitur ejusmodi blasphemiam appellavit, non propter ejus cui blasphemia infertur, dignitatem, sed propter blasphemantis opinionem. At eum, qui verum Deum blasphemat, lapidari vult. Simplicissima illa Interpretatio est, quam Cl. Junius prodidit, & supra Magistrorum vulgus caput hic extulit R. Meir, qui insuper habita communi sententia, omnem blasphemum, sive nomen sive cognomina pronunciasset, hac lege complexus est. Vide sol. 56. saepius jam citati tractatus in Gemara. Cordatior hic quoque Maimonides est, & libere à Magistris dissentit in Halacha Aboda zara, c. 2. Blasphemus non est reus, inquit, lapidationis, nisi expresserit nomen Dei proprium quatuor literarum, Aleph, Daleth, Nun, Jod, & maledixerit ei per aliquod nomen ex eorum numero, quae eradere nefas est. [ talia autem Halacha Jesode thora cap. 6. recensset 7. videl. יהוה אהיה ארני / credo eum sub tetragrammato comprehendisse ] sicut scriptum est, Et qui exprimit nomen DOMINI, &c. Ergo propter nomen proprium expressum lapidatio: propter cognomina, increpatio (אוהרה) Est autem quidam qui eam legem sic interpretatur, blasphemum non esse reum nisi expresserit nomen יהוה / At ego dico, quod propter ambo illa [ vid. יהוה & ארני lapidandus sit. Haec ille, in quibus non semel à receptis Thalmudicorum placitis diversus abit. Primo enim שם הפיוהר של ד' vocat ארני ד' אותיות / nomen, ut quidem vulgo reddunt, Deo proprium. Et certe nulli creaturae communicatur. 2. Si quis Deum blasphemans vel nomen יהוה vel ארני enuntiet, eum reum lapidationis pronuntiat, cum alii soli nomini יהוה id praerogativae tribuant. 3. Ubi alii hoc quoque requirunt, ut nomen יהוה blasphemetur per ipsum יהוה (vide & §. 40.) Maimonides statuit satis esse, si Deus sive per nomen יהוה / sive ארני denotatus, blasphemetur. phemetur per unum ex 7. illis cognominibus. Ineptus essem, si haec omnia probarem. Audebo illud tamen dicere, Maimonidem minus hic ineptum esse, quam reliqui Thalmudistæ, quorum glossæ in ipsum Deum magis injuriæ sunt. Notabis illud quoque hoc loco, isti glossæ, qua רֵבְּנ reddidit nuncupare, nominari, natales suos debere istam quorundam sententiam solam יהוה prolationem blasphemiam esse. Cui non parum roboris accessit à versione Onkeli & Lxx, quorum ille hoc verbum per Chald. פרש id est exprimere, hi per ἐπονομάζειν reddidere. Sed nec hoc termino stetit gentis istius audacia. Cum enim non omni blasphemiæ capitalem poenam destinaverint, tamen non defuisse, qui nudam יהוה pronuntiationem crimen morte expiandum censuerint, supra §.29. ex Philone ostendimus.
units.tr: (Note that he calls it נקב שֵׁם [nakav shem], that is, the sense of cursing, as also in Phesiktha.) "He shall bear his sin against his God even by the name itself," יהוה, that is, he shall be punished בַּקֵּר [baqqer] "when, that is, no warning has gone before. But if a warning has gone before, then he shall die the death." Do you see how the masters clash head-on? Theodoret, in his Questions on this passage, says on verse 15 that the name of God is taken equivocally, for the one who is falsely so called. He who detracts from this, he says, sins, yet punishes him with no penalty. For he does not sin who, while blaspheming God, falsely uses God's name, but believes in him and yet reviles him. For he blasphemes; so he called such a sin blasphemy, not on account of the dignity of the one to whom the blasphemy is directed, but on account of the opinion of the blasphemer. But he who blasphemes the true God he wants stoned. That is the simplest interpretation, which the distinguished Junius set forth. Above the common opinion of the masters, R. Meir raised his head here: setting aside the general view, he embraced under this law every blasphemer who pronounced either the name or the epithets. See sol. 56 of the tractate in the Gemara, already cited often. Maimonides here too is more judicious and freely dissents from the masters in Hilchot Avodah Zarah, ch. 2: <bl>a blasphemer</bl> <bl>is not liable</bl>, he says, <bl>to stoning</bl>, unless he has pronounced the proper four-letter name of God, Aleph, Daleth, Nun, Yod, and has cursed by one of those names which it is unlawful to erase. [Such names he lists in Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah ch. 6, no. 7, namely יהוה, אהיה, ארני. I think he included these under the Tetragrammaton.] As it is written, "And he who pronounces the name of the LORD," etc. Therefore, for the proper name pronounced, stoning; for the epithets, a warning (אוהרה). There is someone who interprets that law thus: the blasphemer is not liable unless he has expressed the name יהוה. But I say that he is to be stoned for both of those [see יהוה and ארני]. So he; and in these matters he departs more than once from the accepted opinions of the Talmudists. For first he calls the ineffable name of the Lord, ארני, a name of four letters, which, as is commonly rendered, is proper to God. And certainly it is communicated to no creature. Second, if anyone blaspheming God pronounces either the name יהוה or ארני, he declares him liable to stoning, whereas the others attribute this privilege to the name יהוה alone. Third, where the others also require that the name יהוה be blasphemed by means of יהוה itself (see also §40), Maimonides holds that it is enough if God is designated, whether by the name יהוה or ארני, and blasphemed by one of those seven epithets. I would be foolish if I tried to prove all this. Yet I will venture to say that Maimonides is less foolish here than the other Talmudists, whose glosses are more an injury to God himself. You will also note here that the gloss of those men, who rendered רֵבְּנ [ribbenu] as "to name, to be called," owes its origin to the opinion of certain people that the mere pronunciation of יהוה is blasphemy. This view gained no little strength from the version of Onkelos and the LXX; the former rendered this verb by the Chaldee פרש [parash], that is, "to express," the latter by ἐπονομάζειν [eponomazein]. But this nation's audacity did not stop at that term either. For although they did not assign capital punishment to every blasphemy, yet there were some who judged that the bare pronunciation of יהוה must be expiated by death, as we showed from Philo above in §29.

units.la: XXXI. Vides, Lector, quanto studio nomen illud venerabile occultaverit superstitiosa natio? Huic δαιμονία non multum absimilis illa est, quam * Plinius Romanis abscribit; Narrat enim eos nomen Dei, in cujus tutela erant, studiose occultasse, ne quomodo ab hostibus evocatus alio commigraret.
units.tr: XXXI. Do you see, reader, with how much zeal that venerable name was hidden by a superstitious nation? That is not very unlike the Roman practice which Pliny attributes to them. For he relates that they carefully concealed the name of the god in whose protection they were, lest, if it were known, the enemy might summon him away and he might migrate elsewhere.

units.la: XXXII. Diximus supra, ex sententia Thalmudicorum, pronuntiationem nominis יהוה in benedictione sacerdotali obtinuisse usque ad excessum Simeonis Justi. Sed & ante ejus obitum plebem ignorasse veram nominis pronuntiationem, ex Ebraeis colligi potest. Nam quid aliud sibi volunt illa verba, quae supra §.24. ex More Nebuchim & §.25. ex Philone produximus? Quomodo, inquies. Annon clara voce benedicebat Sacerdos? Ita certe. Maim. in halacha de Benedict. Sacerdotum, cap. 14. §.1. כה תברכו בקול רם id est Sic benedicetis, vid. voce alta. Sed quemadmodum in Papatu Sacerdos istas voces. Hoc enim est corpus meum, ita apud se mussat & demurmurat, nemo ut astantium distincte exaudire valeat, ita & superstitiosus in Judaismo Sacerdos hoc nomen. Masiecheth Kiddusehin cap. 4. sol. 71. אמר ר׳טרפון פעם אחת עליתי אחר אחי אמי לרוכן והטיתי אזי אצל כהן גרול ושמעתי שהכליע שם בנעימה אחיו הכהנים
units.tr: XXXII. We said above, according to the view of the Talmudists, that the pronunciation of the name יהוה was retained in the priestly blessing until the death of Simon the Just. But that even before his death the common people did not know the true pronunciation of the name may be gathered from the Hebrews. For what else do those words mean which we brought forward above in §24 from the More Nebuchim and in §25 from Philo? "How so?" you will ask. Did the priest not bless with a clear voice? Certainly he did. Maimonides, in the Halakhah on the Blessing of the Priests, ch. 14, §1: כה תברכו בקול רם [thus you shall bless with a loud voice]. But just as in Papacy the priest mutters and murmurs those words, "For this is my body," to himself, so that no one of those standing by can hear them distinctly, so too the superstitious priest in Judaism did with this name. In Masechet Kiddushin, ch. 4, fol. 71: אמר ר׳טרפון פעם אחת עליתי אחר אחי אמי לרוכן והטיתי אזי אצל כהן גדול ושמעתי שהכליע שם בנעימה אחיו הכהנים [Rabbi Tarphon said: once I went up after my mother's brother onto the platform, and I turned my ear toward the high priest, and I heard that he swallowed the name quickly, in tune, along with his brother priests].

units.la: Dixit R. Tharphon, aliquando ascendi post avunculum in suggestum, & adverti aurem ad sacerdotem magnum, & audivi quod celeriter pronuntiaret & quasi absorberet nomen (Tetragrammaton) inter modulationem sacerdotum.
units.tr: Rabbi Tarphon said: once I went up behind my maternal uncle to the platform and turned my ear toward the high priest, and I heard that he pronounced the name (the Tetragrammaton) quickly and, as it were, swallowed it, in the chanting of the priests.

units.la: XXXIII. Sed non hoc solum nomen superstitioni Judaeorum obnoxium fuit. Namque etiam circa nomen Elohim, Deo tributum, eadem occupata fuit, atque etiamnum est. Illud enim extra Biblia passim scribunt אלקים vel אלרים / Sed, ut redeamus ad tetragrammaton, Si adeo profunde demersi fuere in hoc superstitionis coeno Magistri, quid miramur miserum vulgus ita fuisse fascinatum, ut qui illud fortassis noverant, pronuntiare, qui vero ignorabant, in illud inquirere non fuerint ausi. Verissimum siquidem ab omni aevo comprobatum illud Q. Curtii fuit, Nihil efficacius regere multitudinem, quam superstitio.
units.tr: XXXIII. But this name alone was not subject to the superstition of the Jews. For they were likewise occupied with the name Elohim, ascribed to God, and still are. Indeed, outside the Bible they commonly write אלקים or אלרים. But, to return to the Tetragrammaton: if the masters were sunk so deeply in this mire of superstition, why do we wonder that the wretched common people were so bewitched that those who perhaps knew how to pronounce it did not dare to inquire into it, and those who were ignorant did not dare to inquire at all? That saying of Q. Curtius has been most truly confirmed in every age: "Nothing is more effective in ruling the crowd than superstition."

units.la: XXXIV.
units.tr: XXXIV.

units.la: Ipse Josephus, qui exusto templo & captae urbi superavit, cordatissimus alias scriptor, hac superstitione sideratus fuit. Ille, utpote sacerdos, & quidem sacerdos ἐκ τῆς παλαιᾶς Ἰουδαίας ἐπὶ ἱεροσολύμων πατέρων, veram hujus nominis pronuntiationem non potuit ignorare. Et tamen Antiquit. 2. 5. de Mose verba faciens sic inquit, καὶ ὁ Θεὸς σημαίνει αὐτῷ τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ὄνομα, ὁ οὐ πέφηνεν εἰς ἀνθρώπους παραδιδόναι, ἵνα τὸ ἱερὸν ἡμῶν ἐστιν. id est Deus illi indicat propriam suam appellationem, quam antea hominibus non innotuerat, DE QUA MIHI NON EST FAS LOQUI.
units.tr: Josephus himself, who survived the burning of the temple and the capture of the city and was otherwise a most judicious writer, was dazzled by this superstition. Being a priest, and indeed a priest by descent from the old Judaean stock of the fathers who came to Jerusalem [ἐκ τῆς παλαιᾶς Ἰουδαίας ἐπὶ ἱεροσολύμων πατέρων], he could not have been ignorant of the true pronunciation of this name. Yet in the Antiquities 2.5, speaking of Moses, he says: God reveals to him his own name, which had not previously been made known to men, and which is sacred to us [καὶ ὁ Θεὸς σημαίνει αὐτῷ τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ὄνομα, ὃ οὐ πέφηνεν εἰς ἀνθρώπους πρότερον, ἱερὸν ἡμῖν ἐστιν], OF WHICH IT IS NOT LAWFUL FOR ME TO SPEAK.

units.la: XXXV. Illud mihi jam vide, Lector, si tunc quoque, cum in templo adhuc obtinebat ejus prolatio, adeo studiose eam occultarunt Sacerdotes, qui illud sibi solis vindicabant (Glossa ad sol. 18. pag. 2. Massecheth Erubim, Nomen Tetragrammaton non est datum omni, sed tantum sacerdotibus.) si postea omnino pronuntiari, etiam in templo, defuit, si sacerdotibus, qui templo superstitarunt, religio fuit nomen illud exprimere, atque ad posteros transmittere, quis mirabitur, tandem omnino oblteratum fuisse atque animis Judaeorum evulsum.
units.tr: XXXV. Consider this, reader: if, even when its pronunciation was still in use in the temple, the priests guarded it so carefully for themselves alone (Gloss on Massechet Erubin, fol. 18, p. 2: The name Tetragrammaton is given not to everyone, but only to the priests [Nomen Tetragrammaton non est datum omni, sed tantum sacerdotibus]), and if afterwards it was utterly lost, even in the temple, and if it was a matter of scruple for the priests who survived the temple to express that name and hand it down to posterity, who will be surprised that it was at last entirely obliterated and torn from the minds of the Jews?

units.la: XXXVI. Quoniam vero Christiani in primitiva Ecclesia, linguam Ebraeam, aut res ad literaturam Ebraicam pertinentes non nisi ex Ebraeis discere potuerunt, quid miramur eos quoque genuinam certamve nominis hujus prolationem ignorasse? Neque enim discere potuerunt ex Ebraeis quod ipsi Ebraei vel ignorabant vel ut ut scirent, praepostera tamen illa religione docere prohibebantur. Hinc natae illae voces & Epitheta nominis Tetragrammati, quae passim apud patres Graecos & Latinos, nominatim vero Clementem Alex. Theodoretum, Eusebium, etc.
units.tr: XXXVI. But since Christians in the primitive Church could learn the Hebrew language, or matters pertaining to Hebrew literature, only from Hebrews, why should we be surprised that they too were ignorant of the genuine or certain pronunciation of this name? For they could not learn from the Hebrews what the Hebrews themselves either did not know or, though they knew it, were forbidden to teach through that absurd scruple. Hence those words and epithets of the name Tetragrammaton, which are found everywhere among the Greek and Latin Fathers, especially Clement of Alexandria, Theodoret, Eusebius and others,

units.la: &c. &c. obvia habes, vid. ἀνεκφώνητον, ἄῤῤητον, ἄφθεγκτον, ἐ ἀπρόῤῥητον, ἐξ ῥηθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον.
units.tr: &c. &c. You will find them everywhere; see ἀνεκφώνητον [unutterable], ἄῤῥητον [unspeakable], ἄφθεγκτον [unuttered], ἀπρόῤῥητον [not to be spoken], ἐξ ῥηθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον [that cannot be spoken].
