units.la: SIXTINI AMAMA COMMENTATIO De Keri & Chetib, AD Reverendum & Clarissimum virum, D. LVDOVICVM de DIEV Verbi divini in Ecclesia Leidensi Ministrum vigilan- tissimum & orientalium linguarum propagatorem indefessum, fratrem in Christo dilectum.
units.tr: SIXTINI AMAMA COMMENTATIO On the Keri and Chetib, to the Reverend and Distinguished man, Mr LUDOVICUS DE DIEU, most vigilant minister of the divine Word in the Church of Leiden and tireless promoter of the Oriental languages, my beloved brother in Christ.

units.la: OMnes verbi divini Ministros, ceu mysteriorum Dei dispensatores, uti par est, amo, colo, veneror. Non infitebor tamen, me singulari quodam affectu eos prosequi, qui Biblica studia colunt. Inter eos te eminere, res ipsa loquitur. Edidisti non ita pridem Syriacam paraphrasin Apocalypseos, quam tot annis literatior orbis frustra expectaverat. Accesit a te accurata ejusdem versio & doctissimarum animadversionum sylloge. Nunc vero quo magis φιλογλωσσως demereris, totus es in edenda collatione Grammatica Ebraea & Aramaea. Studia & meditationes tua circa ipsos fontes & locorum difficiliorum illustrationem versantur. Macte hoc animo, eruditissime Vir! Perpetent alii Gentilium cloacas & sterquilinia. Alii id operam dent, ut aures populi declamatorum flosculis demulceant: tu perge obscuris sacrae paginae locis facem excellentis tui ingenii allucere. Despreta in praesens iacent haec studia? Quid tum? Masculandus adversus hunc contemptum animus est. Gratior posteritas tuis meritis dignum reponent decus, famamque nominis tui, & ingenii monumenta cum laude & bonis recordationibus prosequetur. Sed in hoc argumento tuarum laudum prolixior essem, nisi tecum sermocinarer. Accipe nunc hanc commentationem, super cujus argumento iam per literas egimus. Illi tuum praescripsi nomen, ut testarer, quantum tibi deferam, & debeam. Grata fuerunt mihi litera, quas hactenus a te accepi. Et dignus essem, cujus fronti ingrati hominis character inureretur, si dissimularem, me ex iis mulmultum profecisse. At gratissima ista erunt, quarum argumentum circa hujus commentatiuncula examen occupabitur. Vale Reverende & inculpate vir. xx. Martii 1628.
units.tr: I love, cherish and revere all ministers of the divine Word, as stewards of the mysteries of God, as is fitting. I will not deny, however, that I pursue with a certain special affection those who cultivate biblical studies. That you stand out among them the thing itself declares. Not long ago you published the Syriac paraphrase of the Apocalypse, which the learned world had awaited in vain for so many years. To it you added an accurate translation and a collection of most learned remarks. Now, to deserve even better of those who love languages [φιλογλωσσως], you are wholly engaged in publishing a comparison of Hebrew and Aramaic grammar. Your studies and reflections are devoted to the sources themselves and to the elucidation of the more difficult passages. Persevere in this spirit, most learned man! Let others endure the sewers and dunghills of the Gentiles. Let others take pains to soothe the ears of the people with the flowers of declaimers; you go on kindling, with the torch of your excellent genius, the obscure places of sacred Scripture. Are these studies despised at present? What of it? The mind must be made strong against this contempt. A more grateful posterity will give your merits the honour they deserve, and will pursue the fame of your name and the monuments of your genius with praise and good remembrance. But I would be more lavish in praise of you in this matter, were I not conversing with you. Now accept this little commentary, on whose subject we have already conferred by letter. I have inscribed your name at its head, to bear witness how much I defer to you and how much I owe you. The letters I have hitherto received from you have been welcome to me, and I would deserve to have the brand of an ungrateful man set upon my forehead if I pretended that I had not profited greatly from them. But those will be most welcome whose subject is the examination of this little commentary. Farewell, reverend and blameless sir. 20 March 1628.

units.la: ANomaliæ omnes circa quas potissimum * noster versatus fuit labor, vel essentiales sunt, vel accidentales. Essentiales voco eas, quæ in ipsis vocibus consistentes causam non habent aliam, quam usum, penes quem, ut aliis linguis, ita & in hac, dum stetit Resp. Judaica, — arbitrium fuit & vis & norma loquendi. Licet enim tam verba quam res amanuensibus suis Spiritus S. dictârit, attemperavit tamen se & cujusque Amanuensis stylo, & cujusque sæculi dialecto. Unde alius est Jesaiæ, alius Amosi stylus. Alia Mosis, alia Jobi, alia Davidis, alia Ezræ, Haggæi, Danielis, &c. dialectus.
units.tr: All the anomalies with which our labour was chiefly concerned are either essential or accidental. I call essential those which, residing in the words themselves, have no other cause than usage, by whose judgement, as in other languages, so also in this one, while the Jewish commonwealth stood, lay the authority, the force and the rule of speaking. For although the Holy Spirit dictated both the words and the things to his amanuenses, he nevertheless adapted himself both to the style of each amanuensis and to the dialect of each age. Hence the style of Isaiah is one thing, that of Amos another; the dialect of Moses is one thing, that of Job, of David, of Ezra, of Haggai, of Daniel, and so on, another.

units.la: II. Anomaliæ istæ, ut jam * ante à nobis dictum est, sunt vel communes, vel propriæ. Communes vocavi eas, quæ regulis aliquatenus comprehendi possunt & in Grammaticâ nostrâ, suis quæque locis, exhibitæ sunt. Proprias dixi, quæ uni certæ radici vocive propriæ sunt, &c.
units.tr: II. These anomalies, as has already been said by us, are either common or proper. I have called those common which can be comprehended to some extent by rules, and which have been set out in our Grammar, each in its own place. I have called proper those which belong to one particular root or word alone, and so on.

units.la: III. Accidentales voco, quæ in vocis peculiari scripturæ consistunt. Suntque duûm generum. Aliæ enim ob Mysterium aliquod, uti quidem Ebræis placet, aliæ ob diversam lectionem irregulariter scribuntur.
units.tr: III. I call accidental those which consist in the peculiar writing of a word. There are two kinds. For some are written irregularly on account of some mystery, as the Hebrews are pleased to hold, and others on account of a different reading.

units.la: IV. Mysterii alicujus causâ, ex Ebr. sententia, litera aliqua vocis vel quantitate majori pingitur in Editionibus accuratioribus, quam reliquæ, ut e. gr. Deut. 6. 4. vel minori, ut Gen. 23. 2. atque istarum literarum totum Alphabethum à Maforethis recensetur & ex iis cl. Buxt. in Tiberiade cap. 14. & 15. Commentarii. Nos vero eas præcipuè * annotavimus, quæ in hodiernis codicibus sic scriptæ tiamnum reperiuntur Vel litera aliqua invertitur, ut Num. 10. 35. vel suspenditur supra alias. ut Jud. 18. 30. vel figurâ finali in medio pingitur ut Jesa. 9. 7. vel initiali in fine, ut Nehem. 2. 13. vel denique supernè punctis extra ordinem insignitur, ut Genes. 19. 33, & 33. 4. quæ omnia à nobis suis quæque locis in Coronide nostra ad Grammaticam indicata sunt.
units.tr: IV. For the sake of some mystery, according to the opinion of the Hebrews, a certain letter of a word is marked in the more accurate editions either with a larger size than the rest, as for example Deut. 6. 4., or with a smaller one, as Gen. 23. 2.; and the whole alphabet of these letters is listed by the Masoretes, and from them the learned Buxtorf in his Tiberias, chapters 14 and 15 of the commentary. We, however, have chiefly noted those which are still found written in this way in present-day manuscripts: either a letter is inverted, as Num. 10. 35.; or it is suspended above the others, as Judg. 18. 30.; or a final letter is marked in the middle, as Isa. 9. 7.; or an initial letter at the end, as Neh. 2. 13.; or finally it is marked above with points out of order, as Gen. 19. 33 and 33. 4. All of these we have indicated in their proper places in our Coronis to the Grammar.

units.la: V. Quæ vero ob lectionis diversitatem irregulariter scribuntur, vulgò 848. numerantur. Ex illis nos eas potissimum annotavitavimus, quæ Grammaticam ullo modo turbant. In illis autem hoc observandum est, punctationem illam, quæ voci intra textum positæ addita est, nullo modo ei convenire ex naturâ & ingenio linguæ Ebrææ, sed contrà in plerisque ab ea plane abhorrere; illi vero voci examussim convenire, quæ in margine cum litera ף notata est. Atque ita in textu duplex lectio insinuatur, una per consonantes, quarum proprias vocales ex analogia Grammatica supplebis, atque hæc vocatur כְּתִיב scriptum, scriptura, denotaturque per circulum voci tali superinpositum; Altera per vocales, non quidem istius vocis, cui subjiciuntur, sed ejus quæ in margine sine vocalibus posita est cum litera ק / quæ significat קְרֵי Keri, legitur, Ex.gr. 2. Sam. 14. 22. עָבְרוּ si legas gnaudera, erit monstrum vocis. Insinuatur hîc duplex lectio, una per consonas, quæ ex anal. Gramm. sic punctandæ, עֲבֵרוּ servum suum, altera per vocales, quæ propriæ sunt voci in margine positæ עַבְדְּךָ servi tui. Quamvis aliquando per accidens fiat, ut in diversa lectione nulla sit punctorum varietas, ut videre est Prov. 4. 3. & 22. 3 Jer.49.30. Jezech. 42. 16. &c.
units.tr: V. Those words, however, which are written irregularly on account of a difference of reading, are commonly numbered at 848. From these we have noted chiefly those which in any way disturb the Grammar. In these cases it must be observed that the pointing which has been added to the word within the text does not in any way agree with the nature and genius of the Hebrew language, but on the contrary in most cases stands plainly apart from it; whereas that which is marked in the margin with the letter ף agrees exactly with the word. Thus a double reading is suggested in the text: one by the consonants, whose proper vowels you will supply from the analogy of the grammar, and this is called Kethib [כְּתִיב], written, scripture, and is indicated by a small circle placed over the word; the other by vowels, not indeed of that word to which they are attached, but of the one placed in the margin without vowels with the letter ק, which signifies Keri [קְרֵי], read. For example, 2 Sam. 14. 22: עָבְרוּ, if you read it gnaudera, it will be a monstrous word. Here a double reading is suggested: one by the consonants, which according to the analogy of the grammar are to be pointed thus, עֲבֵרוּ, his servant [servum suum]; the other by the vowels, which are proper to the word placed in the margin, עַבְדְּךָ, your servant [servi tui]. Although sometimes it happens by chance that there is no variety of points in the different reading, as may be seen at Prov. 4. 3. and 22. 3, Jer. 49. 30, Ezek. 42. 16, and so on.

units.la: VI. Hanc autem lectionis varietatem in quibusdam peperit Judæorum quædam ἐναλάγαα & religio, in quibusdam vero codicum discrepantia & mendosa descriptio.
units.tr: VI. This variety of reading, however, has been produced in some cases by a certain ἐναλλαγή [enallage] and scruple of the Jews, and in others by the discrepancy of manuscripts and faulty copying.

units.la: VII. Religione Judæorum & metu profanationis factum est, inquit cl. Erpenius, ut nomen tetragrammaton יהוה protulerint per nomen אֲדֹנָי / vel (quoties vel ante vel post se habuit ipsum nomen אֲדֹנָי) nomen אֱלֹהִים / unde etiam istarum vocum puncta nomini (יְהוָה) addita sunt, moneretur lector, nomen illud per consonas proprias istarum vocalium legendas esse.
units.tr: VII. Through the religious scruple of the Jews and fear of profanation, as the learned Erpenius observes, it came about that they pronounced the tetragrammaton יהוה [YHWH] by the name אֲדֹנָי [Adonai], or (whenever the name itself stood either before or after אֲדֹנָי) by the name אֱלֹהִים [Elohim]; whence also the points of these vowels were added to the name (יְהוָה), so that the reader would be warned that that name is to be read by the consonants with the proper vowels of these words.

units.la: VIII. Religione quoque factum est, & vitandæ turpitudinis ergò, ut literis vocum quarundam obscœniorum vocales honestiorum adjectæ sint, ut 2. Reg. 18. 27. Jes. 37. 12. quamvis & ex aliquando eadem sint, ut Deut. 28. 30.
units.tr: VIII. It was also done out of religious reverence, and for the sake of avoiding indecency, that the more decorous vowels were added to the letters of certain obscene words, as at 2 Kings 18. 27 and Isa. 37. 12, although sometimes the same vowels are found, as at Deut. 28. 30.

units.la: IX. Reliquæ variæ lectiones (si excipias נַעַר & יְרוּשָׁלַם) ex mendosa codicum descriptione & varietate natæ sunt. Cui ut remedium adhiberent viri eruditi, voces in contextum diu receptas, prout eas invenerunt, reliquerunt integras, sed emendationem earum in margine posuerunt nudis consonis, quarum vocales consonis in contextu positis addidere.
units.tr: IX. The remaining variant readings (except נַעַר [naʿar] and יְרוּשָׁלַם [Yerushalayim]) arose from faulty copying of manuscripts and from variety. To remedy this, learned men left the words which had long been received into the text entire, just as they had found them, but placed the emendation of them in the margin with bare consonants, to which they added vowels, the consonants being placed in the text.

units.la: X. Restitutio illa lectionis versatur vel circa voces integras, vel circa vocum partes, vid. consonas.
units.tr: X. That restoration of the reading concerns either whole words or parts of words, namely the consonants.

units.la: Circa voces integras versatur quadrupliciter 1. Aliquando enim dictio integra in contextu redundat, quam proinde puncfis non vestivere, ut Jerem. 51. 3. Tales autem voces redundantes à Masorethis numerantur. 8 2. Aliquando vox integra deficit, ac tunc in contextu solas vocales ponunt in codicibus punctatis, consonis in margine exhibitis. In codicibus autem non punctatis spacium relinquunt vacuum, Ruth. 3. 17. & aliis locis. 3. Aliquando una in duas finditur. 4 Aliquando contrà duæ in unam coalescunt. Exempla vide Gen. 30.
units.tr: It concerns whole words in four ways. (1) Sometimes a whole word is superfluous in the text, and the pointers therefore did not clothe it with vowels, as at Jer. 51.3. The Masorites count such superfluous words. (2) Sometimes a whole word is missing. In pointed manuscripts they then place only the vowels in the text and show the consonants in the margin. In unpointed manuscripts they leave an empty space, as at Ruth 3.17 and in other places. (3) Sometimes one word is split into two. (4) Sometimes, conversely, two words merge into one. See the examples at Gen. 30.

units.la: XI. Circa vocum partes, id est, consonas versatur 5. modis.
units.tr: XI. As to parts of words, that is, the consonants, it concerns five ways.

units.la: 1. vel enim consona una pro alia posita est,
units.tr: (1) Either one consonant is put in place of another,

units.la: 2. vel redundat.
units.tr: (2) or a consonant is superfluous,

units.la: 3. vel deficit,
units.tr: (3) or a consonant is missing,

units.la: 4. vel transponitur,
units.tr: (4) or a consonant is transposed,

units.la: 5. vel à voce sua avulsa alteri adjungitur.
units.tr: (5) or a consonant is torn away from its own word and attached to another.

units.la: Quod ad 1. modum attinet, is vel ex vicinitate pronuntiationis, vel similitudine figuræ natus est. Præ cæteris autem literæ אהוי frequenter confusæ reperiuntur, vid. א pro י/ ut לא non, pro לי ei, ה pro ut שפכה pro כי & pro י/ לר pro לי / pro י ut לא pro לא non, & pro ה ut היו pro הירה / Jod pro ה/ ut כי / pro כרה sic. At omnium sæpissime Jod & Vau confunduntur, quia maximam figuræ habent affinitatem, אנני pro ני / הוא pro היא & contra הוא pro חיא /
units.tr: As to the first way, this arises either from closeness of pronunciation or from similarity of shape. Above all, the letters א ה ו י are frequently found confused: א for י, as [לא] "not" for [לי] "to me"; ה for ח, and י for ה, as [כי] for [כה] "thus"; and the most frequent confusion of all is between י and ו, because they have the greatest affinity in shape, as [אנני] for [אני] "I", and [הוא] "he" for [היא] "she", and conversely [הוא] for [חיא].

units.la: XII. Reliquarum permutationes rationes sunt, occurrit enim
units.tr: XII. The permutations of the other letters have their own reasons. There occurs:

units.la: ב pro ך semel. ם 6. כ 11. פ 1. ח 1. ש pro ו 2. ד pro ך 2. ו 1. ה pro כ 2. ג 1. ח 2. ו pro ך 1. ה pro y 1. ח 1. ג pro ג 1. כ pro ה 1. ך 1. ם 1. מ pro ב 1. ה 2. ז pro ח 1. ם 1. ט pro ה 1. ע pro א 5. ץ 1. ם pro ב 1. מ 1. ר pro ך 4. ש pro ם 1. pro ך 1.

units.la: XIII. Quod ad 2. & 3. modum attinet, eandem literæ אהוי longè sæpius redundant & deficiunt quam aliæ...
units.tr: XIII. As to the second and third ways, the letters א ה ו י are far more often superfluous and missing than the others.

units.la: א enim medio vocis redundat 45. locis, ut ינאין[?]/ Reliquæ initio medio & fine, ה 33. locis, יעשרה[?] / כהשרה[?] / הניירת[?] / ו 95. locis, ויוציאו[?] / כתוב[?] / ויאמרו[?] / 147. יצאו[?] / דבריך[?] / עשיתי[?] /
units.tr: א is superfluous in the middle of a word in 45 places, as [ינאין?]. Of the others, ה (initial, medial and final) is superfluous in 33 places, as [יעשרה?], [כהשרה?], [הניירת?]; ו in 95 places, as [ויוציאו?], [כתוב?], [ויאמרו?]; and [יצאו] and [דבריך] and [עשיתי] in 147 places.

units.la: Ex reliquis redundant tantùm לש semel, כפת bis, ג ter, ב quater, ער quinquies.
units.tr: Of the remaining letters, only [לש] is superfluous, once; [כפת] twice; [ג] three times; [ב] four times; and [ער] five times.

units.la: XIV. Deficiunt quoque literæ הוי in principio, medio & fine, satis frequenter, Et quidem.
units.tr: XIV. The letters ה ו י are also quite frequently missing at the beginning, in the middle and at the end. Indeed:

units.la: ה 44. locis, אִבְּכֶר / לָגִיר / פִּלֶד /
units.tr: ה is missing in 44 places, as [אִבְּכֶר], [לָגִיר], [פִּלֶד].

units.la: י 30. locis, אָמֵר / אַחַשְׁוֵרֹשׁ / לְדוֹר דּוֹר /
units.tr: י is missing in 30 places, as [אָמֵר], [אַחַשְׁוֵרֹשׁ], [לְדוֹר דּוֹר].

units.tr: In very many places, as [עֲבוֹר], [מְרָנִים], [בְּנִיִּת]; and in countless places at the end of plural nouns, the ' and ךְ are attached before [מִשְׁפָּטֵה], [רְבָּנוּ], although doubt may be raised about these.
