units.la: Aben Ezrae commentarius super loco Gen. xvii. 14. Variae Ebraeorum sententiae de supplicio quod Chereth id est, exterminium vocant. Iunii, Deodati, Mercerii & aliorum sententia, poenam capitalem non denotari. Aliorum opinio, poenam capitalem significari. Eorum ratio. Quid ad eam respondeant Ebraei. Quid sit התראר apud Thalmudicos. De examine restium apud Ebraeos usitato. Vbi twice simpliciter nominatur, strangulationem; ubi sanguis super eum, lapidationem intelligunt Ebraei. De die circumcisionis. Eum ex lege fuisse octavum, etiam si in Sabbathum incideret. Aliquando in 9. 10. 11. & 12. incidisse. Istius traditionis fundamentum. Circumcisio impellit Sabbathum si incidat in tempus suum. Non item si loco suo jam mota sit, aut si sit dubitatio. Quid sit, dies legalis non est a tempore ad tempus. Alia.
units.tr: Aben Ezra's commentary on Gen. 17:14. The various opinions of the Hebrews on the punishment called karet, that is, extermination. The opinion of Junius, Deodatus, Mercerus and others, that a capital punishment is not meant. The opinion of others, that a capital punishment is signified. Their reasoning, and how the Hebrews answer it. What hitcharet means among the Talmudists. On the examination by cords in use among the Hebrews. Where "twice" is named simply, they understand strangulation; where "blood upon him," stoning. On the day of circumcision: that by law it was the eighth day, even if it fell on the Sabbath. That at times it fell on the ninth, tenth, eleventh or twelfth day. The foundation of this tradition. Circumcision overrides the Sabbath if it falls on its proper time, but not if it has already been moved from its place, or if there is doubt. What is meant by "a legal day is not from time to time." Other matters.

units.la: Verba AbenEzrae ad verf. 14. cap. xvii. Genef. ista sunt, יסול יפעוק למו כי ידור נדר / והוא מן ונמלתם את בשר ערלתכם וטעמו אם היה כר מצוה ולא יסול את בשר ערלתו יש עליו כרת כי מצות הנער קטון על האב ואם אביו לא מלהו יסול עצמו בהיותו ברשותו וכרת בידי שמים / והטועים יהשבו כי אם מרת הנער ולא נסול אין לו חלק לעולם הבא, ואין הנפש כרצונם כי נפש כמו איש וטעמו גיף שיש לו נפש וכן נפש כי תחטא וי״א כי כרת המרת קורם גב שנרה וי״א כי כרת שיכרת שמו במות זרעו / על כן אמר הכתוב מעמידה כי מי שיש לו בנים כאלו הוא היו ושמו / לא נברת id est, יניחמו est forma jiphgnol, (id est futurum Kal) instar, chi jiddor, dor neder, ubi voverit votum, &c, estque ejusdem conjugationis cum ונמלחם & circumcidetis carnem praeputii vestri Gen. 17. 11. & sensus est, si fuerit filius praecepti (id est, jam xiii. annum supergressus, quae aetas singulis Judaeis Legis Mosaicae jugum imponit) & non circumciderit carnem praeputii sui, ei incumbit כרת id est, exterminium. At praeceptum quod ad parvulum spectat, patri incumbit. Quod si ergo pater eum non circumciderit, ipse se circumcidet, ubi jam sui juris est. Chereth autem, ab ipso Deo (Ebr. coelo) infligitur. Errant qui existimant, puerum sine circumcisione ex hac vita discedentem non habituram partem in futuro seculo. At vox נפש anima, non significat id quod illi volunt. Nam נפש hic idem est quod איש / & significat corpus, in quo est anima, ut, anima cum peccaverit, Levit. 4. 2. Et sunt qui dicunt, per Chereth intelligi, cum quis moritur ante annum Lii. Alii, cum alicujus nomen exscinditur extincta posteritate. Ideo dicit Scriptura, מעמיר ex populis suis. Nam qui filios reliquit, est ac si viveret, & nomen ejus non exscinditur. Haec Aben. Moses Maimon. Halacha de poenit. cap. 8. exponit in hunc modum, יכרת ברשעו ואבר כבהמה והו כרת / hoc est, exscindetur ob impietatem suam & peribit ut bestia. Atque hoc intelligitur per illud Chereth, quod extat in lege, quando dicitur, & excindendo excindetur anima, &c. Addit, ex traditione habet, illud הכרת exscindendo, ad saeculum praesens: תכרת exscindetur, ad futurum seculum pertinere. Equidem non ignoro, quomodo hic sudent interpretes, ut lectoribus persuadeant, Maimonidem Αμωνλω impiarum animarum non negare: Sed & illud scio, vocem illam כבהמה sicut bestia a Maimonide, si ita sensit uti interpretes eum sensisse volunt, non fuisse adhibendam. Moses Kotsensis in libro praeceptorum magno, quem כמנ id est, ספר מצוות vocant, sol. 35. columna. 3. ait כרת esse cum quis ex hac vita discedit inter L. & Lx. annum. Et paulo post ex alterius sententia, מת קורם ששים זהו מיתת כרת id est, qui moritur ante LX. annum, ille moritur morte Chereth. Ibidem distinguit inter Chereth & ערירי id est, eum qui ἄπεν & illiberis moritur. R. Salomo utrumque conjungit, dum illa verba, exscindetur anima, ita Interpretatur, הולך עירירי ומת קורם ומנו id est, abibit ex hac vita sine liberis & morietur ante tempus suum. Respexere, opinor, ad Levit. 20. verf. 20. & 21 verf. 20. עיריים morientur, verf.
units.tr: The words of Aben Ezra on verse 14 of Genesis 17 are these: [Hebrew text] and their sense is this: if he is a son of the commandment (that is, one who has already passed his thirteenth year, the age at which the yoke of the Mosaic Law is laid on every Jew) and does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin, then karet, that is, extermination, rests upon him. But the commandment concerning the little child falls on the father. If therefore the father has not circumcised him, he shall circumcise himself, once he is his own master. Karet, however, is inflicted by God himself (in Hebrew, heaven). Those are mistaken who think that a boy who departs this life without circumcision will have no part in the world to come. The word nefesh [נפש] ("soul") does not mean what they want it to mean. For nefesh here is the same as ish [איש, "man"], and it signifies the body in which the soul is, as in "if a soul sins," Lev. 4:2. Some say that karet means that a man dies before the age of fifty. Others say it means that a person's name is cut off when his posterity is extinct. Therefore Scripture says "from his people," for one who has left sons is as if he were alive, and his name is not cut off. Thus Aben Ezra. Moses Maimonides, in Hilkhot Teshuvah, ch. 8, explains it in this way: he shall be cut off for his wickedness and perish like a beast [Hebrew]; this is karet. And he adds that this is what is meant by the expression karet in the Law, where it is said, "in being cut off he shall be cut off, his soul," and so on. He adds that by tradition the words "he shall be cut off" (hikkaret) refer to the present age, while "he shall be cut off" (tikkaret) refers to the age to come. I am not unaware of how these interpreters sweat to persuade their readers that Maimonides does not deny the immortality of impious souls. But I also know that the phrase "like a beast" should not have been used by Maimonides, if he thought as the interpreters want him to have thought. Moses Kotsensis, in his great book of precepts, which they call the Sefer Mitzvot, folio 35, column 3, says that karet is when a man departs this life between his fiftieth and sixtieth year. And a little later, on the opinion of another, "he who dies before sixty, that is the death of karet." In the same place he distinguishes between karet and ariri, that is, one who dies childless and without offspring. R. Solomon joins both together, interpreting the words "his soul shall be cut off" thus: [Hebrew] that is, he shall go from this life without children and shall die before his time. I think they had in view Lev. 20:20 and 21, where the verse 20 reads "they shall die childless" (ariri).

units.la: עריִם erunt, quæ subtilius distinguit R. Salomo in hunc modum, Si habet liberos, sepelient eos. Si non habet, morietur illiberis. Hæc duo distinguit duobus istis textibus, Sine liberis morientur. Si habent liberos tempore transgressionis, orbi erunt quando morientur, nam sepelient eos, iisque supervivent. Sine liberis erunt, Si non habent liberos tempore transgressionis, manebunt reliquo vita sine liberis, &c. Ebraei ergo hanc poenam soli Deo relinquunt. Cl. Junius, licet ab his diversus abeat, non agnoscit tamen capitale supplicium. Hoc enim ad Gen. 17. 14. ejus scholion est, hic & in suturo sæculo à sanctorum consortio excludetur. Deodatus, sicuti ego non habebo eum pro membro mei populi, ita etiam excommunicetur ex Ecclesia. Ita & Genev. Atque hi omnes ubicunque eadem phrasis recurrit, Lectorem suum ad hujus loci annotationem ablegant. Eadem quoque sententia placuit Mercero, Luthero, Calvino & aliis. Sunt tamen qui capitale supplicium à Magistratu infligendum ea phrasi denotari existimant. Cui opinioni præsidia quærunt ex ejusmodi locis, ubi uni eidemque flagitio & mors & כרת decernitur. Ex. gr. Exod. 31. verf. 14. Levit. 20. confer verf. 6. & ult. verum ad hæc loca respondent Ebraei, distinguendo inter flagitia manifestaria & occulta. Namque quod ad locum Exod. 31. 14. attinet, sic ait Maimon. cap. 1. Tract. de Sabbatho §. 2. מהו הייב על עשייה מלאכה אם עשה ברצונו בזדון הייב כרתי ואם היו עם עריִם והתראה נסקל ואם בשוגגתם חייב קרבן חטאת קבוערה hoc est, Quid est cum dicimus aliquem reum esse ob factum opus [in Sabbatho?] Si fecit volens in superbia, reus est exterminii. Si sint testes & pramonitio, lapidatur. Si ex errore, tenebitur offerre oblationem ordinarii sacrificii pro isthoc peccato. Eadem invenies in comm. R. Salomonis. Idem Rabbi Salomo ad verf. ult. cap. 20. Levit. כאן נאמר כהם מיתרי ילמעלרה כרת עדים והתראה בסקילה מיד בלא התראה בכרת ושגגתם חטאה וכן בכל הייבי מיתות שבאמר בהם כרת Hic, inquit, decernitur illis mors: at supra (verf. 6.) exterminium. Si testes sint & præcesserit pramonitio, lapidatio obtinebat. Si sciens volensque hoc delictum patrabat, non antegressa pramonitione, locum habebat exterminium. Si per errorem, sacrificio peccatum expiabat. Atque ita se res habet cum omnibus reis mortis, de quibus usurpatur illud כרת. In quibus verbis observa vocem בהתרַאה à noà nobis redditam prænmonitio. Est enim ab Hiphil הַתְרָה / præmonere, protestari. Quia vero doctissimus quidam vir vocem eam solet reddere, evidentem probationem, operæ erit locum unum atque alterum nostro interpretamento firmando adducere. Sic ergo legitur in Misna tractatu Sanhedrin, cap. 5. ubi agitur de examine testium in judiciis capitalibus, היו בודקים אותם בשבע חקירות באיזו שבוע באיזו שנה באיזו חרש בכסה בחרש באיזה יום באיזו שעה באיזה מקום / ר' יוסי אומר באיזה יום באיזו שעה באיזה מקום / סכירים אתם אותו התריהם כו hoc est Probant eos (testes) septem investigationibus, qua septimana (Glossa, באיזה שבוע של יובל qua septimana Jubilæi id est, ut loquitur Moses Kotzensis, præcepto affirm. 109. באיזו שמטה qua hebdomade annali, quales septem inter singulos Jubilæos interfluebant) quo anno, quo mense, quoto die mensis, qua feria septimana, qua hora, quo loco. R. Iose dicit, quo die, qua hora, quo loco (Rogant testes,) an nostis eum, an præmonuistis eum, &c. Maim. in Halacha Sanhedr. cap. 12. postquam posteriora illa retulisset, hæc adjicit אחד תלמיד חכם אחד עם הארץ צריך התראה שלא נתנה התראה אלא להבחין בין שוגג למויד שמא שוגג הוא id est, sive aliquis sit discipulus Sapientis, (id est Sapiens, quomodo olim sapientes se Philosophos appellarunt) sive Idiota, opus est ut fiat ei talis præmonitio. Namque ea non alium in finem instituta est, quam ut discerni posset inter eum qui ex errore peccat, & eum qui sciens, volens & quasi elata manu peccat. Et addit וכיצר מתרין בו אומרים לו פרוש או אל תעשה שזו עבירה היא והייב את עליה מיתת ב' או מלקות hoc est, quomodo præmonent eum? dicunt ei, separa te ab isto, aut ne facias, nam transgressio est, & reus eris mortis infligenda à domo judicii aut flagellationis, &c. Qua de re quid sentiam, alias, Deo volente, dicam. Ego certe istius rei præsidium nullum in divinis literis hactenus investigare potui. Et quod ad pleraque flagitia attinet, ex. gr. pulsationem parentum, homicidium, Sodomiam, concubitum cum matre vel filia, annon ipsa natura & conscientia (ut de Lege morali quæ omnib. Judæis nota erat, nihil dicam) illis instar sonori præmonitoris erat? Sed redeamus ad כרת / Thalmudici in Massecheth Cheritut. 36. flagitia recensent, quorum patratores in hanc pœnam incurrant. Observant, omnia illa peccata committi adversus præcepta negativa, gativa, exceptis duobus, quibus affirmativa violantur, quorum alterum de circumcisione Gen. 17. 14. alterum de Paschate agit, Exod. 12. 15. His autem lubet adjicere alium insuper locum ex Maimonide, in Halacha אסורי ביאה id est de illicito concubitu, cap. 1. Quisquis elata manu se polluit illicita concubitu, ex eorum genere, de quibus in Lege agitur, reus est exterminii. Quod si ex errore peccet, expiet peccatum sacrificio ad hoc destinato. Sunt autem quaedam species עריות nuditatum, id est, incestuosi concubitus, quae capite luuntur ex sententia domus judicii, יחר על הכרת שהוא שוה בכלם praeter exterminium, quod in omnibus pariter obtinet. Omnes qui illicitis libidinibus se polluunt, talibus vid. quae supplicio capitali ex decreto judicum vindicantur, si fuerint testes; & pramonitio praecesserit, & illi tamen patrent, afficiuntur isto supplicio, quod singulis destinatum est. Etiamsi transgressor fuerit discipulus sapientis, nec morte nec verberibus multatur, nisi praecesserit admonitio; Quippe ea introducta est, ut distinguetur inter peccantem elata manu & peccantem ex ignorantia. (Quid est libidinibus laxare fibulam si hoc non est?) Inter illicitas mixtiones, queis capitalia supplicia decreta sunt, quaedam strangulatione expiantur. Qui lapidibus obruuntur, isti sunt, 1. Qui rem habet cum matre. 2. cum noverca. 3. uxore filii sui. 4. masculo. 5. bestia. 6. Foemina quae admittit bestiam. Isti sunt qui comburuntur: Qui cot cum filia uxoris, dum ipsa adhuc superstes est, cum filia filia ejus, cum filia filii ejus, cum matre uxoris & matre matris ejus: cum matre patris ejus, cum filia sua, cum filia filia sua, & filia filii sui. At concubitus cum alterius conjuge strangulatione punitur. S. S. E. morte morietur adulter & adultera Lev. 20. 10. Et nota per mortem absolute & simpliciter memoratam intelligi strangulationem. (Ea enim levissima poena censebatur inter capitales. Homicidia tamen, de quibus eadem phrasis usurpatur, Exod. 21. 12. gladio puniverre, & tam ex Joh. 8. verf. 4, 5. quam Ezech. 16. verf. 40. & 38. collatis liquet, adulterium olim lapidatione fuisse expiatum) Si fuerit filia Sacerdotis, illa comburitur, stuprator vero strangulatur. Si puella desponsata, in utrumque lapidatione animadvertitur. Et ubicunque reperitur, morte morietur, sanguis ejus super eum, lapidatio intelligitur. Caeteri concubitus solo exterminio puniuntur, neque in illis obtinet capitalis poena. Quod si tamen testes sint & pramonitio, judices flagellant eum, Nam omnes rei exterminii (isto casu) flagris caduntur. Haec Maim. Si autem quaeras quinam sint isti concubitus, queis incumbit כרת / accipe eos a Mose Kotzensi.
units.tr: erunt (עריִם, that is, childless). R. Salomo distinguishes this more finely, in this way: If he has children, they will bury them. If he has none, he will die childless. He distinguishes these two by the two texts, "They shall die childless." If they have children at the time of the transgression, they will be bereaved when they die, for they will bury them and outlive them. "They shall be childless": if they have no children at the time of the transgression, they will remain without children for the rest of their life, etc. The Hebrews therefore leave this punishment to God alone. The distinguished Junius, although he departs from them, does not acknowledge capital punishment. For in his scholion on Gen. 17:14 he says: here, and in the future age, he will be excluded from the fellowship of the saints. Deodatus: just as I will not count him a member of my people, so he is to be excommunicated from the Church. So too the Geneva Bible. All of these, wherever the same phrase recurs, send their reader to the annotation on this passage. The same opinion has pleased Mercerus, Luther, Calvin and others. Yet there are some who think that capital punishment to be inflicted by the magistrate is signified by that phrase. For this view they seek support from passages where both death and כרת [karet] are decreed for one and the same crime, for example Exod. 31:14 and Lev. 20, compare vers. 6 and the last verse. But the Hebrews answer these passages by distinguishing between manifest and hidden crimes. For as regards Exod. 31:14, Maimonides says in ch. 1 of the tractate on the Sabbath, §2: What does it mean when we say that someone is guilty on account of doing work [on the Sabbath]? If he did it willingly, in arrogance, he is liable to exterminium (כרת). If there are witnesses and a prior warning, he is stoned. If it was done in error, he is bound to offer the sin offering of ordinary sacrifice for that sin. [מהו החייב על עשיית מלאכה אם עשה ברצונו בזדון חייב כרת ואם היו עדים והתראה נסקל ואם בשוגג חייב קרבן חטאת קבועה] You will find the same in the commentary of R. Salomo. The same R. Salomo, on the last verse of Lev. 20, says: Here, he says, death is decreed for them; but above (vers. 6) exterminium. If there were witnesses and a prior warning, lapidation was in force. If he committed this offence knowingly and willingly, without a previous warning, exterminium took place. If through error, the sin was expiated by sacrifice. And so it is with all the capital offenders about whom כרת is used. In these words observe that the word בהתראה (with warning), which we render prænmonitio, comes from the Hiphil הַתְרָה, to warn, to protest. Since a certain very learned man is accustomed to render that word as evident proof, it will be worth adducing one or two passages to confirm our interpretation. Thus it is read in the Mishnah, tractate Sanhedrin, ch. 5, where the examination of witnesses in capital trials is discussed: They examine them by seven inquiries: in which week (Gloss: in which week of the Jubilee, that is, as Moses Kotzensis puts it, in precept 109, in which annual week, of the seven that flowed between each Jubilee), in which year, in which month, on which day of the month, on which day of the week, at which hour, in which place. R. Iose says: on what day, at what hour, in what place (the witnesses are asked) whether you know him, whether you warned him, etc. Maimonides, in Halacha Sanhedrin ch. 12, after reporting these latter points, adds: whether he is a disciple of the Wise (that is, a sage, as the philosophers of old called themselves sages) or an ignorant man, a warning must be given to him. For such a warning was instituted for no other purpose than that a distinction might be made between one who sins through error and one who sins knowingly, willingly and with a high hand; perhaps he sinned in error. And he adds: how do they warn him? They say to him: separate yourself from that, or do not do it, for it is a transgression, and you are guilty of death to be inflicted by the court, or of flogging, etc. What I think about this matter I will say elsewhere, God willing. Certainly I have so far been unable to find any support for this in the divine writings. And as for most of the crimes, for example the striking of parents, homicide, sodomy, intercourse with a mother or a daughter, was not nature itself and conscience (not to mention the moral law, which was known to all Jews) like a loud-sounding warner to them? But let us return to כרת. The Talmudists in Massechet Cheritut 36 list the crimes whose perpetrators incur this penalty. They observe that all those sins are committed against negative precepts, except two, by which affirmative precepts are violated: one of these concerns circumcision, Gen. 17:14, the other concerns the Passover, Exod. 12:15. To these I wish to add another passage from Maimonides, in the Halacha on forbidden intercourse, ch. 1: Whoever with a high hand defiles himself by illicit intercourse, of the kind spoken of in the Law, is liable to exterminium. If he sins in error, he expiates the sin with the sacrifice appointed for this. There are certain kinds of nakedness (עריות), that is, incestuous intercourse, which are punished by death by sentence of the court, in addition to the exterminium, which applies equally to all. All who defile themselves with forbidden lusts, that is, those who are avenged by capital punishment by the decree of judges, if there were witnesses and a warning preceded, and yet they commit the offence, are subjected to that punishment which is appointed for each. Even if the transgressor is a disciple of the wise, he is punished neither by death nor by flogging, unless a warning has preceded; for it was introduced so that a distinction might be made between one who sins with a high hand and one who sins through ignorance. (What is it to loosen the bridle to lusts, if this is not?) Among the forbidden mixtures for which capital punishments are decreed, some are expiated by strangulation. Those who are overwhelmed with stones are these: 1. he who has intercourse with his mother; 2. with his stepmother; 3. with his son's wife; 4. with a male; 5. with a beast; 6. a woman who admits a beast. These are the ones who are burned: he who has intercourse with the daughter of his wife, while she is still alive, with the daughter of her daughter, with the daughter of her son, with the mother of his wife and the mother of her mother, with the mother of his father, with his own daughter, with the daughter of his daughter and the daughter of his son. But intercourse with another's wife is punished by strangulation. "They shall surely die, the adulterer and the adulteress," Lev. 20:10. And note that by death, mentioned absolutely and simply, strangulation is to be understood. (For that was considered the lightest penalty among capital ones. Homicides, however, to which the same phrase is applied, Exod. 21:12, were punished by the sword; and it is clear from John 8:4-5 as well as Ezek. 16:40 and 38 taken together that adultery was formerly expiated by stoning.) If she is the daughter of a priest, she is burned, but the seducer is strangled. If the girl is betrothed, both are punished by stoning. And wherever it is found, "he shall surely die, his blood shall be upon him," stoning is meant. Other intercourse is punished only by exterminium, and in those cases capital punishment does not apply. But if there were witnesses and a warning, the judges flog him; for all who are liable to exterminium (in that case) are beaten with the lash. Thus Maimonides. But if you ask what those intercourses are upon which כרת rests, take them from Moses Kotzensis.

units.la: vide Kim-chiam hoc fatentem Qui rem habet cum sorore patris, matris, uxoris, cum uxore fratris sui, & cum menstruata.
units.tr: See Kimchi admitting this: He who has to do with his father's sister, his mother's, his wife's, with his brother's wife, and with a menstruating woman.

units.la: Hæc ex magna testimoniorum sylva libuit accongerere, ut intelligeres, quid Ebræi de hac phrasi תכרת נפשו sentiant. De quare integer extat tractatus in Thalmud, titulo כריתות / Ego in sententia Cl. Junii, Deodati, & Genev. acquiesco, quæ in eo cum Ebraeorum conspirat, quod eam à pœna capitali à Judicibus infligenda distinguat. Loquor de ista phrasi exscindetur anima ejus, juvant hanc sententiam ista quoque loca, ubi Deus expresse sibi hanc pœnam reservat, Levit. 17. 10. Levit. 20. 6. Ego exscindam ilam animam, &c. Nuspiam vero legitur, Tu exscindes ilam animam, sicuti Ex. 22. Tu maleficam non sines vivere, quibus verbis Magistratum alloquitur Deus. Rursus dico, me loqui de ista phrasi, exscindetur anima ista è populo, vel, exscindetur iste è medio populi. Nam quominus hæc extendi possint ad omne נכרת quod in sacris occurrit, si non alius, vel unicus ille locus, Dan. 9. 26. Post. 62. septimanas יכרת המשיח / impediat. Porro de suppliciis istis, quæ in superioribus memoravimus, prolixius, cum bono Deo, alibi dicemus.
units.tr: I have chosen to gather these from a large forest of testimonies, so that you may understand what the Hebrews think of the phrase תכרת נפשו [tikkarēt nafšô]. There is an entire tractate in the Talmud on this subject, under the title כריתות [Keritot]. I agree with the view of the distinguished Junius, Diodati and the Geneva [annotators], which agrees with that of the Hebrews in that it distinguishes this penalty from the capital punishment to be inflicted by judges. I am speaking of that phrase, that soul shall be cut off. These passages also support this view, where God expressly reserves this penalty to himself: Lev. 17:10; Lev. 20:6, I will cut off that soul, etc. Nowhere is it read, You shall cut off that soul, as in Ex. 22, You shall not let a sorceress live*, words with which God addresses the magistrate. Again I say that I am speaking of that phrase, that soul shall be cut off from its people, or that one shall be cut off from the midst of the people. For nothing prevents these from being extended to every niphal of כרת [kārat] that occurs in the sacred books, unless that one place, Dan. 9:26, After sixty-two weeks the Messiah shall be cut off יכרת המשיח [yikkarēt hammāšîaḥ], stands in the way. Further, concerning those punishments which we mentioned above, we shall speak at more length elsewhere, God willing.

units.la: Verbum addam de die circumcisionis, quem octavum Deus esse voluit; etiamsi in Sabbathum incideret. Et quidem hoc sic satis rigide observatum à Judæis est. Namque etiam tempore Christi (Joh. 7. 22.) ipso Sabbatho, si in illud dies à natali octavus inciderct, hæc sacra peragebant. Et etiam illud dictitant מילה דוחה את השבת id est, circumcisio pellit Sabbathum id est, veneratio Sabbathi non impedit circumcisionem. Repertum tamen ab ipsis ἐπίταγμα est, quod suæ ab hac lege secessioni oppandant. Audi decretum Thalmudicum Massechet Sabbath cap. 19. in Misna, קטן נימול לשמתה לתשעה י׳ א ולשנים עשר לא פחות לא יותר / הא כיצד כרכו לשמנה / נולד לבין שמשות נימול לתשעה / בין שמשות של ערב שבת נמול לעשתה / יום טוב לאחר השבת נמול לאחר עשר / שני ימים של ראש השנה נמול לשנים עשר
units.tr: I will add a word about the day of circumcision, which God wished to be the eighth, even if it fell on the Sabbath. And indeed the Jews have observed this quite rigidly. For even in Christ's time (John 7:22) they performed this rite on the Sabbath itself, if the eighth day from birth fell on it. They also repeat the saying מילה דוחה את השבת [mîlâ dôḥâ et haššabbāt], that is, circumcision overrides the Sabbath, i.e., reverence for the Sabbath does not hinder circumcision. Yet they have devised an ordinance (ἐπίταγμα) by which they cover their departure from this law. Hear the Talmudic decree in Massechet Shabbat, ch. 19, in the Mishnah: קטן נמול לשמונה לתשעה לעשרה לאחד עשר ולשנים עשר לא פחות לא יותר הא כיצד כרכו לשמונה נולד בין השמשות נמול לתשעה בין השמשות של ערב שבת נמול לעשרה יום טוב לאחר השבת נמול לאחד עשר שני ימים של ראש השנה נמול לשנים עשר

units.la: hoc est, Infans circumciditur die octavo, 9. 10. & 12. non antea, non postea. Quomodo? ordinarie die octavo. Si natus sit inter Soles, (id est in crepusculo vespertino) circumciditur die nono, Si in crepusculo vespera Sabbathi, circumciditur die decimo. Quod si dies ille qui Sabbathum excipit, sit festus, circumciditur die undecimo. Quod si duo dies in principio anni Sabbatum excipiant, in duodecimum differtur circumcisio. Fundamenta, quibus hæc traditio nititur, refert Maimon. in comment. ad hanc Misnam. Qui nascitur, inquit, inter soles, dubium est utrum die an nocte nascatur. Et quia circumcisio non poterat administrari noctu, (Maimon. in Halacha Mila cap. 1. §. 8. Non circumcidunt
units.tr: That is: an infant is circumcised on the eighth day, or the ninth, tenth and twelfth, not earlier, not later. How so? Ordinarily on the eighth day. If he was born between the suns (that is, at evening twilight), he is circumcised on the ninth day. If he was born at evening twilight of the Sabbath eve, he is circumcised on the tenth day. If the day that follows the Sabbath is a festival, he is circumcised on the eleventh day. If two days at the beginning of the year follow the Sabbath, circumcision is deferred to the twelfth day. Maimonides, in his commentary on this Mishnah, gives the grounds on which this tradition rests. He who is born, he says, between the suns is in doubt whether he was born by day or by night. And since circumcision could not be performed by night (Maimonides, in Halacha Mila, ch. 1, §8, They do not circumcise

units.la: unquam אלא ביום אחר עלות השמש שנאמר ביום השמיני ולא בלילה nisi de die, orto jam sole, sicuti scriptum est, * die octavo, non nocte. Ideo differunt hujus infantis circumcisionem in diem sequentem qui à natali nonus est. E. gr. nascitur Rubeni filius die Mercurii in crepusculo vespertino, non circumciditur die Mercurii sequentis septimanæ, sed die Jovis. Nascitur Rubeni filius die veneris in crepusculo vespertino, nec die veneris, nec die Saturni circumcidunt, sed differunt circumcisionem in primum septimanæ [ita loquitur Maimonides] id est, diem Solis, à natali decimum. Atqui, inquies, antea dictum, circumcisionem pellere Sabbathum. Audi distinctionem. Ibidem §. 9. מילה בזמנה דוחה את השבת ושלא
units.tr: never אלא ביום אחר עלות השמש שנאמר ביום השמיני ולא בלילה but only by day, after sunrise, as it is written, "on the eighth day," and not by night. So they defer the circumcision of this infant to the following day, which is the ninth from birth. For example, if Reuben's son is born on Wednesday at evening twilight, he is not circumcised on the Wednesday of the following week, but on Thursday. If Reuben's son is born on Friday at evening twilight, they circumcise him neither on Friday nor on Saturday, but defer the circumcision to the first day of the week [so Maimonides], that is, Sunday, the tenth from birth. But, you will say, it was said before that circumcision overrides the Sabbath. Hear the distinction. In the same place, §9: מילה בזמנה דוחה את השבת ושלא

units.la: בזמנה אינה דוחה את השבת ולא את יום טוב id est, circumcisio quae fit tempore suo (id est die 8.) pellit Sabbathum, atque jam mota est suo loco, nec pellit Sabbathum nec diem festum, id est, cogitur & Sabbatho & diei festo cedere. Et paulo post, non pellunt Sabbathum ob dubium, hoc est si dubium sit, an tempus nativitatis in vespera Sabbathi, diei an. nocti annumerandum sit. At si tempus extra dubitationis aleam positum esset, alia erat ratio. AbenEzra ad Lev. 12. 3. Die octavo circumcidetur, אםרו הל ביום ולא בלילה והנה הנולד הצי שעה
units.tr: בזמנה אינה דוחה את השבת ולא את יום טוב That is, circumcision performed at its proper time (that is, on the eighth day) overrides the Sabbath; but if it is not performed at its proper time, it does not override the Sabbath or a festival day. In other words, it must yield to both the Sabbath and the festival day. And a little later: they do not override the Sabbath when there is doubt, that is, if it is uncertain whether the time of birth in the evening before the Sabbath should be counted to the day or to the night. But if the time were placed beyond the hazard of doubt, the reasoning was different. Abenezra on Lev. 12:3, On the eighth day he shall be circumcised, אמרו חכמים ביום ולא בלילה [ʾāmərû ḥakhāmîm bayyôm welō' balāylâ],

units.la: קודם שקיערת החמה יהיה נימיל לשמה ימים והציוום כי יום התורה אינו מעת לעת id est, Dicunt Sapientes nostri p. m. die, & non nocte [sc. administrabitur circumcisio] Quod si infans nascatur dimidia hora ante solem occasum, (ecce tempus, quod extra dubium diei annumerabatur) circumcidetur post sex dies & dimidium. [Etiam Sabbatho] nam dies Legalis non est a tempore ad tempus. Hoc est, dies Legalis non accipitur stricte pro die 24. aut 12. horarum, ita vid. ut tum demum dicatur completus, cum eadem diei hora recurrit. Nota, Lector, particulam illam diei natalis, semihorium, synecdochice pro toto die à Magistris sumi, (eodem plane modo, quo reliquum diei Veneris, quo mundi Salvator expiravit, integer dies censetur.) Si ergo iste dies synecdochicus ad 6. integros adjiadjiciatur, jam in diem octavum incidit circumcisio. Atque ita AbenEzram in concordiam redigó cum Thalmudicis. Sed quid hoc inquies, post dies 6. & dimidium? Pone, Rubeni natum filium die Sabbathi, dimidia hora ante occasum Solem, adjice ad illum diem sex sequentes, an ergo circumcidetur infans die octavo, qui rursus incidit in Sabbathum, post meridem, elapso vid. jam dimidio diei? Certe omne illud tempus quod ortu & occasu Solis concludebatur, erat legitimum. Maimon. in Halach. Mila, cap. 1. §. 8. מל משעלה עמוד השחר כשר וכל היום כשר למילה ואף על פי כן מצוה להקדים בתחלת היום שזריזין מקדימים למצוה
units.tr: והנה הנולד בין השמשות [wehinnēh hannôlād bēn haššimšôt]. That is, "Our sages say by day and not by night" [namely, that circumcision is to be performed]. If an infant is born half an hour before sunset (behold, a time which was reckoned beyond doubt as belonging to the day), he shall be circumcised after six and a half days, even on the Sabbath, for the legal day is not from time to time. That is, the legal day is not taken strictly as a day of twenty-four or twelve hours; it is thus considered complete only when the same hour of the day returns. Note, reader, that the masters take that particle of the day of birth, the half hour, synecdochically for the whole day, in exactly the same way as the rest of Friday, on which the Saviour of the world expired, is counted as a whole day. If, therefore, that synecdochic day is added to six full days, circumcision falls on the eighth day. And so I bring Abenezra into agreement with the Talmudists. But what, you will say, about "after six and a half days"? Suppose Reuben's son is born on the Sabbath, half an hour before sunset; add to that day the six that follow. Will the infant then be circumcised on the eighth day, which again falls on the Sabbath, after noon, when half the day has already passed? Certainly all that time which was bounded by sunrise and sunset was lawful. Maimonides, in Halacha Mila, ch. 1, §8: מל משעלה עמוד השחר כשר וכל היום כשר למילה ואף על פי כן מצוה להקדים בתחלת היום שזריזין מקדימים למצוה

units.la: id est, qui circumcidit post ortam columnam aurorae, rite facit: nam totus dies est idoneus circumcisioni; nihilominus tamen jubemur ante capere hoc opus in principio diei. Nam expediti antevertunt praeceptum id est, non in ultimam horam rejiciunt, ut solent ignavi & lentuli. Non audeo tamen asserere, AbenEzram hic adversari vetustae consuetudini, quae etiamnum durat, (Buxt. in Synag. Jud. pag. 81. Vulgo tamen tempore matutino, quando jejunus adhuc est, circumcidi consuevit.) Quid ergo? Puto eum per dimidium diem intelligere noctem, primam diei naturalis seu ἡμερονυκτίου particulam. Sed hoc à me dissertum, non assertum. Scio enim AbenEzram à Thalmudicorum scitis non semel recedere.
units.tr: That is, he who circumcises after the column of dawn has risen acts rightly, for the whole day is fit for circumcision; nevertheless we are bidden to undertake this work at the beginning of the day. For the diligent anticipate the precept, that is, they do not put it off to the last hour, as lazy and slow people are wont to do. Yet I do not dare to assert that Abenezra here opposes the ancient custom, which still persists (Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, p. 81: commonly, however, circumcision has been customary in the morning, when the infant is still fasting). What then? I think he understands by "half the day" the night, the first part of the natural day, or nychthemeron. But this I offer as a matter for discussion, not as an assertion. For I know that Abenezra departs from the opinions of the Talmudists more than once.

units.la: Habes, Lector, compendium eorum, quae de tempore circumcisionis Ebraei notarunt & etiamnum observant. Habes simul in hoc [& habebis postea plura] evidentissimum exemplum istius praevaricationis, quam ipsis objectat Salvator, Marc. 7. Sane belle aboletis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem vestram servetis.
units.tr: You have, reader, a summary of what the Hebrews have observed about the time of circumcision and still observe. You also have here, and will have more later, a most evident example of that transgression with which the Saviour charges them, Mark 7: Full well do you set aside the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.

units.la: AD LOCUM Psalm. 1. verf. 5. Pio, & πολυίστορι Iuveni-Viro, D. IOHANNI COCCE- IO, meo in Thalmudicis studiis consecraneo, S. P.
units.tr: TO THE PASSAGE ON Psalm 1, verse 5. To the pious and learned young man, Mr. JOHANN COCCEIUS, my fellow student in Talmudic studies, greetings.

units.la: ON ignoras, eruditissime Cocceje, aliquando anxie inter nos quaesitum fuisse de germano sensu verborum Kimchii, qua ad verf. 5. primi Psalmi commentatus est. Occæcaverat nos tot doctorum prejudicium, qui Kimchii verba in eam sententiam citare consueverunt, tanquam si Αγμουλω impiarum animarum, postquam ex corporibus suis exivere, negitasset. Videbamus periodum unam atque alteram huc aurigari. At cum universum locum expenderemus, multas difficultates recepta sententia intercedere cognovimus. Quae super ea nuper in chartam conjeci, ad te affero, qui ex divite tuo penu nonnulla quoque huc contulisti, & suspenso gradu ambulantem firmasti tuo judicio, cui quantum deferam, supra pag. 307. testatum feci. Vale doctissime Cocceje & diurna bono Ecclesia & Reip. literaria; quae in te magnum & incomparabile columen aliquando habitura est.
units.tr: You will not be unaware, most learned Cocceius, that among us there was once an anxious inquiry into the true sense of the words of Kimchi, in his commentary on verse 5 of the first Psalm. The prejudice of so many learned men, who are accustomed to cite Kimchi's words to this effect, had blinded us, as if he had denied that the souls of the impious continue to exist after they have left their bodies [Αγμουλω]. We saw one or two sentences being dragged in this direction. But when we weighed the whole passage, we found that many difficulties stood against the accepted interpretation. I now send you what I have lately committed to paper on this subject. You have added some points from your rich store, and by your judgment you have steadied a man who walks with hesitant steps. How much I defer to that judgment I have already declared on p. 307. Farewell, most learned Cocceius, and may the Church and the republic of letters long enjoy you, who will one day be a great and incomparable pillar of both.

units.la: Promisimus pag. 445. nos ostensuros, Kimchium vocem יקומו quae verf. 5. Psal. 1. occurrit, accepisse in significatione subsistendi, prout in foro oppohitur ר׳ cadere. Commentatio ista Kimchiana ita vulgo intellecta fuit, ac si impiorum animas post hanc vitam superesse negaret. Et nos isti sententiae haesisse non infitemur. Nunc cur aliter sentiamus, facile ostendemus, ubi ipsa Kimchii verba praemiserimus. Sic ergo inquit, על כן הרשעים הולכים בדרך רע בעולם הזה לא יקומו במשפט רוצה לומר ביום הדין והוא יום המיתה לא תהיה להם תקומה. והטאים גם כן והוא הדין ללצים לא תהיה להם בערת צדיקים כי הצדיקים במותם תהיה להם תקומה. וכן אבל הרשעים לא תהיה להם תקומה אלא תאבד נפשם עם גופם ביום המיתה] ואמר כעדת צדיקים / כי כשימורת הצדיק / ונפשו עם נפשות הצדיקים מתענגת עם כבוד אל בעולם העליון
units.tr: On p. 445 we promised to show that Kimchi understood the word יקומו, which occurs in verse 5 of Psalm 1, in the sense of "to subsist", as opposed to "to fall" in a forensic setting. This Kimchian comment has commonly been understood as if he denied that the souls of the impious survive this life, and we do not deny that we once held that view. Why we now think otherwise will be easily shown once we have set out Kimchi's own words. He says: "Therefore the wicked who walk in an evil way in this world will not arise in judgment, that is, on the day of judgment, which is the day of death; there will be no תקומה for them. Sinners likewise, and the same judgment applies to scoffers: there will be no תקומה for them in the assembly of the righteous, since the righteous at their death will have a תקומה. But as for the wicked, there will be no תקומה for them; rather their soul will perish together with their body on the day of death." He says "in the assembly of the righteous" because, when the righteous man dies, his soul rejoices with the souls of the righteous in the glory of God in the upper world. [על כן הרשעים הולכים בדרך רע בעולם הזה לא יקומו במשפט רוצה לומר ביום הדין והוא יום המיתה לא תהיה להם תקומה. והטאים גם כן והוא הדין ללצים לא תהיה להם בערת צדיקים כי הצדיקים במותם תהיה להם תקומה. וכן אבל הרשעים לא תהיה להם תקומה אלא תאבד נפשם עם גופם ביום המיתה] ואמר כעדת צדיקים / כי כשימורת הצדיק / ונפשו עם נפשות הצדיקים מתענגת עם כבוד אל בעולם העליון

units.la: Verba illa, quæ uncinulis istis inclusa vitæ, exhibendæ sententiæ Kimchianæ vulgo citari solent, quæ certe seorsim accepta extendere videntur. Ita enim Latine reddunt, sed improbos quod attinet, illis non erit resurrectio: sed peribit anima ipsorum cum corpore ipsorum in die mortis. At si locum integrum, quem nos exhibuimus, expendas, videbis per תקומה neutiquam intelligi posse resurrectionem. Quod ut appareat, vertam totum Latine, voces illas יקומו & תקומה integras relicturus. Ideo improbi, qui ambulant in via mala in hoc mundo, non יקומו in judicio, vult dicere, in die judicii, hoc est, in die mortis [Nota, an in die mortis locum habet resurrectio? Vides ergo illud יקומו non posse exponi resurgent, non erit ipsis תקומה / [nec hoc potest reddi resurrectio.] 2. Et peccatores similiter. Et idem judicium erit irrisorum Non erit ipsis תקומה in cœtu justorum. nam justis, cum moriuntur, erit תקומה / 3. Sed improbos quod attinet, illis non erit תקומה / sed peribit anima ipsorum cum corpore ipsorum in die mortis. 4. Et dicit, in cœtu justorum. Quando enim moritur justus, anima ejus cum justorum animis delitiatur cum divina gloria in superiori mundo. Ex his evidenter apparet, תקומה non usurpatum fuisse Kimchio, pro resurrectione, quam תְּהִיָּה vocare solent. Ideo opinabamur תקומה Kimchio idem esse quod השארות הנפש / seu ἀλγμοvή τῆς ψυχῆς, ut hoc dicat §. 1. non superstites erunt in die judicii, hoc vult dicere, in die judicii, hoc est in die mortis non erit ipsis ἀλγμονή sed annihilabuntur eorum anima. Firmabat nos in hac sententia locus Amos. 7. 2. Quis יקום stabit Jacobo? id est superstitabit, superstes manebit, & Jos. 2. 10. & non קמה stetit amplius spiritus in viro. Chald. אשתאברת / διαμένει, permansit. Accedebat & authoritas Corn. Betrami, quem in additionibus ad thesaurum Pagnini, th. קום videbamus hoc eodem modo Kimchium interpretatum fuisse. Pagninus enim locum illum non intellexit. Movebat nos denique locus ad Ps. cIv. 30. ואם תהיה תהיית המתים לכל אדם: זה מהלקרת בין הכמינו ורוב כויגיית התלמוד / היא כי תחיית המתים לצדיקים ולא לרשעים id est an omnium mortuorum futura sit resurrectio, contravertitur inter sapientes nostros. At stylus seu cursus thalmudicus hucfere inclinat, quod resurrectio tantum futura cura sit justorum, non vero improborum. Sed ipse Kimchi aliis in locis ita se explicat, ut dubitari nemo possit, quin animarum impiarum post hanc vitam ἀγνοοῦν agnoverit. Ecce enim comm. in hunc ipsum Psalmum, ad verf. ultimum, Deus novit viam justorum, sic inquit, dicit, quod Dominus exaltandus congreget animas justorum ad se & novit eas & curam earum gerit, ut benefaciat illis & ut satiet illos bonis suis & scientia sua & providentia sua, quod est magnum bonum & magna retributio, sicuti dictum est 1. Sam. 25. Eritque anima domini mei ligata in fasciculo viventium cum Domino Deo tuo. Et via improborum peribit. Quia cum moriuntur, non erit ipsis תקוסה sicuti dicit, וילכו לאבדון & peribunt animae ipsorum, & ibunt in locum perditionis. Videamus & commentarium ejus ad 1. Sam. 25.
units.tr: The words enclosed in these brackets, which are usually quoted to present Kimchi's sense, seem to bear that meaning when taken alone. For they render in Latin: "but as for the wicked, there will be no resurrection, but their soul will perish with their body on the day of death." But if you weigh the whole passage we have given, you will see that תקומה cannot be understood as "resurrection" at all. To make this plain, I shall translate the whole into Latin, leaving the words יקומו and תקומה untranslated. "Therefore the wicked, who walk in an evil way in this world, will not יקומו in judgment, that is, in the day of judgment, which is the day of death. [Note: does resurrection take place on the day of death?] You see, then, that יקומו cannot be rendered 'they will rise', nor can 'there will be no תקומה for them' be rendered 'there will be no resurrection'. 2. Sinners likewise. The same judgment applies to scoffers. There will be no תקומה for them in the assembly of the righteous, for the righteous, when they die, will have a תקומה. 3. But as for the wicked, they will have no תקומה; rather their soul will perish with their body on the day of death. 4. And he says: in the assembly of the righteous. For when the righteous man dies, his soul delights with the souls of the righteous in the glory of God in the upper world." From this it is clearly evident that Kimchi did not use תקומה for resurrection, which they usually call תחיה. So we supposed that for Kimchi תקומה is the same as the survival of the soul, or ἀλγμονή of the soul, so that his meaning is: "they will not survive on the day of judgment, that is, on the day of death; there will be no ἀλγμονή for them, but their souls will be annihilated." We were confirmed in this view by Amos 7:2, "Who shall יקום (stand) for Jacob?", that is, who shall survive, who shall remain alive; and Josh. 2:10, "no more קמה (stood) spirit in man." The Chaldee has אשתאברת, διαμένει, "remained." The authority of Cornelius Bertram also supported us; in his additions to Pagninus's thesaurus, under the root קום, we saw that he had interpreted Kimchi in this same way. For Pagninus did not understand that passage. Finally, a passage on Ps. 104:30 moved us: "And if there will be a resurrection of the dead for every man, this is disputed among our wise men and in most of the Talmud: whether the resurrection will be for the righteous only and not for the wicked." That is, whether there will be a resurrection of all the dead is disputed among our sages. But the style and course of the Talmud incline to the view that resurrection will be only for the righteous and not for the wicked. Yet Kimchi himself explains himself in other places in such a way that no one can doubt that he recognised the continued existence of the souls of the impious after this life. See his commentary on this same Psalm, at the last verse: "God knows the way of the righteous." He says: "that is, the Lord, who is to be exalted, will gather the souls of the righteous to himself, and he knows them and takes care of them, so that he may do good to them and satisfy them with his goods, with his knowledge and with his providence, which is a great good and a great reward, as it is said in 1 Sam. 25: 'And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God.' But the way of the wicked will perish, because when they die there will be no תקומה for them, as it says, וילכו לאבדון, and their souls will perish and go into the place of destruction." Let us also look at his commentary on 1 Sam. 25.

units.la: 29. Eritque anima Domini mei in fasciculo viventium, cum Domino Deo tuo, & animam hostium tuorum ejaculabitur e medio cavo funda. Ad haec verba ita commentatur, שלא יוכלו להמיתך מי שרודפין אותך והידה בהיים ארת השם כלומר שתלך בורכיו כל יסיך וכן ורעה לא תמצא בך כל יסיך וימירת האל יתעלרת ויתברך הרגרפים אותך
units.tr: 29. "And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God, and the souls of your enemies he shall sling out, as from the hollow of a sling." On these words he comments thus: "that those who pursue you may not be able to kill you, and that you may walk in the life of the LORD, that is, that you walk in his ways all your days; and so: and evil will not be found in you all your days. The God who is exalted and blessed will destroy those who pursue you." [שלא יוכלו להמיתך מי שרודפין אותך והידה בהיים ארת השם כלומר שתלך בורכיו כל יסיך וכן ורעה לא תמצא בך כל יסיך וימירת האל יתעלרת ויתברך הרגרפים אותך]

units.la: ne possint te occidere quicunque persequuntur te, & ut sis in vita cum Domino, q. d. ut ambules in viis ejus omnibus diebus tuis, & sic, Et malum non invenietur in te omnibus diebus tuis (infra verf. 28.) & interficiet Deus exaltandus & benedictus eos qui persequuntur te. ויפריח נפשם כמו אבן הקלע וכף הקלע פירוי מושב אבן הקלע שהוא עשוי כמו כף ולדעת יונתן פירוי נפש ארני צרורדה בצרור החיים לעולם הבא שתרגם הפסוק כן ותהא נפשא דרבוני גניזה בגנז היי עלמא קדם יי אלהך ויה נפש בעלי,
units.tr: "That they may not be able to kill you, whoever pursue you, and that you may be in life with the LORD, that is, that you may walk in his ways all your days; and so: and evil will not be found in you all your days (see below, verse 28), and God, who is exalted and blessed, will destroy those who pursue you." [ויפריח נפשם כמו אבן הקלע וכף הקלע פירוי מושב אבן הקלע שהוא עשוי כמו כף ולדעת יונתן פירוי נפש ארני צרורדה בצרור החיים לעולם הבא שתרגם הפסוק כן ותהא נפשא דרבוני גניזה בגנז היי עלמא קדם יי אלהך ויה נפש בעלי] He will hurl their soul like the stone of a sling. By "the hollow of the sling" is meant the seat of the sling-stone, which is made like a palm. And according to Jonathan's interpretation, "the soul of my lord shall be bound" means that it shall be bound in the bundle of life in the world to come. He renders the verse thus: "and the soul of my lord shall be hidden in the treasury of the world of life before the LORD your God, and the soul of your enemies he shall hurl away." [ויפריח נפשם כמו אבן הקלע]

units.la: & projiciet animam eorum, sicut lapidem funda, per הקלע intelligitur sedes lapidis funda, quae facta est instar volae. Et juxta sententiam Jonathani haec est loci interpretatio, anima domini mei ligata erit in fasciculo viventium in futuro seculo, nam in hunc modum vertit locum, Eritque anima domini mei repositam in thesauro seu repositorio vitae aeternae coram Domino Deo tuo, & animam adversariorum tuorum projiciet, quemadmodum lapidem funda projiciunt. וכן ברבר רלל רי אליעזר אומר נשמתן של צדיקין גנוזות החת כסא הכבוד שנאמר בצרור החיים וגוי ונשמתן של רשעים סטרפות ומשוטטות מסוף העולם ועד סופו ואין להם מנוחה שנאמר יקלענה יגו
units.tr: "And he will cast out their soul as one casts a stone from a sling." By "sling" is understood the seat of the sling-stone, which is made like a palm. And according to Jonathan, this is the interpretation of the passage: "the soul of my lord will be bound in the bundle of the living in the world to come," for thus he renders the passage: "and the soul of my lord shall be laid up in the treasury, or storehouse, of life eternal before the LORD your God, and the souls of your adversaries he shall cast out, as stones are cast from a sling." And so in the sayings of our teachers, R. Eliezer, of blessed memory, is recorded as saying: "The souls of the righteous are hidden under the throne of glory, as it is said, 'in the bundle of life,' etc.; but the souls of the wicked are hurled and wander from one end of the world to the other, and have no rest, as it is said, 'he shall sling it.'" [וכן ברבר רלל רי אליעזר אומר נשמתן של צדיקין גנוזות החת כסא הכבוד שנאמר בצרור החיים וגוי ונשמתן של רשעים סטרפות ומשוטטות מסוף העולם ועד סופו ואין להם מנוחה שנאמר יקלענה יגו]

units.la: E: sic in sententiis doctorum nostrorum p. m. R. Eliezer dixisse legitur, anithas justorum repositas esse sub throno gloria sicuti scriptum est בצריר &c. & anima improborum abripiuntur & discurrunt ab una mundi extremitate ad alteram usque, neque ulla ipsis quies est, sicuti scriptum est, יקלענה / &c. Hanc sententiam dum non improbat Kimchius, probasse existimo. Sed clarius loquitur ad Ps. 22. circa finem, Atque sunt ex gentibus, quos non suscipiet etiamsi incurvaverint se illi. אותם שהרגו ישראל שהם יורדי עפר כלומר כגיהנם ולא יחיה האל נפש אחר מהם illi qui interfecerunt Israel, qui sunt descendentes in pulverem, q. d. quod futuri sint in Gehenna, & quod non vivificaturus sit ullam animam ex illis. Ubi manifeste apparet, eum per vivificare intelligere, ad vitam aeternam traducere, quemadmodum vivere est beate vivere, & תחיה est ἀναβίωσις id est non resuscitatio simpliciter, sed resuscitatio ad vitam aeternam, prout morti aeternae opponitur. Atque hinc lux accedit ad illud πολυθρύλητον Thalmudicorum, non esse תחיית המתים id est, resurrectionem mortuorum nisi justorum duntaxat. An ergo animae improborum annihilantur? Neutiquam. Etiamsi enim negarent improborum resurrectionem, non tamen inde colligi posset, ipsos της ψυχης Αλεμονην negare. An ergo non resurgent improbi ex Thalmudicorum istorum, qui sic loquuntur, sententia? Neque illud sequitur. Cum enim sic loquuntur, resurrectionem ad vitam aeternam intelligunt. Si cui duriusculus iste tropus forte videatur, is adeat Luc xx. 36. ubi codem modo vox Graeca ἀναστασις usurpatur. Adscribam locum, Filii huius aevi ducunt uxores, &c. Qui vero digni habiti fuerint, qui aevum illud consequantur, & resurrectionem ex mortuis, (nota, Nam resurrectionem, prout late accipitur, omnes consequentur, Act. 24. 15.) neque ducunt uxores, neque nuptum dantur. Nec enim mori possunt amplius, pares enim sunt angelis, & filii sunt Dei, quum sint υιοι αναστασεως id est, filii resurrectionis. Ubi obiter observo purum putum Thalmudisinum in istis verbis, qui vero digni habiti fuerint qui seculum illud consequantur. Maimon. Halacha de paenit. cap. 8. הטובה הצפונה לצדיקים חיי העולם הבא והיא ההיים שאין מות עמהם והטובה שאין עמרה רעה הוא שכתוב בתורה למען ייטיב לך והארכת ימים - מפי השמועה למרו למען ייטיב לך לעולם שכולי טוב הארכת לעולם שכולו ארוך וזה הוא העולם הבא: שכר הצדיקים הוא שיזכו לנועם זה ויהיו בטובה זו ופירעון הרשעים הוא שלא יוכו להיים אלו אלא יכרתו ויסותו וכל מי שאינו זוכה להיים אלו הוא המת וגומר / Bonum quod te- repositum est justis, est vita futuri seculi, vita sine morte, bonum sine ulla mixtura mali, S. S. E. in lege, ut bene tibi sit & prolonges dies. Didicerunt ex traditione, ut bene sit tibi, intelligendum de seculo, quod totum bonum est, & ut prolonges dies, capiendum de seculo quod totum longum est, atque hoc est seculum venturum. Merces justorum ista est, quod digni habebuntur hac amœnitate & in hoc bono victuri sint. Vindicta, contra, improborum hæc est, quod non habebuntur digni isthac vita, sed excindentur & morientur. Quisquis non habebitur dignus hac vita, iste mortuus est, &c. Addo & locum Joh. v. 29. Et prodibunt, qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vita, εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, hoc est תחיה / qui vero mala egerunt in resurrectionem judicii. Sola beata vita vere vita est, contra, in æternis suppliciis vivere, non vita sed mors est, quam Targum מותא חנינא / mortem secundam vocat. Iesa. xxii. 14. donec moriamini, Chald. donec moriamini morte secunda. Hinc in Apocalysi ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος cap. II. & xx. & xxi. Hanc Kimchi ad dictum locum Jesaiæ vocat, mortem animæ, מיתת הנפש בעולם / vult dicere, inquit, mortem animæ in futuro seculo. Huc pertinent πολυθρύλητα illa, quæ in Ebræorum scriptis passim occurrunt, justi, etiam cum mortui sunt, vivunt. Improbi, etiam dum vivunt, mortui sunt. Puto jam liquere. non alienas à stylo scripturæ Novi Testam. istãs phrases esse, qua animæ improborum perire, mori, & non resurrecturæ dicuntur. Item cum improbos in suturo seculo partem habituros negitant. Illos vid. nec ἀμφιβολία τῶν ψυχῶν, nec resurrectionem corporum negare. Quid ergo fiet verbis Kimchii ad Ps. primum? Dicam verbo, יקומו accepit in significatione subsistendi, prout opponitur τῷ cadere causa. Itidem תקומה accepit eo sensu, quo Levit. xxvi. 37. eandem vocem à Mose usurpatam esse pag. 445. in fine, ostendimus. R. Salomo in comm. vocat הקמת רגל / Atque hæc erat forensis formula לא היתה לו הקמת רגל id est cecidit causa. Interpretare hoc modo voces יקומו & תקומה quas in testimonio Kimchii sine interpretatione reliquimus, & nullæ erunt salebræ. Quod denique ad locum Kimchii attinet, quem ex comm. ejus ad Psal. civ. produximus, dices, in posterioribus verbis quibus asseritur, resurrectionem tantum fore piorum, eodem modo accipiendam vocem resurrectionis, quo in prioribus, ubi dicit, controverti utrum omnes homines resurrecturi sint. Hinc enim colliges, aut nonnullos Thalmudicorum isti hæsisse sententiæ, omnes in universum homines mines ad vitam æternam resurrecturos, aut hunc esse posteriorum verborum sensum, improbos omnino non resurrecturos. Resp. Kimchium non decidere controversiam, sed tantùm ostendere, quomodo Thalmudici Doctores de hac re vulgo loqui solent. Illam autem formulam, qua vulgo uti solent, dubitationi isti, utrum omnes homines, etiam improbi, resurrecturi sint, occasionem præbuisse. Quid vero prisci illi Pharisæi, quid ipse B. Paulus super hoc articulo senserit, ex aureo illo loco Actorum xxiv, 15. liquido apparet.
units.tr: So it is read in the sayings of our teachers, of blessed memory, that Rabbi Eliezer said the souls of the righteous are laid up under the throne of glory, as it is written, "in the bundle of life" [בצרור] etc., and the souls of the wicked are cast out and wander from one end of the world to the other, and have no rest, as it is written, "they shall be slung out" [יקלענה] etc. Although Kimchi does not disapprove of this saying, I think he approved it. But he speaks more clearly on Psalm 22, near the end: "And there are some of the nations whom he will not receive even if they bow themselves down to him" [אותם שהרגו ישראל שהם יורדי עפר כלומר כגיהנם ולא יחיה האל נפש אחר מהם]: "those who killed Israel, who are going down to the dust, that is, to Gehenna, and God will not make alive any soul among them." Here it plainly appears that by "make alive" he means bringing to eternal life, just as "to live" means "to live blessedly," and [תחיה] is ἀναβίωσις, that is, not resuscitation simply, but resuscitation to eternal life, as opposed to eternal death. And hence light falls on that much-repeated saying of the Talmudists, that there is no resurrection of the dead [תחיית המתים], except of the righteous only. Do the souls of the wicked then perish? By no means. For even if they denied the resurrection of the wicked, it could not be inferred from this that they deny the ruin of the soul [ψυχῆς ἀπώλειαν]. Do the wicked, then, not rise again according to the opinion of these Talmudists, who speak in this way? That does not follow either. For when they speak thus, they understand resurrection to eternal life. If this rather harsh figure of speech perhaps seems strange to anyone, let him consult Luke 20:36, where the Greek word ἀνάστασις is used in the same way. I will quote the passage: "The sons of this age marry wives, etc. But those who have been counted worthy to attain that age, and the resurrection from the dead" (note, for the resurrection, taken in its broad sense, all will attain it, Acts 24:15), "neither marry wives nor are given in marriage. For neither can they die any more, for they are equal to the angels, and are sons of God, since they are sons of the resurrection" [υἱοὶ ἀναστάσεως], that is, "sons of the resurrection." Here I note in passing the pure Talmudism in these words, "those who have been counted worthy to attain that age." Maimonides, Halacha on repentance, chapter 8: הטובה הצפונה לצדיקים חיי העולם הבא והיא החיים שאין מות עמהם והטובה שאין עמה רעה הוא שכתוב בתורה למען ייטיב לך והארכת ימים - מפי השמועה למדו למען ייטיב לך לעולם שכולו טוב והארכת לעולם שכולו ארוך וזה הוא העולם הבא: שכר הצדיקים הוא שיזכו לנועם זה ויהיו בטובה זו ופירעון הרשעים הוא שלא יזכו לחיים אלו אלא יכרתו וימותו וכל מי שאינו זוכה לחיים אלו הוא המת וגומר. "The good that is laid up for the righteous is the life of the world to come, which is life without death, good without any evil. The Torah says, 'that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days' (Deut. 22:7). By tradition they learned: 'that it may be well with you' is to be understood of the world, which is wholly good, and 'that you may prolong' of the world, which is wholly long, and this is the world to come. The reward of the righteous is that they are counted worthy of this delight and will be in this good; the recompense of the wicked is that they are not counted worthy of this life, but are cut off and die. Whoever is not counted worthy of this life is dead, etc." I add also John 5:29: "And those who have done good will come forth to the resurrection of life," εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, that is, [תחיה]; "but those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment." Only the blessed life is truly life; on the other hand, to live in eternal punishments is not life but death, which the Targum calls [מותא חנינא], "the second death." Isaiah 22:14: "until you die," Chaldee: "until you die the second death." Hence in the Apocalypse ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος, chapters 2, 20 and 21. Kimchi, on the said passage of Isaiah, calls this "the death of the soul" [מיתת הנפש בעולם]; "he means," he says, "the death of the soul in the future age." To this belong those much-repeated sayings that occur everywhere in Hebrew writings: "The righteous, even when they are dead, live. The wicked, even while they live, are dead." I think it is now clear that these phrases, in which the souls of the wicked are said to perish, to die, and not to rise again, are not foreign to the style of Scripture of the New Testament. Likewise when they deny that the wicked will have a share in the future age, they do not, as I see it, deny either the destruction of souls or the resurrection of bodies. What then will happen to Kimchi's words on the first Psalm? I will say in a word: he took יקומו in the sense of standing, as opposed to falling in a lawsuit. Likewise he took תקומה in the sense in which we showed, on page 445 near the end, that Moses used the same word in Leviticus 26:37. R. Solomon, in his commentary, calls it הקמת רגל, and this was the legal formula לא היתה לו הקמת רגל, that is, "his cause fell." Interpret the words יקומו and תקומה, which we left without translation in Kimchi's testimony, in this way, and there will be no difficulties. Finally, as for the passage of Kimchi that we quoted from his commentary on Psalm 104, you will say that in the latter words, where it is asserted that only the righteous will rise, the word "resurrection" is to be taken in the same sense as in the earlier words, where he says that it is disputed whether all men will rise. For from this you would infer either that some of the Talmudists held the opinion that all men without exception will rise to eternal life, or that the sense of the latter words is that the wicked will not rise at all. I reply: Kimchi does not settle the controversy, but only shows how the Talmudic doctors commonly speak about this matter. Moreover, that formula which they commonly use gave occasion to the doubt whether all men, even the wicked, will rise. But what the ancient Pharisees thought about this article, and what the blessed Paul himself thought, is clear from that golden passage in Acts 24:15.
