units.la: XXVI. 7. Qui suspendit terram super בליםרה 480.
units.tr: XXVI. 7. Who hangs the earth upon nothing [בליםרה] 480.

units.la: XXXVII. 7. Qui in manu omnium hominum signat, ut noverint singuli
units.tr: XXXVII. 7. Who sets a seal on the hand of every man, that all men may know their works.

units.la: opera sua. An ex istis verbis aliquod patrocinium Chiromantiæ queri possi-
units.tr: his works. Could any support for chiromancy be sought from these words

units.la: t. Vera Ebræi textus expositio. 422.
units.tr: t. True exposition of the Hebrew text. 422.

units.la: XXXIX. 1. An nosti tempus partus tragelaphorum? Tragelaphum non esse fabulosum
units.tr: XXXIX. 1. Do you know the time when the tragelaphs give birth? That the tragelaph is not a fabulous animal.

units.la: animal. Quid sit יעלה / B. Augustini allegoria. 422.
units.tr: animal. What is ya'alah [יעלה] / B. Augustine's allegory. 422.

units.la: XL. 10. Ecce Behemoth, quem feci tecum. Querela de studiorum præcipitatione.
units.tr: XL. 10. Behold Behemoth, which I made with thee. A complaint about the haste of studies.

units.la: Elogium egregii juvenis, D. Theodori Saeckma. Behemoth, elephas, ϑηρίον. Belluæ, de Elephantis. Plurale pro singul. auxeseos causa. Chochmoth, de increata sapientia. Elephas unde dictus? An ab Ebr. eleph, bos? An vero ab אלף discere: Bos Luca. Belluæ docilitas. Barrus ex Chaldæo בעירא / Fabulæ Judæorum de bove sylvestri. Pseudo-Ezras. Elephanti omnia accurate convenire. Diabolo non item. Evangelicorum quorundam error.
units.tr: A eulogy of an outstanding young man, D. Theodore Saeckma. Behemoth, elephant, beast [ϑηρίον]. Beasts: concerning elephants. The plural is used for the singular, for the sake of magnification. Chochmoth: concerning uncreated wisdom. Whence is the elephant so named? Is it from the Hebrew eleph, ox? Or rather from alaph [אלף] to learn: the Lucanian ox. The docility of the beast. Barrus from the Chaldee be'ira [בעירא]: the Jewish fables about the wild ox. Pseudo-Ezra. All things agree accurately with the elephant, but not so with the devil. The error of certain evangelicals.

units.la: 14. Ipse est principium viarum Domini. Hoc loco primarium eorum argumentum contineri, qui Diabolum hic describi existimant. Locum illum citari à Bell. ad probandum Monarchicum statum Ecclesiæ. Per vias Domini, operaque ejus intelligi. Principium, pro præstantissimo. Conferuntur varii interpretes. Ἀρχή. Explicatur locus Sirach. xi. 3. Apoc. 3. 4. Principium creationis Dei. Angelos ante creationem mundi creatos, ex hoc loco collegisse Bedam. Locum hunc male opponi Ario. Lxx. interpretum exorbitatio. Quomodo illudatur Diabolo, &c. Augustini error.
units.tr: 14. He is the beginning of the ways of the Lord. Here is contained the chief argument of those who think that the Devil is described in this place. Bellarmine cites the passage to prove the monarchical state of the Church. By "the ways of the Lord" are understood his works. "Beginning" [ἀρχή] is taken for the most excellent. Various interpreters are compared. The passage is explained by Sirach xi. 3 and Apoc. 3. 4, "the beginning of the creation of God." Bede gathered from this place that the angels were created before the creation of the world. This place is wrongly set against Arius. The Septuagint translators go beyond what the text says. How the Devil is mocked, etc. The error of Augustine.

units.la: Leviathan. Non esse Diabolum, aut ejus collegam, vel optionem, sed balænam. Examinantur quatuor loca, quæ persuadere Scholasticis, hic diabolum describi.
units.tr: Leviathan. That this is not the Devil, or his colleague or counterpart, but a whale. Four passages are examined which the Schoolmen rely on to persuade us that the Devil is described here.

units.la: XLI. 3. Locus primus, Non parcam ei verbis potentibus & ad deprecandum compositis. Nihil tale in Ebræo extare.
units.tr: XLI. 3. The first passage: "I will not spare him, nor speak to him words of power and suited to entreaty." Nothing of the sort is found in the Hebrew.

units.la: 16. Locus secundus, cum sublatus fuerit, timebunt angeli, & territi purgabuntur. Aliam plane in Ebr. esse sententiam. Ridicula Emmanuelis Sa, interpretatio vocis purgabuntur.
units.tr: 16. The second passage: when he is raised up, the angels will be afraid, and, struck with terror, they will be purified. The Hebrew has quite a different sense. The interpretation of the word purgabuntur by Emmanuel Sá is ridiculous.

units.la: Versus penult. Lxx. ad illudendum ei ab angelis meis. Nihil tale in Ebr.
units.tr: The penultimate verse, in the Septuagint: "to mock him, by my angels." Nothing like this in the Hebrew.

units.la: Vers. ult. locus 4. omnes sublime videt. Ipse est rex super omnes filios superbiæ.
units.tr: Last verse, locus 4. He beholds all that is high. He himself is king over all the sons of pride.

units.la: PSALMI.
units.tr: PSALMS.

units.la: Semel illud observa, lector, nos Psalmos citare secundum eos numeros, qui in Ebr. textu & nostris Editionibus observantur. Nemo enim ignorat Græcos & vulgatum interpretem circa numeros ab Ebræis variare. Quæ discrepantia, unde orta sit, quousque se porrigat, diximus pagina.
units.tr: Note this once for all, reader: we cite the Psalms by the numbering used in the Hebrew text and in our editions. No one is unaware that the Greeks and the Vulgate translator differ from the Hebrews in their numbering. Where this discrepancy arose, and how far it extends, I have explained on the page.

units.la: Unde translatum sit Psalterium, quod in Bibliis vulgatis legitur. Quid sit Psalterium Gallicanum, Quid Romanum.
units.tr: Whence the Psalter read in the common Bibles was translated. What the Gallican Psalter is, and what the Roman Psalter is.

units.la: I. 5. Ideo non resurgent impii in judicio. Examinatur ista versio. Verus sensus explicatur.
units.tr: I. 5. "Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment." This version is examined, and the true sense is explained.

units.la: An Kimchius in comm. ad hunc locum statuat animas improborum annihilari?
units.tr: Whether Kimchi, in his commentary on this passage, holds that the souls of the wicked are annihilated.

units.la: II. 12 Apprehendite disciplinam. Rejicitur ea versio. Confessio Bellarm. & Andradii, ex textu Ebr. invictum adversus Judæos argumentum depromi posse.
units.tr: II. 12. "Take hold of instruction." This version is rejected. The confession of Bellarmine and Andradius. From the Hebrew text an argument invincible against the Jews can be drawn.

units.la: II. 12 Colite Dominum cum reverentia, &c. κύριον quinquies occurrere in Scriptura. Recensentur loca nullibi servilem timorem denotari.
units.tr: II. 12. "Serve the Lord with reverence," etc. κύριον [kyrion] occurs five times in Scripture. The passages are listed, and in none of them is servile fear denoted.

units.la: VIII. 5. Quid est homo aut filius hominis, &c. Discursum Augustini ad illum locum niti ficulneo fundamento. Et aliquando pro aut poni. 7. Omnia subjecit pedibus ejus, &c, Inepta allegoria Antonii Episcopi Florentini locum istum de Papa exponentis. 448.
units.tr: VIII. 5. "What is man, or the son of man," etc. Augustine's discourse on that passage rests on a fig-leaf foundation. "Et" is sometimes put for "aut." 7. "Thou hast put all things under his feet," etc. The foolish allegory of Antonius, Bishop of Florence, who expounds this passage of the Pope. 448.

units.la: XIV. Sepulcrum patens, &c. Versus istos tres in Ebr. non extare; Ab Apostolo ex variis Scripturae locis contextos esse. 449.
units.tr: XIV. "Their throat is an open sepulchre," etc. These three verses are not found in the Hebrew; the Apostle put them together from various places of Scripture. 449.

units.la: XVI. 10. Non relinques animam meam in inferno. Animae variae significationes. Pro persona, vita, corpore, & quidem mortuo. An peccaverit Beza, vocem cadaver usurpando Act. 2. Eandem vocem Patres & Pontificios usurpasse. 449.
units.tr: XVI. 10. "Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell." The various meanings of "soul": for a person, for life, for the body, and indeed for a dead body. Whether Beza erred in using the word "cadaver" at Acts 2. The Fathers and the Papists used the same word. 449.

units.la: XVII. 14. Saturati sunt filiis. Quid legerint interpretes, qui verterunt saturati sunt porcina, vel porcis. Augustini expositio. Legisse cos vios vel vios pro vios. Augustini jocus, melius esse, Herodis porcum quam filium esse. 551
units.tr: XVII. 14. "They are satisfied with children." What the translators read who rendered it "they are satisfied with swine's flesh" or "with swine": they read χοίρων [choiron], swine, for υἱῶν [huion], sons. Augustine's exposition. Augustine's joke that it is better to be Herod's pig than his son. 551.

units.la: XVIII. 26. Cum sancto sanctus eris, & cum perverso perverteris. Verba ea de Deo dici, male usurpari de familiaritate colenda cum bonis & fugienda cum malis. 450.
units.tr: XVIII. 26. "With the holy thou wilt be holy, and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted." These words are said of God, and they are wrongly applied to cultivating familiarity with the good and shunning the bad. 450.

units.la: 36. Quando me humilias, tunc me magnificas. 451. & 456.
units.tr: 36. "When thou humblest me, then thou makest me great." 451 and 456.

units.la: XIX. 5. In omnem terram exivit linea eorum. 151.
units.tr: XIX. 5. "Their line has gone out into all the earth." 151.

units.la: Ibid. Sol posuit tabernaculum in illis. Ita habet in Ebraeo, fatentibus Pontificiis. LXX. In sole posuit tabernaculum suum. Ea versio rejicitur. Frustra esse Cenemanum & alios in conciliatione utriusque textus. Manichaeos ex vulgata versione in adorationem Solis delatos. Sixti Senensis censura. An Origenes eidem errori haeserit. Augustini alienia expositio. Bellarminiex hoc loco conclusio. Carthusiani, Lombardi; Geneb. Bell. interpretationes. Theodoreti & Lyrae melior explicatio. 451.
units.tr: Ibid. "He has set his tabernacle in them" [the sun]. So it reads in the Hebrew, as the Papists admit. The LXX reads "In the sun he has set his tabernacle." That version is rejected. Cenemanus and others labour in vain to reconcile the two texts. The Manichaeans were led by the Vulgate version to worship the sun. The censure of Sixtus of Siena. Whether Origen fell into the same error. Augustine's alien exposition. Bellarmine's conclusion from this passage. The interpretations of the Carthusians, Lombard, Genebrard and Bellarmine. The better explanation of Theodoret and Lyra. 451.

units.la: 14. Et ab alienis parce servo tuo. Alia esse in Ebraeo. Quid decepit Gr. & Latinos. Emmanuelis Satimiditas. Alienae interpretationes Scholasticorum & applicationes. Alius vulgatae versionis de sectus. 455.
units.tr: 14. "And spare thy servant from strangers." The Hebrew has something else. What deceived the Greeks and Latins. The timidity of Emmanuel. The alien interpretations and applications of the Schoolmen. Another deviation of the Vulgate version. 455.

units.la: Ibid. Si mei non fuerint dominati, tunc immaculatus ero & emundabor a delicto maximo. Mei Genitivi casus esse. Pium IV. haec male sibi aptasse. Querela ejus de suorum promotione, notanda Politicis. 456.
units.tr: Ibid. "If my enemies have not ruled over me, then I shall be blameless and cleansed from the greatest sin." "Mei" is a genitive case. Pius IV wrongly applied this to himself. His complaint about the promotion of his own people is to be noted by politicians. 456.

units.la: XXII. 2. Longe a salute mea verba delictorum meorum. In Ebraeo aliter legi, longinquus a salute mea, verbis rugitus mei. Scholasticorum interpretationes Quid sit rugire hoc loco. Aliquid de justificatione. 457.
units.tr: XXII. 2. "Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions." In the Hebrew it is read differently: "far from my salvation, the words of my roaring." The interpretations of the Schoolmen. What "roaring" means in this place. Something about justification. 457.

units.la: 17. Foderunt manus meas & pedes meos. Interpretamenta veterum. Quid sit in Masora כתרילישני germanam lectionem esse כארי, Joh. Isaaci error. Iudaeorum confessio. Masora marginalis ad Num. 24. 9 [Nota, in mendo eam cubare. Nam in ea confunditur phathachatum cum Kimetzato. Num. 23. 24. occurrere quintum, sed cum vau in principio] cur in hodiernis exemplaribus Bibliorum sit כארי / Judaeorum pertinacia. 458.
units.tr: 17. "They pierced my hands and my feet." The interpretations of the ancients. What is meant in the Masorah by [כתרילישני], and that the true reading is [כארי]. The error of John Isaac. The confession of the Jews. The marginal Masorah on Num. 24.9 [note that the error lies in it: for there the patah is confused with the qamets; the fifth occurs at Num. 23.24, but with a vav at the beginning]. Why in present-day copies of the Bible the word is [כארי]. The obstinacy of the Jews. 458.

units.la: Dissertatio de Keri & Chetib. 462.
units.tr: Dissertation on the Keri and Chetib. 462.

units.la: XXIV. 2. Super maria fundavit eam. Priscorum sententia, terram innatare aquae instar ratis. Non esse Antipodas. Zachariae Papae imperitia. Vergilius Juvanensium Episcopus haereseos postulatus, quod doceret esse Antipodas. Explicantur loca Psal. 75. 4. & 104. 5. Job. 26. 7. Quid ibi sit בליםור / Quot modis dici possit, terram fundatam esse super aquas. Sixti Senensis error. An terra sit altior mari. Explicatur locus Psal. 107. 23. Doctissimorum quorundam virorum error circa vocem Orbis. 476.
units.tr: XXIV. 2. "He founded it upon the seas." The opinion of the ancients that the earth floats on the waters like a raft. That there are no Antipodes. The ignorance of Pope Zachary. Virgil, Bishop of Salzburg, was accused of heresy because he taught that there are Antipodes. The passages Ps. 75.4, Ps. 104.5 and Job 26.7 are explained. What the Hebrew word [בליםור] there is. In how many ways it can be said that the earth is founded upon the waters. The error of Sixtus of Siena. Whether the earth is higher than the sea. The passage Ps. 107.23 is explained. The error of certain very learned men concerning the word "world" (orbis). 476.

units.la: 7. & 9. Attollite portas principes vestras. Examinatur ista versio. Inepti hic interpretes. 486. XXV. 19. De necessitatibus meis eripe me. Vox necessitas non intellecta ab interpretibus. Male accipi pro necessitate peccandi. Quid sit ἀνάγκη in lingua Hellenistica. Eam pro afflictione poni. 487. XXIX. 1. Afferte Domino filii Dei, afferte Domino filii arietum. Alterutrum redundare in Ebraeo. Per filios arietum inepte fideles, per arietes Apostolos intelligi. Cur mitrae Episcopales bicornes sint. 488. XXXI. 16. Inmanibus tuis sunt sortes meae. οἱ κλῆροί μου. Melior lectio & veritas Ebr. οἱ κλῆροί μου. Aliena Augustini expositio. 490. XXXIII. 15. Qui finxit sigillatim corda eorum. Hunc locum male à Scholasticis allegari, destruendis duobus erroribus. Quid sit ξῦ' μόνας. יחדיו / יחד 489. 6. Verbo Domini caeli facti sunt. 489. XXXIV. 1. Cum immutavit vultum suum &c. 395. XXXV. 18. In populo gravi laudabo te. In Ebr. esse עמום / quod etiam numerosum significat. Augustini glossa aliena. 490. XXXIX. 10. Obscurdui & non aperui os meum, quia tu fecisti. Augustinum legisse, quia tu fecisti me, & proinde aberrasse in loci istius interpretatione. 490. 6. Palmares de fidi dies meos. Latina vetus, veteres posuisti dies meos. Eam ex sphalmate librarii natam esse. Annotatoris ad Biblia Romana impudentia. Quid sit παλαιστής. Palmus duplex. Παλαιστής luctator. Unde alia interpretatio nata est, ab Ebr. aliena. 551. XL. 8. In capite libri scriptum est de me. Quid sit מגלה / Priscus mos convolvendi libros. Unde volumen. In volumine libri, locutio ek parallelon. Quid sit κεφαλίς apud Lxx. interpretes & in Epist. ad Ebraeos x. 7. Quomodo laboraverint interpretes, qui per κεφαλίς caput id est, principium intellexere. Variae opiniones de isthoc principio. κεφαλίς volumen, מגלה / An Genef. I 1. per principium Filius Dei intelligatur. Hilarii & Tertulliani crassus error. Variae expositiones aliorum. Paraphrasis Jerosolymitana. Quid illi spectaverint, qui per principium filium Dei intellexerunt. An huc pertineat locus Joh 8. 25, & Joh. 1. 1. & Ps. 110. Aooc. 3. 14. 490. XLII. 1. Deum fontem vivum. Pontificiorum quorundam circa hunc locum pervicacia. 79. & 495. XLIV. 13 Non fuit multitudo in jubilationibus eorum. Augustinum mendosa lectione deceptum fuisse. Verior lectio, in commutationibus eorum. Veritas Ebraea. 553. XLV. 1. Prdiis qui commutabuntur. Aliena Patrum expositio. 495. 5. Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum potentissime. Quomodo fluctuent Interpretes in hujus loci expositione. 496. XLVIII. Oratio Stephani Archi-Episcopi Patraccensis. 496. XLIX. 16. In inferno. An limbus, an purgatorium intelligatur. 519. L. 11. Pulchritudo agri mecum est. An hinc probari possit, Deo omnia esse praesentia. 496. LI. 7. In iniquitatibus conceptus sum & in peccatis &c. Curiosae Patrum & Scholasticorum quaestiones, An filiis impurentur peccata parentum. Augustinus à se ipso diversus. Quomodo peccata & iniquitates. In Ebraeo esse singularia. 497. LX. 10. Moab. olla spei meae. Alia lectio, aula spei meae. Aula pro olla. Ambrosii lapsus. 498. 598.
units.tr: 7. & 9. "Lift up your gates, O princes." This version is examined. Foolish interpreters here. 486. XXV. 19. "Deliver me from my necessities." The word "necessity" was not understood by the translators. It is wrongly taken to mean the necessity of sinning. What ἀνάγκη [anankē] means in Hellenistic language, and that it is used for affliction. 487. XXIX. 1. "Bring to the Lord, O sons of God; bring to the Lord, O sons of rams." That one of the two phrases is redundant in the Hebrew. By "sons of rams" the faithful are foolishly understood, and by "rams" the Apostles. Why Episcopal mitres are two-horned. 488. XXXI. 16. "In thy hands are my lots." οἱ κλῆροί μου [hoi klēroi mou]. The better reading and the Hebrew truth. Augustine's alien exposition. 490. XXXIII. 15. "He who formed their hearts one by one." This passage is wrongly cited by the Schoolmen, and it serves to destroy two errors. What ξῦ' μόνας [xy' monas] means. יחדיו / יחד [yachdav / yachad]. 489. 6. "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made." 489. XXXIV. 1. "When he changed his countenance," etc. 395. XXXV. 18. "In a numerous people I will praise thee." The Hebrew is עמום [amum], which also means numerous. Augustine's alien gloss. 490. XXXIX. 10. "I was dumb and did not open my mouth, because thou hast made it." Augustine read "because thou hast made me," and so went astray in the interpretation of this passage. 490. 6. "Thou hast made my days as handbreadths." The old Latin has "thou hast made my days old." This arose from a slip of the scribe. The impudence of the annotator on the Roman Bible. What παλαιστής [palaistēs] means. Two kinds of palm. παλαιστής [palaistēs] means a wrestler. Whence another interpretation arose, alien from the Hebrew. 551. XL. 8. "In the head of the book it is written of me." What מגלה [megillah] means. The ancient custom of rolling up books, and whence the word volumen. In the volume of the book, an expression by parallelism. What κεφαλίς [kephalis] means among the LXX and in Heb. 10.7. How those interpreters laboured who understood κεφαλίς as the head, that is, the beginning. Various opinions about this beginning: κεφαλίς [kephalis] as volume, מגלה [megillah]. Whether through "the beginning" (Gen. 1.1) the Son of God is understood. The gross error of Hilary and Tertullian. Various other expositions. The Jerusalem paraphrase. What those intended who understood the Son of God by "the beginning." Whether John 8.25, John 1.1, Ps. 110 and Apoc. 3.14 pertain here. 490. XLII. 1. "God, the living fountain." The obstinacy of certain Papists about this passage. 79 and 495. XLIV. 13. "There was no multitude in their rejoicings." Augustine was deceived by a faulty reading. The truer reading is "in their exchanges" (commutationibus). The Hebrew truth. 553. XLV. 1. "Princes who shall be changed." The alien exposition of the Fathers. 495. 5. "Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, most mighty." How the interpreters waver in the exposition of this passage. 496. XLVIII. The oration of Stephen, Archbishop of Patras. 496. XLIX. 16. "In hell." Whether limbo or purgatory is meant. 519. L. 11. "The beauty of the field is with me." Whether from this it can be proved that all things are present to God. 496. LI. 7. "I was conceived in iniquities and in sins," etc. The curious questions of the Fathers and Schoolmen: whether the sins of parents are imputed to their children. Augustine at odds with himself. How sins and iniquities differ. In the Hebrew the words are singular. 497. LX. 10. "Moab is the pot of my hope." Another reading is "the hall of my hope": aula [hall] for olla [pot]. The slip of Ambrose. 498, 598.

units.la: LXII. 13. Reddis unicuique secundum opera ejus. Versio Lutheri expenditur prout meretur. An voces OMEN, & ARBITRIUM sint in Bibliis.
units.tr: LXII. 13. Reddis unicuique secundum opera ejus. Luther's version is weighed at its true worth. Whether the words OMEN and ARBITRIUM are in the Bible.

units.la: LXIV. 7. Accedet homo ad cor altum & exaltabitur Deus. Quam procul ea interpr. ab Ebraeo abeat.
units.tr: LXIV. 7. Accedet homo ad cor altum & exaltabitur Deus. How far that translation departs from the Hebrew.

units.la: LXVIII. 21. Increpa feras arundinis. Arundinis copia in Aegypto, & usus in veteri militia. Per feram arundinis alii Aegyptios, alii Pharaonem intelligunt. Augustl. legit, feras calami, & intelligit haereticos. Ejus fundamentum. Varius usus vocis הָרָמָה.
units.tr: LXVIII. 21. Increpa feras arundinis. Reeds were plentiful in Egypt, and were used in ancient warfare. Some understand by the beast of the reeds the Egyptians, others Pharaoh. Augustine reads feras calami, and understands heretics. His foundation for this. The varied use of the word הָרָמָה [harmah].

units.la: Vers. ult. Mirabilis est Deus in sanctis suis. Non agi de sanctis in Ebraeo.
units.tr: Last verse. Mirabilis est Deus in sanctis suis. The Hebrew does not speak of saints.

units.la: LXXI. 16. Quoniam non cognovi literaturam, introibo in potentias Domini. Lovaniensem Belgicam a textu Latino recessisse. Alia lectio, quia non cognovi negotiationem. Inde probare Gelasium Papam, clericis omni mercatura interdictum esse. Querela de studiis nostrae juventutis.
units.tr: LXXI. 16. Quoniam non cognovi literaturam, introibo in potentias Domini. The Louvain Belgic version has departed from the Latin text. Another reading: quia non cognovi negotiationem. From this, to prove that Pope Gelasius forbade clerics all trade. A complaint about the studies of our youth.

units.la: LXXI. 6. Quoniam tu es patientia mea. In Ebr. esse, expectatio mea. Non significaficant patientiam in adversis, sed in expectatione. Explicatur locus Luc. 8. fructum ferunt in patientia. ὑπομονὴ nusquam in V. T. tolerantiam adversorum significare.
units.tr: LXXI. 6. Quoniam tu es patientia mea. In the Hebrew it is expectatio mea. The word does not signify patience in adversity, but patient expectation. The passage Luke 8, fructum ferunt in patientia, is explained. ὑπομονή [hypomonē] nowhere in the Old Testament signifies endurance of adversities.

units.la: LXXII. 14. Ex usuris & iniquitate redimet me. Allegorica interpretatio vocis usura. An ab Ebr. נשׁך Graecum τόκος fit. Quoties נשׁך per τόκος reddITUM fit. Egregia descriptio usurarii ex Gregorio Nysseno. [Vide plura apud Senensem lib. v. Annotat. CLXXXVIII.]
units.tr: LXXII. 14. Ex usuris & iniquitate redimet me. The allegorical interpretation of the word usura (usury). Whether the Greek τόκος [tokos] comes from the Hebrew נשׁך [nashak]. How often נשׁך is rendered by τόκος. An excellent description of the usurer from Gregory of Nyssa. [See more in Senensis, book 5, annotation 188.]

units.la: 5. Et permanebit cum Sole & ante Lunam. Vera locutionum istarum sententia, cum Sole, coram Luna. Ex hoc loco male demonstrari Christi aeternitatem a parte anteriori & posteriori. non semper de tempore, sed & aliquando de loco usurpari. Augustinus sudat.
units.tr: 5. Et permanebit cum Sole & ante Lunam. The true sense of these expressions is with the Sun, before the Moon. From this passage Christ's eternity is wrongly proved from the former and the latter part. The word is not always used of time, but sometimes also of place. Augustine labours over it.

units.la: LXXII. 16. Eritque firmamentum in terra in summis montium. Per firmamentum Interpretes intelligere frumentum. Explicatur textus Ebraeus. Et in eo vox פַּר־ / Augustini expositio. Quosdam de sacramento. Eucharisticae locum exponere. An Deut. 16.10. extet vox MISSA. Bellarminum hic adversari Genebrardo. Pontificios recedere a vulgata versione, qui afferunt in Ebraeo esse placentulam frumenti. Pauli Burgensis & Galatini ineptiae. Chaldaea paraphrasis an quippiam habeat de elevatione hostiae. Cordatum Bellarmini judicium de nugis Burgensis. Explicatur Chaldaeus textus. Baculus panis. Kimchii commentariis. In eo nihil de transubstantiatione. Producitur locus alius ex comm. Kimchi in Hoseam, ubi de mutatione naturae in diebus Messiae agitur.
units.tr: LXXII. 16. Eritque firmamentum in terra in summis montium. The interpreters understand firmamentum to mean grain. The Hebrew text is explained, and in it the word פַּר־ [par]. Augustine's exposition. Some relate it to the sacrament, and expound it as a passage about the Eucharist. Whether the word MISSA occurs in Deut. 16.10. Bellarmine here opposes Genebrardus. The Papists depart from the Vulgate version, who assert that the Hebrew has a little cake of grain. The trifles of Paul of Burgos and Galatinus. Whether the Chaldee paraphrase contains anything about the elevation of the host. Bellarmine's sensible judgement on the nonsense of Burgos. The Chaldee text is explained. A staff of bread. In Kimchi's commentaries. Nothing about transubstantiation is in it. Another passage is cited from Kimchi's commentary on Hosea, where the change of nature in the days of the Messiah is discussed.

units.la: LXXIV. 12. Operatus est salutem in medio terrae. Per medium terrae aliquos Judaeam aut Jerusalem intelligere. Quomodo Judaea & Jerusalem in medio terrae. Quid sit umbilicus terrae, Jezech. 38.12. Umbilicus Italiae &c. Quid medium in corpore humano. Augustini sententia per medium terrae corpus Christi intelligentis. Ande loco crucifixionis hic loquatur Psaltes. Affirmari hoc communiori sententia. Calvariae mons an τῆς ἀναστάσεως μὲ-(αὐτοῦ fit. An Adam sepultus sit in monte Calvariae. An sanguis Christi Calvariam Adami rigaverit. An huc pertineat locus iste, Surge qui dormis & continget te Christus, ut quidam legunt, Eph. v. Vera hujus loci (Ps. 74.) interpretatio authoritate Pontificiorum confirmatur. Alia.
units.tr: LXXIV. 12. Operatus est salutem in medio terrae. Some understand by the middle of the earth Judaea or Jerusalem. How Judaea and Jerusalem are in the middle of the earth. What is the navel of the earth, Ezek. 38.12. The navel of Italy, etc. What the middle is in the human body. Augustine's view that by the middle of the earth is meant the body of Christ who understands. Whether the Psalmist here speaks of the place of the crucifixion. This is asserted by the more common opinion. Whether the hill of Calvary is τῆς ἀναστάσεως μέσον [tēs anastaseōs mesos], the middle of the resurrection of Christ. Whether Adam was buried on the hill of Calvary. Whether the blood of Christ watered the Calvary of Adam. Whether this passage belongs here, Arise, you who sleep, and Christ shall give you light, as some read it, Eph. 5. The true interpretation of this passage (Ps. 74) is confirmed by the authority of the Papists. Another point.

units.la: LXXV. 4. Ego confirmavi columnas ejus.
units.tr: LXXV. 4. Ego confirmavi columnas ejus.

units.la: LXXVIII. 49. aliis 54. immissiones per angelos malos. An angelorum malorum opera usus sit Deus in plagis Aegyptiorum. Augustinum fluctuare. An sansanctianget polsint dici mali, ab effectu. Græcæ versionis ambiguitas. Ea deceptum fuisse vulgatum.
units.tr: LXXVIII. 49, in others 54. immissiones per angelos malos. Whether God used the work of evil angels in the plagues of the Egyptians. Augustine wavers. Whether those who are holy can be called evil from their effect. The ambiguity of the Greek version. The Vulgate was deceived by it.

units.la: LXXXI. 16. Et fuisset tempus eorum in seculum.
units.tr: LXXXI. 16. Et fuisset tempus eorum in seculum.

units.la: LXXXII. 1. Deus stetit in synagoga Deorum. Quomodo sudet Bellarm. in conciliatione versionis istius cum originario textu. Nomen pro pronomine. Synagoga & Ecclesia synonyma, coetum tamen fidelium V. T. communiter dici Synagogam. Bellarmini & Catechescos Tridentinæ impudentia. An fideles V.T. instar pecudum terrena tantum bona spectarint. Synagoga & ejus conjugata usurpari etiam de coetu fidelium N.T.
units.tr: LXXXII. 1. Deus stetit in synagoga Deorum. How Bellarmine sweats in reconciling this version with the original text. The noun for the pronoun. Synagogue and Church are synonyms, yet the congregation of the faithful of the Old Testament is commonly called the Synagogue. The impudence of Bellarmine and of the Tridentine Catechism. Whether the faithful of the Old Testament, like beasts, regarded only earthly goods. The synagogue and its cognates are also used of the congregation of the faithful in the New Testament.

units.la: 6. Ego dixi Dii estis. Ad magistratum tantum pertinere. Explicatur locus Joh. x. 35. Sermo pro mandato. An Sacerdotes N. T. vocentur Dii. An Constantinus hunc locum bene allegaverit.
units.tr: 6. Ego dixi Dii estis. This pertains only to the magistrate. The passage John 10.35 is explained. The word means command. Whether the priests of the New Testament are called gods. Whether Constantine quoted this passage rightly.

units.la: LXXXIII. 1. Deus quis similis erit tibi? Eam versionem non posse conciliari cum Ebraeo. Augustini expositio.
units.tr: LXXXIII. 1. Deus quis similis erit tibi? That version cannot be reconciled with the Hebrew. Augustine's exposition.

units.la: LXXXIV. 7. 8. 9. Ascensiones in corde suo disposuit, in valle lacrymarum, in loco quem posuit. Etenim benedictionem dabit Legis lator, ibunt de virtute in virtutem. Eam versionem immane ab Ebraeo discrepare. Textus Ebraeus explicatur. Examinatur & versio B. Lutheri. An vita nostra vocetur hoc loco vallis lacrymarum. An Christiani omnes vocentur DI.
units.tr: LXXXIV. 7, 8, 9. Ascensiones in corde suo disposuit, in valle lacrymarum, in loco quem posuit. Etenim benedictionem dabit Legis lator, ibunt de virtute in virtutem. That version differs enormously from the Hebrew. The Hebrew text is explained. Luther's version is also examined. Whether our life is called here the valley of tears. Whether all Christians are called gods.

units.la: 12. Quia misericordiam & veritatem diligit Dominus. Nihil tale esse in Ebraeo. Ruere ergo expositiones Patrum. Quid spectaverint Interpretes Graeci.
units.tr: 12. Quia misericordiam & veritatem diligit Dominus. Nothing like this is in the Hebrew. Thus the expositions of the Fathers collapse. What the Greek interpreters had in view.

units.la: LXXXV. 13. Eruisti animam meam de inferno inferiore. An de purgatorio, an limbo, an Gehenna agatur. Dissensus interpretum. Nihil obstare vocem inferiore, quominus de sepulcro Ebraeum exponatur. An diversae regiones inferni ex hoc loco colligi possint. Infer ab inferendo. Variae sententiae, cujus respectu infernus inferior dicatur.
units.tr: LXXXV. 13. Eruisti animam meam de inferno inferiore. Whether it is about purgatory, limbo or Gehenna. The disagreement of the interpreters. The word inferiore (lower) does not prevent the Hebrew from being explained of the grave. Whether different regions of hell can be gathered from this passage. Infer from inferendo. The various opinions as to the respect in which hell is called lower.

units.la: LXXXVII. 4. Memor ero Raab. Non meretricem, sed Ægyptum significari. Quomodo duo illa in Ebraea scriptura distinguantur. Error Theop. August. Euthymii.
units.tr: LXXXVII. 4. Memor ero Raab. Not a harlot, but Egypt is meant. How those two are distinguished in the Hebrew Scripture. The error of Theophylact, Augustine and Euthymius.

units.la: 5. Nunquid Sion dicet homo, & homo natus est in ea. Et fundavit eam altissimus. Textus Ebraei sententia breviter explicatur. Posita versio examinatur. Alienae ejus expositiones. Codices Graecos hodie legere, mater Sion, dicet homo. Ejus alienae rursus expositiones. Quantam caliginem unum illud librariorum sphalma huic loco offuderit. Nostra expositio firmatur authoritate. Emm. Sa, & Genebrardi. An ex hoc loco utraque Christi natura demonstrari possit.
units.tr: 5. Nunquid Sion dicet homo, & homo natus est in ea? Et fundavit eam altissimus. The sense of the Hebrew text is briefly explained. The version proposed is examined. Other expositions of it. Today the Greek codices read mother Sion, shall man say. Their other expositions again. How much darkness that single error of the scribes has cast over this passage. Our exposition is confirmed by authority: Emmanuel Sa and Genebrardus. Whether from this passage both natures of Christ can be demonstrated.

units.la: LXXXVIII. An medici suscitabunt? Nihil tale in Ebraeo. Medicos à Thalmudicis inter opifices numerari. Elogium Medicorum.
units.tr: LXXXVIII. An medici suscitabunt? Nothing like this is in the Hebrew. Physicians are counted among the craftsmen by the Talmudists. A eulogy of physicians.

units.la: LXXXIX. 44. Abbreviasti dies adolescentiae ejus. 39. Tu disturbasti Christum tuum. 48. Memento quae mea sit substantia.
units.tr: Psalm 89: You have shortened the days of his youth. 39: You have disturbed your Christ. 48: Remember what my substance is.

units.la: XC. 9. Consumimus dies nostros sicut ִ 238.525. versio vulg. anni nostri sicut aranea meditabuntur. Eam cum Ebr. textu conciliari neutiquam posse.
units.tr: XC. 9. Consumimus dies nostros sicut ... 238, 525. The Vulgate version: our years shall meditate like a spider. That it can by no means be reconciled with the Hebrew text.

units.la: 10. Si autem in potentatibus, octoginta anni, & amplius eorum labor & dolor. Examinatur illa versio. Elegantes interpretationes textus Ebraei. Alia.
units.tr: 10: But if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their labour and sorrow. That rendering is examined. Elegant interpretations of the Hebrew text. Another.

units.la: 11. Quoniam super venit nobis mansuetudo & corripiemur. Nec volam nec vestigium istius versionis in Ebr. comparere.
units.tr: 11. Quoniam super venit nobis mansuetudo & corripiemur. Neither the flight nor the trace of that version appears in the Hebrew.

units.la: 1: Dextram tuam sic notam fac nobis, &c. 529.
units.tr: 1: Dextram tuam sic notam fac nobis, etc. 529.

units.la: XCI.6. Ab incursu & daemonio meridiano. In Ebr. nullam daemonii mentionem fieri. Scaligeri interpretatio. 529.
units.tr: XCI. 6. Ab incursu & daemonio meridiano. The Hebrew makes no mention of any demon. Scaliger's interpretation. 529.

units.la: XCII. 15. Bene patientes erunt. Quid sit. ἐνπαθῶν. 530.
units.tr: XCII. 15. Bene patientes erunt. What it means: ἐνπαθῶν [enpathōn]. 530.

units.la: 13. Iustus ut palma florebit. Gr. ut Phoenix. An Phoenicem avem intellexerint interpretes. An avis illa in rerum natura sit. Frustra pro ajente sententia allegari hunc locum. 530.
units.tr: 13. Iustus ut palma florebit. The Greek has as the phoenix. Whether the interpreters understood the bird phoenix. Whether that bird exists in nature. This passage is cited in vain as support for an active agent. 530.

units.la: XCVI. 10. Dicite in gentibus, Dominus regnavit. An illa verba, a ligno, quae Iustinus legit in textu Ebr. fuerint olim. Lindani imprudentia. 331.
units.tr: XCVI. 10. Dicite in gentibus, Dominus regnavit. Whether those words, from the wood, which Justin read in the Hebrew text, were once there. Lindanus's carelessness. 331.

units.la: XCIX. 15. Adorate scabellum ejus, quia sanctum est. Veteres fere scabellum pro objecto adorationis accepisse. vid. pro terra & terram pro Christo. Ancaro Christi in Eucharistia adoranda sit. Alphonsi de Castro expositio de cruce. Concilii Nicenisecundi error. Bellarminus, Svarez, Lorinus confutantur. Confertur locus Psalm. 132.7. Conceditur. Per scab. pedum arcam intelligi. Confertur locus Psal. 138.2. Objectum adorantis ab objecto adorationis esse distinguendum. Veteres versus Jerusalem & templum orasse. Examinatur locus Ps. LXXII. 16. Unde Missam fabricant nonnulli interpretes. 532.
units.tr: XCIX. 15. Adorate scabellum ejus, quia sanctum est. Almost all the ancients took the footstool to be the object of worship, and the earth to mean Christ. Whether Christ in the Eucharist is to be adored. Alphonsus de Castro's exposition of the cross. The error of the Second Council of Nicaea. Bellarmine, Suárez and Lorinus are refuted. Psalm 132.7 is compared. It is conceded. That the footstool means the ark of the feet. Psalm 138.2 is compared. The object of the worshipper must be distinguished from the object of worship. The ancients prayed toward Jerusalem and the temple. Psalm 72.16 is examined. From which some interpreters build up the Mass. 532.

units.la: CII. 21. Ut audiret gemitus compeditorum, ut solveret filios interemptorum. Alienae interpretum expositiones. Conciliatur versio vulg. cum textu Ebr. Genitivus finis. Filius perditionis. Filii mortis, phrasis ambigua. Participiorum passivorum peculiaris significatio. 540.
units.tr: CII. 21. That he might hear the groaning of the prisoners, and loose the children of the dead. Other interpreters' expositions. The Vulgate version is reconciled with the Hebrew text. The genitive of purpose. "Son of perdition." "Sons of death," an ambiguous phrase. The peculiar meaning of passive participles. 540.

units.la: CIV. 3: Qui Contignat in aquis caenacula sua. Locum illum nihil facere pro aquis supra firmamentum. 177.
units.tr: CIV. 3: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters. That passage does nothing to place waters above the firmament. 177.

units.la: 5. Qui fundavit terram super bases suas. Quae sint bases terrae. 480.
units.tr: 5. Who laid the foundations of the earth upon their bases. What the bases of the earth are. 480.

units.la: 24. Omnia fecisti in Sapientia. An per sapientiam Filius Dei intelligatur. 494.
units.tr: 24. In wisdom hast thou made them all. Whether the Son of God is understood by wisdom. 494.

units.la: 26. Draco iste quem fecisti ad illudendum ei. Ineptae expositiones natae, tam eorum qui de balaena, quam qui de diabolo locum interpretantur. Vetera loci sententia: Explicatur vers. penult cap. 40. Iobi. 542.
units.tr: 26. This dragon which thou hast made to play therein. Foolish expositions arose, both of those who interpret the passage of the whale and of those who interpret it of the devil. The meaning of the passage in the older writers. The penultimate verse of Job 40 is explained. 542.

units.la: CX. Tecum principium in die virtutis tuae. Nobilissimi juvenis Epei ab Aykva elogium. Quantopere ea versio ab Ebraeo textu discrepet. Bellarminiana textus Ebr. perversio. Graecae vocis arche ambiguitas. Ea deceptus interpres vulgatus. Varii interpretum errores. An principium pro principatu positum sit. An Christus principium; 546.
units.tr: CX. Thine is the principality in the day of thy power. The praise of the most noble youth Epeus of Aykva. How far that version departs from the Hebrew text. Bellarmine's perversion of the Hebrew text. The ambiguity of the Greek word ἀρχή. The Vulgate translator was deceived by it. The various errors of the interpreters. Whether "principium" is put for "principatus." Whether Christ is the principle. 546.

units.la: 10. Ex utero ante Luciferum genui te. Nihil tale esse in Ebraeo. Locum nihil facere ad probandam Deitatem Christi. Interpretum genera. Maldonati portentosa phrasis. Augustini aberratio. 127. 547.
units.tr: 10. From the womb before the morning star have I begotten thee. Nothing like this is in the Hebrew. The passage does nothing to prove the Deity of Christ. The kinds of interpreters. Maldonatus' monstrous phrase. Augustine's error. 127. 547.

units.la: CXI. Magna sunt opera Domini, exquisita in omnes voluntates ejus. Locum illum allegari a Magistro sententiarum, ut probet plures esse voluntatis signi species. Censura L. Danaei. 556.
units.tr: CXI. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out according to all his pleasures. The Master of the Sentences cites this passage to prove that there are several kinds of signs of the will. Criticism by L. Danaeus. 556.

units.la: CXVIII. 27. Ornate festum frondibus. 556.
units.tr: CXVIII. 27. Bind the feast with boughs. 556.

units.la: CXIX. 28. Dormitavit anima mea &c. Natam eam versionem ex sphalmate librarii. 553.
units.tr: CXIX. 28. My soul melteth for heaviness, etc. That version arose from a scribal slip. 553.

units.la: 109. Anima mea in manibus meis. Explicatur phrasis Ebraea. Mendosa lectio, in manibus tuis. Augustini expositio. 422. 553.
units.tr: 109. My soul is in my hands. The Hebrew idiom is explained. The faulty reading "in thy hands." Augustine's exposition. 422. 553.

units.la: 112. Propter retributionem. An hic locus faciat ad probandam sententiam, bona opera mercedem proprie dictam mereri. Vocem Ebraeam שָׂכָר significare 1. calcaneum. 2. finem, in finem, in perpetuum, semper. Atque ita vulg. vers. 33. reddidisse. 3. mercedem. Gratuitam quoque benefificentiam, mercedem & retributionem vocari. <bl>נסל</bl>/ Dictum Antigoni de nonspectanda retributione.
units.tr: 112. For the reward. Whether this passage supports the view that good works properly deserve a wage. The Hebrew word שָׂכָר [sakar] means: (1) the heel; (2) the end, to the end, for ever, always, and so the Vulgate has rendered it at verse 33; (3) wage. Gratuitous beneficence is also called wage and recompense. [נסל] The saying of Antigonus about not looking for recompense. 173.

units.la: 173. Vide humilitatem meam. Non intelligi hoc loco virtutem.
units.tr: 173. Behold my humility. It is not to be understood here of virtue.

units.la: CXXVII. 4. Filii excussorum. Alienæ Hilarii & Augustini expositiones. Hieronymi censura. Misera Augustini disputatio, quot modis aliquid dicatur excuti. Per excussos Apostolos intelligi. In Ebræo esse fili juventutis. Phrasis ea explicatur. Refutatur Genebrardi assertio, נעורים non juventutem sed pueritiam denotare.
units.tr: CXXVII. 4. The children of the shaken off. The expositions of Hilary and Augustine, which differ from this. Jerome's criticism. Augustine's miserable disputation on how many ways something may be said to be shaken off. That the shaken off are to be understood as the Apostles. In the Hebrew it is children of youth. That phrase is explained. Genebrard's assertion that [נעורים, naʿurim] denotes childhood rather than youth is refuted.

units.la: CXXVIII. 2. Labore fructuum tuorum. Versionem eam natam ex ambiguo vocis Græcæ κοπιῶν, Quid sit κόπος. Supervacanea Augustini subtilitas, distinguentis inter labores fructuum & fructus laborum. In Ebr. esse, labores manuum tuarum.
units.tr: CXXVIII. 2. The labour of thy fruits. That version arose from the ambiguity of the Greek word κοπιῶν. What κόπος means. Augustine's superfluous subtlety, distinguishing between the labours of fruits and the fruits of labours. In the Hebrew it is the labours of thy hands.

units.la: CXXXII. 1. Memento Davidis & omnis mansuetudinis ejus. Ebræa aliter habere, ac proinde hic non allegari merita Davidis.
units.tr: CXXXII. 1. Remember David and all his meekness. The Hebrew reads otherwise, and therefore the merits of David are not alleged here.

units.la: 7. Adorate in loco ubi steterunt pedes ejus.
units.tr: 7. Worship at the place where his feet stood.

units.la: 15. Viduam ejus benedicés. Natam ineptam illam lectionem ex permutatis literis χ & ℓ. Errorem illum à doctissimis Pontificiis agnitum, nec tamen correctum hactenus.
units.tr: 15. I will abundantly bless her widow. That foolish reading arose from the interchange of the letters χ and ℓ. This error was recognised by the most learned Papists, yet has not been corrected until now.

units.la: CXXXIII. 3. Sicut ros Hermon qui descendit in montem Sion. Difficultas sublata observato asyndeto.
units.tr: CXXXIII. 3. As the dew of Hermon that descended upon the mount of Sion. The difficulty is removed by observing the asyndeton.

units.la: CXXXVI. 6. Qui expandit terram super aquas.
units.tr: CXXXVI. 6. Who stretched out the earth above the waters.

units.la: CXXXIX. 2. Tu cognovisti sessionem meam & resurrectionem meam. Hunc locum male in festo Paschatis cani. Non agi hic de resurrectione Christi. Explicantur Ebræa.
units.tr: CXXXIX. 2. Thou knowest my sitting down and my rising up. This passage is wrongly sung at the Feast of Easter. The passage is not about the resurrection of Christ. The Hebrew is explained.

units.la: C. Mirabilis facta est scientia tua ex me.
units.tr: C. Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me.

units.la: 17. Mihi autem nimis honorificati sunt amici tui, Deus nimis confortatus est principatus eorum. Examinatur ista versio. Ostenditur, multum discrepare ab Ebræo. Quæ causæ. An locus iste faciat ad probandum invocationem Sanctorum. Sanctos V. T. ex Bell. quoque sententia fuisse invocatos & quare. Explicatur locus Ps. 132. 1. Sanctos administrare hunc mundum, male ex hoc loco probari. Præfecturæ inter Divos distributæ. Proponuntur variæ expositiones interpretum.
units.tr: 17. But to me thy friends are made exceeding honourable, O God, their principality is exceedingly strengthened. This version is examined. It is shown to differ much from the Hebrew. The causes of this. Whether this passage supports the invocation of saints. That the saints of the Old Testament were also invoked, even by Bellarmine's own opinion, and why. Psalm 132.1 is explained. That the saints govern this world is wrongly proved from this passage. The prefectures distributed among the gods. Various expositions of the interpreters are set forth.

units.la: CXLVIII. Laudate eum aquæ quæ supra cælum.
units.tr: CXLVIII. Praise him, ye waters that are above the heavens.

units.la: CL. 1. Laudate Dominum in sanctis ejus. Versionem eam natam ex Græca. Posse commode exponi Interpretes hic prævaricari. De sanctis defunctis plane non agi. Ingenuæ confessiones quorundam Pontificiorum. Lovaniensis Editio Belgica.
units.tr: CL. 1. Praise God in his saints. That version arose from the Greek. It can conveniently be explained that the interpreters here go astray. It is plainly not about the saints departed. Candid confessions of certain Papists. The Louvain edition, the Belgic edition.

units.la: PROVERBIA.
units.tr: PROVERBS.

units.la: I. 20. Sapientia, de filio Dei.
units.tr: I. 20. Wisdom, concerning the Son of God.

units.la: VI. 31. Deprehensus reddet sputulum. An pœna furti tempore Salomonis exasperata sit. Thomæ infirma ex hoc loco argumentatione. Verus loci sensus & Salomonis scopus.
units.tr: VI. 31. The thief, when caught, will restore sevenfold. Whether the penalty for theft was made harsher in Solomon's time. Thomas's weak argument from this passage. The true sense of the passage and Solomon's aim.

units.la: VIII. 22. Dominus possedit me initio viâ suâ. Valde in hoc loco sudasse Patres, & nominatim Athanaf.
units.tr: VIII. 22. The Lord possessed me at the beginning of his way. The Fathers, and Athanasius by name, sweated greatly over this passage.

units.la: Universæ dissertationis, qua Cl. Drusius defenditur, summam videbis.
units.tr: You will see the sum of the whole dissertation, in which the illustrious Drusius is defended.

units.la: [Pag. 579. sub finem adde hæc formalia verba Thomæ, quæ extant in Summa parte 1. qu. 41. art 3. resp. ad quartum arg. Velper hoc, inquit, quod sapientia creata & genita nuncupatur, modus divinæ generationis nobis insinuatur. In generatione enim, quod generatur accipit naturam generantis, quod perfectionis est. In creatione vero creans non mutatur: sed creatum non recipit naturam creantis. Dicitur ergo filius simul creatus & genitus; ut ex creatione accipiatur immutabilitas patris: & ex generatione unitas naturæ in patre & filio. Et sic exponitur intellectus hujus scripturæ ab Hilario libro de Synodis.]
units.tr: [Page 579. At the end add these formal words of Thomas, which stand in the Summa, part 1, question 41, article 3, reply to the fourth objection: Moreover, by this, he says, that wisdom is called created and begotten, the mode of divine generation is suggested to us. For in generation, what is generated receives the nature of the one generating, which belongs to perfection. In creation, however, the creator is not changed, but the created thing does not receive the nature of the creator. Therefore the Son is called both created and begotten: so that from creation we take the immutability of the Father, and from generation the unity of nature in Father and Son. And so the meaning of this Scripture is explained, as Hilary does in his book On the Synods.]

units.la: XVI. 11. Et opera manuum ejus omnes lapides sacculi. Locus explicatur, olim lectum, seculi.
units.tr: XVI. 11. And all the stones of the bag are his work. The passage is explained; it was formerly read seculi (of the age).

units.la: 15. Sicut nubes pluviæ serotinæ. Quid differant malkosch & jorab. Pluvia in messe.
units.tr: 15. Like clouds of late rain. How malkosch and jorab differ. Rain at harvest.

units.la: XVIII. Qui tenet adulteram, stultus est & impius. Versum istum non extare in Ebr. Male ergo à Scholasticis allegari.
units.tr: XVIII. He who holds an adulteress is foolish and impious. This verse is not found in the Hebrew. It is therefore wrongly cited by the Schoolmen.

units.la: XX. 25. Ruina est homini devotare sanctos. Melior lectio, devorare. Examinatur versio. Labor interpretum in conciliatione cum textu Ebraeo.
units.tr: XX. 25. It is a snare for a man to devote the saints. The better reading is devour. The translation is examined. The labour of the translators in reconciling it with the Hebrew text.

units.la: XXII. 20. Ecce descripsi eam tibi tripliciter. Ex eo loco triplicem scripturæ sen-sum à nonnullis probari. Aliorum alienæ expositiones.
units.tr: XXII. 20. Behold, I have described it to you threefold. Some prove a threefold sense of Scripture from this passage. Other men's strained interpretations.

units.la: XXIV. Septies in die cadit justus. Illud in die, nec esse in Ebr nec Græco, nec Belg. nec Latina correcta. Cadere hinc non valere idem quod peccare. Vera loci sententia.
units.tr: XXIV. The righteous falls seven times a day. The words in die (in a day) are found neither in the Hebrew, nor the Greek, nor the Belgic version, nor the corrected Latin. From this, to fall does not mean the same as to sin. The true sense of the passage.

units.la: XXV. verf. penult. Scrutator majestatis opprimetur â gloria. Locum male versum pejus vulgo applicari. Versus Scaligeri adversus curiositatem in rebus divinis. Explicantur versus 16. & 17. Pretiosum pro raro. Alia.
units.tr: XXV., second last verse. The searcher of majesty will be overwhelmed by glory. A passage badly translated and applied even worse by the common people. Scaliger's verses against curiosity in divine matters. Verses 16 and 17 are explained. Precious for rare. Other matters.

units.la: XXVI. 19. Viam viri in adolescentia. Alienæ expositiones. In Ebræo aliter legi, de voce עלמה virgo παρθένος. Qualis fuerit virginum educatio apud veteres. An in templo virgines reclusæ habuerint. Locus 2. Mach. 3. Meretricem Chaldæis נפקרת ברא vocari, & quare. Testudo domiporta, hieroglyphicum honestæ matronæ.
units.tr: XXVI. 19. The way of a man in youth. Other men's interpretations. In the Hebrew it is read differently; on the word almah, virgin [παρθένος]. What the upbringing of virgins was like among the ancients. Whether virgins were kept shut up in the temple. The passage in 2 Maccabees 3. The Chaldeans call a harlot naphqarta bara [נפקרת ברא], and why. The tortoise carrying its house, a hieroglyph of the respectable matron.

units.la: XXXI. Noli regibus dare vinum. An Regibus vino interdictum sit.
units.tr: XXXI. Do not give wine to kings. Whether wine was forbidden to kings.

units.la: Ibid. Date siceram pereunti. Consuetudo Ebræorum, qua facinorosos morituros haustu vini reficiebant. Eam postea degenerasse. Cur Christo oblatum vinum myrrhatum. Myrrhæ vis in obumbranda mente & tolerandis tormentis. Quid sit Obed in textu Ebræo. Explicatur locus Deut. xxvi. 5.
units.tr: Ibid. Give strong drink to him who is perishing. The custom of the Hebrews by which those criminals about to die were revived with a draught of wine. That custom later degenerated. Why myrrhed wine was offered to Christ. The power of myrrh in dulling the mind and enduring torments. What Obed means in the Hebrew text. The passage Deut. 26. 5 is explained.

units.la: Calix consolationis, Jerem. 16. 7. Ibid.
units.tr: The cup of consolation, Jer. 16. 7. Ibid.

units.la: KOHELETH.
units.tr: KOHELETH.

units.la: I. 1. Vanitas vanitatum. Augustinum legisse vanitas vanitantium, Ejus expositio. Retractatio. 597. IV. 15. Cum juvene secundo, quis resurget pro eo? Ita legisse Ambrosium, & de Christo expositisse. Confertur cum textu Ebræo. B. virgo Maria, quoquomodo olla & aula dici possit.
units.tr: I. 1. Vanity of vanities. Augustine read "vanitas vanitantium" (vanity of vanity-makers); his exposition. Retractions, 597. IV. 15. "With the second youth, who will rise up in his place?" Ambrose read it thus and expounded it of Christ. Compared with the Hebrew text. How the blessed Virgin Mary can be called both a pot and a court.

units.la: Nescit homo, utrum amore vel odio dignus sit. Rev. viri, D. Ludovici de Diem expositio.
units.tr: Man does not know whether he is worthy of love or of hatred. The exposition of the reverend man, Lord Ludovicus de Diem.

units.la: Si ceciderit lignum &c.
units.tr: If the tree falls, etc.

units.la: CANTICUM.
units.tr: CANTICUM.

units.la: Ordinavit in me charitatem. Aliter esse in Ebraeo. Huic tamen loco prolixissimas disputationes superstructas esse. Examinatur locus Rom. 13. Quae autem sunt a Deo, ordinata sunt. Inde male probari subordinationem gladii temporalis, item, ceremonialia praecepta habere finem. Vera loci lectio & distinctio.
units.tr: Ordinavit in me charitatem. In the Hebrew it is otherwise. Yet very lengthy disputations have been built upon this passage. The passage Rom. 13 is examined: Quae autem sunt a Deo, ordinata sunt. From it they wrongly prove the subordination of the temporal sword, and likewise that the ceremonial precepts have come to an end. The true reading and punctuation of the passage.

units.la: SIRACH.
units.tr: Sirach

units.la: XVIII. 1. Qui vivit in aeternum, creavit omnia simul. An Deus uno die vel instanti omnia creaverit. Augustini sententia. Cognitio matutina & vespertina. Procopii sententia. Explicatur locus Gen. 2. 4. Dies pro tempore. Genuina loci interpretatio. | 600 XXIV. 3. Primogenita ante omnem creaturam. Non extare in Graeco. | 601 XLIV. Henoch translatus est in Paradisum ut det gentibus poenitentiam. Verba illa, in Paradisum non esse in Graeco. Quatuor quaestiones de Henoch. I. An mortuus sit. Neg. II. Quo translatus sit. Ubi & de Elia. An Henoch & Elias sint duo illi testes, de quibus Apocal. xi. 3. Sixti Senensis audacia. III. Ubi post diluvium sint Henoch & Elias. An Paradisus adhuc supersit. An quaestio ista sit de fide. Senensem inepte urgere illa verba, ut det gentibus poenitentiam. Graeca aliter sonare. De paradiso contrariae Pontificiorum sententiae. IV. Ubi post ascensionem Christi sint iidem. An Johannem Evangelistam collegam habeant. An ipse quoque tempore Anti-Christi venturus sit. Johan. xxi. Sic cum volo manere. Responsio Corn. a Lapide ad eum locum. | 602
units.tr: XVIII. 1. "He who lives for ever created all things together." Whether God created all things in one day or in an instant. The opinion of Augustine. Morning and evening knowledge. The opinion of Procopius. The passage Gen. 2. 4 is explained. "Day" means time. The genuine interpretation of the passage. | 600 XXIV. 3. "The firstborn before every creature." Not extant in the Greek. | 601 XLIV. Enoch was taken up into Paradise so that he might give repentance to the nations. The words "into Paradise" are not in the Greek. Four questions about Enoch. I. Whether he died. No. II. Where he was taken. Also concerning Elijah. Whether Enoch and Elijah are those two witnesses of whom Apoc. xi. 3 speaks. The audacity of Sixtus of Siena. III. Where Enoch and Elijah are after the flood. Whether Paradise still exists. Whether this question belongs to faith. That the Sienese presses the words "that he might give repentance to the nations" foolishly. The Greek sounds otherwise. On Paradise, the contrary opinions of the Papists. IV. Where the same two are after the ascension of Christ. Whether they have John the Evangelist as a colleague. Whether he too is to come at the time of Antichrist. John xxi. "So I want him to remain." The reply of Cornelius a Lapide to that passage. | 602

units.la: SYLLABUS LIB. IV. IESAIAS.
units.tr: SYLLABUS OF BOOK IV. ISAIAH.

units.la: I, 5 6. Omne caput languidum & omne cor maerens. A planta pedis, &c. Vulg. versionem Graecam sequutus est. לכ jam omne, jam totum significat.
units.tr: Isa. 1:5-6. The whole head is sick and the whole heart faint, from the sole of the foot, etc. The Vulgate followed the Greek version. לכ [kol] now means "every" and now "the whole."

units.la: Male ex hoc loco citatur peccatum originale.
units.tr: This passage is wrongly cited for original sin.

units.la: 24. Heu ego consolabor super hostibus meis & vindicabor de inimicis meis.
units.tr: 24. Ah, I will console myself over my enemies and be avenged on my foes.

units.la: 21. Vrbs ——— in justitia dormiebat. Ita habet Editio Basil. Ex Graeca LXX. κοιμᾶσθαι in Lingua Hellenistica aliquando significat manere, pernoctare.
units.tr: 21. The city ——— slept in righteousness. So reads the Basel edition. From the Greek of the Seventy: in Hellenistic usage, koimasthai sometimes means to remain, to spend the night.

units.la: II. 22. Quiescite ergo ab homine, cujus spiritus in naribus ejus est, quia excelsus reputatus est. Sic vulg. Aliter in textu Ebraeo. Variorum adducuntur ad hunc locum sententiae.
units.tr: II. 22. Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for he is reckoned high. So the Vulgate. The Hebrew text reads otherwise. Various opinions on this passage are cited.

units.la: III. 7. Non sum medicus. Valesius deceptus ex Vulg. versione.
units.tr: III. 7. I will not be a healer. Valesius was misled by the Vulgate version.

units.la: 12. PopulE mi, quite beatum dicunt, decipiunt te,
units.tr: 12. O my people, those who call you blessed deceive you.

units.la: V. 1. Cantabo dilecto meo Canticum patruelis mei vineae meae. Examinatur Vulg. & Lutheri versio, quid sit in cornu filio olei a multis non intellectum. Inepta Belg. Lovan. versio. Ex eorum versione Scriptura cum fructu a Laicis legi nequit. Terra Israel vocatur filius olei.
units.tr: V. 1. I will sing to my beloved a song of my kinsman concerning his vineyard. The Vulgate and Luther's version are examined, to see what in cornu filio olei means, which many have not understood. The Belgic Louvain version is absurd. From their version Scripture cannot be read with profit by laymen. The land of Israel is called "son of oil."

units.la: VII. 9. Si non credideritis non intelligetis. אם aliquando interrogationis particula.
units.tr: VII. 9. If you will not believe, you will not understand. אם [im] is sometimes an interrogative particle.

units.la: VIII. 19. 20. Vulg. Et cum dixerint ad vos, quaerite a Pythonibus, &c. Multorum allegorizandi pruritus damnatur, &c. אם לא יאמרו כרבר כעל אם. Hae verba variis expositionibus obnoxia. Piscat. praefertur. Quid sit De voce Python. D. Heinsii sententia. Magus ab Ebraeo מהגים deduci videtur, ut & Magister. Petr. Clunacens. inepte pro mortuis orandum esse probare nititur.
units.tr: VIII. 19-20. Vulgate: And when they say to you, Seek of the Pythons, etc. The itch of many to allegorize is condemned. Hebrew: אם לא יאמרו כדבר הזה [im lo yomeru kidvar ha-zeh], "if they do not speak according to this word." These words are open to various interpretations. Piscator is preferred. What a Python is. The opinion of D. Heinsius. The magus seems to be derived from the Hebrew מהגים [mehagim], as also the magister. Peter of Cluny clumsily tries to prove that one must pray for the dead.

units.la: IX. 6. Aeternum Dei filium indigitari Epitheto Angeli magni consilii desumptum est ex Graeca interpretatione hujus loci, nusquam in Ebraeo occurrit.
units.tr: IX. 6. The epithet "Angel of great counsel," used of the eternal Son of God, is taken from the Greek translation of this passage; it nowhere occurs in the Hebrew.

units.la: 7. למרבה Moses & Prophetae, ex Drusii, Scaligeri & aliorum sententia, charactero Samaritano usi fuerunt. Mem finale in hac voce a Prophetae manu esse non vidētur. Ineptiae Ebr. Elias hic plane ineptit. Christ. circa hanc vocem mysteria. Ab-Ezrae sententia de voce הם.
units.tr: 7. למרבה [lemarbeh]. Moses and the Prophets, according to the opinion of Drusius, Scaliger and others, used the Samaritan character. The final mem in this word does not seem to be in the prophet's hand. Hebrew absurdities. Elias plainly errs here. Christian mysteries about this word. Ab-Ezra's opinion on the word הם [hem].

units.la: 14. Et disperdet Dominus ab Israel caput & caudam incurvantem & depravantem una die. Non ita in Originario habetur.
units.tr: 14. And the Lord will cut off from Israel head and tail, the bending and the defiled, in one day. This is not so in the original.

units.la: X. 15. Nunquid gloriabitur securis contra eum, qui secat in ea? Aut exaltabitur, &c. Male hic locus in jure Canonico citatur ad primatum Rom. Ecclesia stabiliendum.
units.tr: X. 15. Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? Or shall the saw exalt itself, etc.? This passage is wrongly cited in canon law to establish the primacy of the Roman Church.

units.la: 22. Consummatio abbreviata inundabit justitiam. Obscura & hic Belg. Lovan. versio.
units.tr: 22. A consummation cut short shall overflow with righteousness. Obscure here too in the Belgic Louvain version.

units.la: XI. 2. 3. Hoc loco non septem, ut scholastici volunt, sed sex tantum S.S. dona recensentur. Ex quinque sensibus tres tantum, auditus, visus, & olfactus Deo in S.S. tribuuntur, maxime autem olfactus. A. Gell. hac de re elegans dissertatio.
units.tr: XI. 2-3. Here not seven, as the Schoolmen wish, but only six gifts of the Holy Spirit are listed. Of the five senses, only three are attributed to God in Scripture: hearing, sight and smell, and especially smell. A. Gell. has an elegant dissertation on this matter.

units.la: 10. Et erit sepulchrum ejus gloriosum.
units.tr: 10. And his sepulchre shall be glorious.

units.la: XIII. 1. Onus Babel. משא frequenter usurpatur de infaustis Prophetiis, non autem semper ut vult. Hieron.
units.tr: XIII. 1. The burden of Babylon. The word משא [massa] is often used of unhappy prophecies, but not always as he would have it. Jerome.

units.la: 3. Mandatum sanctificatis meis. Elegantissima Forerii ad hanc Vulg. versionem, verba. Vera significatio קרשה & קדושה.
units.tr: 3. My sanctified ones I have commanded. The most elegant remarks of Forerius on this Vulgate version. The true meaning of קרשה [qedasha] and קדושה [qedushah].

units.la: XIV. 12. Quomodo cecidisti de caelo Lucifer, fili aurora. Male ex hoc loco probat Thomas, quod Diabolus appetierit esse ut Deus.
units.tr: XIV. 12. How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the dawn! Thomas wrongly proves from this passage that the devil desired to be like God.

units.la: 26. Hoc consilium, quod cogitavi super omnem terram.
units.tr: 26. This is the counsel that I have purposed against all the earth.

units.la: XVI. 1. Emitte agnum Domine, Dominatorem terra. Hic locus plane alieno sensu de Christo exponitur. Lutheri interpretatio rejicitur. | 666.
units.tr: XVI. 1. Send forth the lamb, O Lord, the ruler of the land. This passage is explained of Christ in a quite alien sense. Luther's interpretation is rejected. | 666.

units.la: XXII. 14. Non remittetur vobis haec iniquitas donec moriamini. In hoc loco fundatur unica judaeorum consolatio. Precatio judaei ex morbo decumbentis. | 668.
units.tr: XXII. 14. Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till you die. The only consolation of the Jews rests on this passage. A Jew's prayer of one lying sick. | 668.

units.la: 17. Ecce Dominus asportari te faciet, sicut asportatur gallus gallinaceus. | 670.
units.tr: 17. Behold, the Lord will have you carried off, as a cock is carried off. | 670.

units.la: XXVIII. 16. Ecce ego mitto in fundamentis Sion lapidem, Lapidem probatum, &c. Pinti error. Kimchi inepta interpretatio de Ecclesia. | 672.
units.tr: XXVIII. 16. Behold, I lay in the foundations of Zion a stone, a tried stone, etc. Pinto's error. Kimchi's absurd interpretation concerning the Church. | 672.

units.la: 19. Tantummodo sola vexatio intellectum dabit auditui. | 673.
units.tr: 19. Only vexation will give understanding to the hearing. | 673.

units.la: XXX. 15. Cum conversus ingemueris tunc salvaberis &c. Non ita in Ebraeo. Melius vulg. | 676.
units.tr: XXX. 15. When you return and groan, then you shall be saved, etc. This is not so in the Hebrew. The Vulgate is better. | 676.

units.la: 26. Eritque lux lunae sicut lux solis &c. Obscuritas lunae & solis calamitates, lux L. & S. multiplicata, laetitiam significat. | 677.
units.tr: 26. The light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, etc. The darkness of the moon and the calamities of the sun; the multiplied light of moon and sun signifies joy. | 677.

units.la: 27. Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo. Nomen aliquando pro fama & gloria accipitur apud Ebraeos. Futurum apud Ebraeos saepe notat actum solitum. Thophet idem cum valle Hinnom. sequiori aevo pro damnatorum loco usurpatum. | 678.
units.tr: 27. Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar. Among the Hebrews "name" is sometimes taken for fame and glory. The future tense among the Hebrews often denotes a customary action. Tophet is the same as the valley of Hinnom; in a later age it was used as the place of the damned. | 678.

units.la: XXXIII. 13. Qui excutit manus suas ab omni malo manere. | 682.
units.tr: XXXIII. 13. He who shakes his hands free from every evil. | 682.

units.la: XXXVII. 35. Propter David servum meum. Christus servus Dei vocatur. Falso defunctorum merita ex hoc loco a pontificiis probantur. | 683.
units.tr: XXXVII. 35. For David my servant's sake. Christ is called the servant of God. The Papists falsely prove the merits of the dead from this passage. | 683.

units.la: XL. 1. Completa est malitia ejus, dimissa est iniquitas ejus: suscepit &c. Examinatur haec versio. Militia a librariis corrupta est in malitia. | 683.
units.tr: XL. 1. Her warfare is accomplished, her iniquity is pardoned; she has received, etc. This version is examined. "Militia" [warfare] has been corrupted by copyists into "malitia" [malice]. | 683.

units.la: XLII. 1. ruach esse communis gen. tam de Spiritu quam de vento. Iacob & Israel quae sunt in verf. Lxx. abesse a textu Ebr. Anima Dei vel hominis sumi pro ipso Deo vel homine. | 685.
units.tr: XLII. 1. ruach [רוח] is of common gender, both of Spirit and of wind. The words Iacob & Israel, which are in the verse of the Seventy, are absent from the Hebrew text. The soul of God or of man is taken for God himself or man himself. | 685.

units.la: XLIII. 20. Textus Graecus Lxx. aliter sonat quam in Ebraeo est.
units.tr: XLIII. 20. The Greek text of the LXX reads differently from the Hebrew.

units.la: XLV. 1. Haec dicit Dominus Christo meo Cyro &c. Hic locus nequaquam intelligendus de Christo. Ineptum de quavis comparatione velle typum instituere. | 688.
units.tr: XLV. 1. Thus says the Lord to my anointed Cyrus, etc. This passage is by no means to be understood of Christ. It is absurd to wish to establish a type from any comparison whatever. | 688.

units.la: 8. Rorate caeli desuper & nubes pluant justum: aperiatur terra & germinet Salvatorem &c. Neque haec ad Christum, ut antitypum accommodari possunt. Tres modi sunt, quibus probatur aliquem scripturae locum ad Christum pertinere. Nugae Pinti & aliorum de Maria. | 689.
units.tr: 8. Drop down, you heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain down the righteous; let the earth open and bring forth a Saviour, etc. Nor can these words be applied to Christ as the antitype. There are three ways by which it is proved that a passage of Scripture pertains to Christ. The trifles of Pinto and others about Mary. | 689.

units.la: 14. 15. Tantum in te est Deus & non est absque te Deus. Vere tu es Deus &c. Bellerm. ficulneum hinc argumentum de Christi Deitate. Suaviludium Pinti de hostia consecrata. | 692.
units.tr: 14-15. Surely God is in you, and there is no other; there is no God besides you. Truly you are a God, etc. Bellarmine's flimsy argument from this passage about the deity of Christ. Pinto's playful trifle about the consecrated host. | 692.

units.la: XLVI. 3. Audite me domus Iacob ── qui portamini a meo utero, quigestamini a mea vulva. Lutherus hic deceptus a vulg. | 548.695.
units.tr: XLVI. 3. Hear me, house of Jacob, who are carried from my womb, who are borne from my belly. Luther is deceived here by the Vulgate. | 548.695.

units.la: LI. 20. Filii tui ── sicut beta semicocta. | 19.697.
units.tr: LI. 20. Your sons ... like a half-boiled beet. | 19.697.

units.la: LIII. 4. Percussum a Deo. | 697.
units.tr: LIII. 4. Smitten by God. | 697.

units.la: LXI. 2. Ut praedicarem annum placabilem Domino. Scaliger de ministerio Christi. Annus sumitur pro tempore & contra. Cajephas quandiu sacerdotio functus. | 698.
units.tr: LXI. 2. To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord. Scaliger on the ministry of Christ. "Year" is taken for time, and conversely. How long Caiaphas served in the priesthood. | 698.

units.la: LXIII. 1. Quis est ille, qui venit de Edom. &c. Variae de hoc vaticinio controversiae. De Christo hic locus intelligendus. | 699.
units.tr: LXIII. 1. Who is this that comes from Edom, etc.? Various controversies about this prophecy. This passage is to be understood of Christ. | 699.

units.la: 2. Cur rubrum est indumentum tuum, & vers. 3. Aspersus sanguis eorum super vestimenta mea. Sa per sanguinem peccata intelligi vult | 701.
units.tr: 2. Why is your apparel red, and your garments like his that treads in the winepress? and v. 3: Their blood is sprinkled upon my garments. He wishes "blood" to be understood as sins. | 701.

units.la: 3. Torcular calcavi solus. Hier. torcular pro peccatorum Suppliciis ponit. Calcare torcular non significare peccatorum supplicia experiri, sed a-lios |
units.tr: 3. I have trodden the winepress alone. Jerome takes the winepress to stand for the punishments of sins. To tread the winepress does not mean to undergo the punishments of sins, but to punish

units.la: lios punire. Male pro concione de passione Christi ex hoc loco allegarit Ick hebbe de Wijn-perse alleen gheareden. Ibidem. De gentibus non est vir mecum. Pinti ineptiae ad haec verba de Maria virgine. 703.
units.tr: others. Wrongly, in a sermon on the passion of Christ, someone cited this passage: "I have trodden the winepress alone" (Dutch: Ick hebbe de Wijn-perse alleen gheareden). Also on the words "Of the peoples there was no man with me," Pinto's absurdities about the Virgin Mary. | 703.

units.la: 5. Et excandescentia fulci vit me. 794.
units.tr: 5. And my fury upheld me. | 794.

units.la: LXIV. 1. Vtinam dirumperes caelos &c. Querela quod fontes raro inspiciantur, & quid damni inde eveniat. 705.
units.tr: LXIV. 1. Oh that you would rend the heavens, etc. A complaint that the springs are seldom consulted, and what harm comes of this. | 705.

units.la: 6. Tanquam pannus menstruata omnes justitiae nostrae. Ex hoc loco non pro-
units.tr: From this passage original sin cannot be pro-

units.la: bari peccatum originale. Optima regenitorum opera non esse peccata &c. Lutherus in sua versione sibi nimis indulget. Variae expositiones vocis ⊐ꟷ. 705.
units.tr: ved. The best works of the regenerate are not sins, etc. Luther indulges himself too much in his version. Various explanations of the word בגד [beged]. | 705.

units.la: LXVI. 7. Antequam parturiret, peperit: antequam veniret partus ejus, peperit
units.tr: LXVI. 7. Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she brought forth a man child.

units.la: masculum. Haec de spirituali Ecclesiae partu intelligenda Pintus & alii. 709.
units.tr: These words are to be understood of the spiritual birth of the Church, say Pinto and others. | 709.

units.la: IEREMIAS
units.tr: JEREMIAH

units.la: II. 18. Et nunc quid tibi vis in via Aegypti, ut bibas aquas Schichor. Num per Schichor Nilus designatur. 710.
units.tr: II. 18. And now what do you want in the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of Shihor? Whether by Shihor the Nile is meant. 710.

units.la: VI. 8. Ne fort recedat anima mea a te. 712.
units.tr: VI. 8. Lest perhaps my soul depart from you. 712.

units.la: VII. 4. Templum Domini, &c. 712.
units.tr: VII. 4. The temple of the Lord, etc. 712.

units.la: 18. Ut faciant placentas Reginae caeli. Quid per Reginam caeli intelligatur, variae sententiae. 712.
units.tr: 18. To make cakes for the Queen of heaven. What is meant by the Queen of heaven: various opinions. 712.

units.la: XI. 19. Mittamus lignum in panem ejus. Examinantur variae expositiones,
units.tr: XI. 19. Let us put wood into his bread. The various expositions are examined,

units.la: vera datur. 713.
units.tr: and the true one is given. 713.

units.la: XII. 3. Sanctifica eos in die occisionis. Lyrae sententia praefertur. Hellenisticae linguae proprium, voces graecas ad significationum Ebraearum amplitu-
units.tr: XII. 3. Sanctify them for the day of slaughter. Lyra's opinion is preferred. It is a peculiarity of the Hellenistic language to stretch Greek words beyond the range of the Hebrew meanings

units.la: dem dilatare & contra & interpretari. Pro interpretamento ponere. 715.
units.tr: and, conversely, to interpret, and to put forward as an interpretation. 715.

units.la: 13. καλέσει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀφελήσεων αὐτοῖς. Rom. lat. cleri illorum non prodeunt illis. Non ita in Ebraeo. 716.
units.tr: 13. [καλέσει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀφελήσεων αὐτοῖς]. The Latin reads: their clergy will not profit them. It is not so in the Hebrew. 716.

units.la: XVI. 16. Ecce ego mittam piscatores multos dicit Dominus, piscabuntur eos &
units.tr: XVI. 16. Behold, I will send many fishers, says the Lord, and they shall fish them,

units.la: post haec mittam, &c. A Postillatoribus multis imperite hic locus citari solet.
units.tr: and after these things I will send, etc. Many Postillators commonly cite this passage here carelessly.

units.la: Verbis illis non promissio sed comminatio continetur. 716.
units.tr: Those words contain not a promise but a threat. 716.

units.la: XVII. 9. Profundum est cor super omnia, & bonum est, quis cognoscet eum; variae
units.tr: XVII. 9. The heart is deep above all things, and it is good; who shall know it? Various expositions are offered.

units.la: 11. Perdix fovit quae non peperit: fecit divitias suas & non in iudicio, in dimidio dierum, &c. Gemina Ellipsis hic notanda venit. Kimchi sententia de perdice. Junii & Tremellii interpretatio praeferenda. 718.
units.tr: 11. The partridge has hatched what it did not bring forth; he has made riches, but not in judgment; in the middle of his days, etc. A double ellipsis is to be noted here. Kimchi's opinion about the partridge. The interpretation of Junius and Tremellius is to be preferred. 718.

units.la: XXII. 11. Haec dicit Dominus ad Sellum filium Iosiae. 721.
units.tr: XXII. 11. Thus says the Lord to Shallum the son of Josiah. 721.

units.la: XXIII. 5. Suscitabo David germen justum. Romanae edit. versio lat. dissentit ab Ebraeo. Ἀνατολή inter alias significationes significat germen. 721.
units.tr: XXIII. 5. I will raise up to David a righteous branch. The Latin version of the Roman edition differs from the Hebrew. Among other meanings, ἀνατολή [anatolē] means branch. 721.

units.la: 6. Et hoc est nomen, quo vocabunt eum. Dominus justus noster. Ita
units.tr: 6. And this is the name by which they will call him: The Lord our righteousness. The common readings sound otherwise in the Hebrew,

units.tr: 23. Am I a God at hand, says the Lord, and not a God from afar?
